title: Associate Director, Data Engineering
description:
At MCG, we lead the healthcare community to deliver patient-focused care. We have a mission-driven team of talented physicians and technical experts developing our evidence-based content and innovating our products to accelerate improvements in healthcare. If you are driven to enhance the US healthcare system, MCG is eager to have you join our team. We cultivate a work environment that nurtures personal and professional growth, and this is a thrilling time to become a part of our organization. With dynamic roles that offer meaningful impact, you'll be able to fully realize your potential. Plus, you'll enjoy world-class benefits and the security, stability, and resources of our parent company, Hearst, with over 100 years of experience.

MCG develops evidence-based guidelines that help patients get the right care across healthcare settings. Our Data Science team combines AI with the expertise of our clinical editors and guidelines to improve the efficiency and accuracy of documentation workflows. We bring deep experience applying natural language processing to clinical data and are expanding what reliable, explainable agentic workflows can do.

As Associate Director, Data Engineering, you will shape the data foundation behind MCG’s AI products. You will partner with Product Managers, Software Engineers, and Data Scientists to build and operate the platform that moves data from ingestion to trusted datasets and actionable insights. Your work will help scientists improve our products, inform our AI roadmap, and give teams clearer ways to make data-informed decisions. This role spans platform engineering, data operations, analytics, and emerging agentic workflows, with room to shape how this capability grows.

You Will

  • Partner with Product Managers and customers to understand needs, translate them into requirements, and design end-to-end data and insights solutions for AI features.
  • Grow and maintain the data platform that supports MCG’s AI work, connecting data ingestion, transformation, governance, and delivery into dependable workflows.
  • Develop and maintain high-quality, well-governed datasets that Data Scientists can use to build, evaluate, and continuously improve AI products.
  • Use MCG’s data to identify patterns, opportunities, and customer-relevant insights that can inform product decisions and the AI roadmap.
  • Create and maintain clear, dynamic dashboards that help partners across the business understand performance and make data-informed decisions.
  • Apply strong data operations and software engineering practices to improve the quality, reliability, repeatability, and usability of data pipelines and platform capabilities.
  • Collaborate across Product, Engineering, and Data Science to clarify tradeoffs, surface data risks early, and deliver solutions that meet technical and business needs.

Our Tech Stack

  • Python, C#, C++
  • Databricks
  • Flyte, Tableau, Power BI
  • Azure, AWS

What We’re Looking For

  • At least 10+ years of experience in data engineering, data science, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience building, maintaining, or growing data platforms that support AI or machine learning products.
  • Strong data operations and software engineering skills, including experience designing reliable data workflows and production-ready pipelines.
  • A clear understanding of the machine learning lifecycle and how dependable data supports model development and ongoing product improvement.
  • Experience working with governed data lakes and applying sound practices for data quality, organization, and access.
  • Ability to turn product, customer, and scientific needs into practical technical data solutions.
  • Excellent written communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to explain data concepts and recommendations to varied audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with deep learning, natural language processing, or other applied AI methods.
  • Experience working with healthcare or clinical data.

Pay Range: $192,00 - $269,000

Other compensation: Bonus Eligible

Location: Seattle Preferred

✈️ Travel expected 1–3 times per year for company-sponsored events

📈 401K retirement plan; flexible spending and health savings account

🏝️ 15 days of paid time off + additional front-loaded personal days

🏖️ 14 company-recognized holidays + paid volunteer days

👶 up to 8 weeks of paid parental leave + 10 weeks of paid bonding leave

🌈 LGBTQ+ Health Services

🐶 Pet insurance

title: Laboratory Technician I
description:
JOB TITLE: Laboratory Technician I

POSITION NUMBER: 2610-20450-LabTec-01

POSITION LOCATION: Atlanta, GA, USA

ANTICIPATED START DATE: 2-4 weeks after candidate identification

TRAVEL: As required to fulfill the responsibilities of the position


ASRT, Inc. provides scientific, information management, management consulting, bioinformatics, and administrative program support to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and other Federal and private sector clients. The successful candidate will be a full-time employee of ASRT, Inc. and will be assigned to the Division of Core Laboratory Services and Response (DCLSR), National Center for Emerging and Zoonotic and Infectious Diseases (NCEZID), at the CDC, 1600 Clifton Road, Atlanta, GA.


SCOPE OF WORK

The Laboratory Technician I will provide support for non-research biological science work to the Specimen Triage and Tracking Laboratory. The duties and responsibilities of the position include, but are not limited to the following:


MAJOR DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Performs non-research biological science work or biological science support work in various scientific and public health areas associated with numerous biological agents.
  • Responsible for formulating media orders to support DSR activities.
  • Process and formulate reagent and media orders, including plates, buffers dyes, broths etc.
  • Responsible for ordering glassware, chemicals, and other equipment and supplies required to formulate and process media order.
  • Create and maintain documentation and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP).
  • Perform routine maintenance of equipment to include cleaning of equipment, laboratory and disposing of biohazard waste.
  • Responsible for order chemicals to keep lab stocked of ingredients.
  • Work collaboratively with team members ensuring effect process flow.
  • Document temperature ranges for freezers, refrigerators, balances and various hoods used, cleaning out of desiccators, water baths etc.

title: Senior PHP Software Engineer (Remote)
description:
Onze klant is een vooraanstaande speler in de internationale technologiesector, gespecialiseerd in geavanceerde softwarebeveiliging en digitale bescherming. In een landschap waarin digitale transformatie razendsnel gaat en moderne softwareontwikkeling steeds complexer wordt, biedt dit bedrijf innovatieve oplossingen die organisaties wereldwijd grip geven op de kwaliteit en veiligheid van hun applicaties. Met een ijzersterke staat van dienst en een wereldwijde aanwezigheid vertrouwen talloze toonaangevende ondernemingen op hun expertise. Het werk van dit bedrijf vormt een essentiële pijler onder de betrouwbaarheid van de digitale toepassingen die we dagelijks gebruiken. Als Senior Software Developer speel je een sleutelrol in het bouwen en verfijnen van dit toonaangevende platform. Je versterkt een hecht, internationaal team van gedreven vakgenoten waar transparantie, wederzijds respect en een open feedbackcultuur de norm zijn. Neem het voortouw bij het ontwerp en de realisatie van krachtige backend-services met talen zoals Go, Java of Node.js. Waarborg de schaalbaarheid en prestaties van het platform door potentiële knelpunten in de architectuur proactief op te lossen. Begeleid junior collega's via gerichte code reviews en kennisdeling om zo het niveau van het gehele team naar een hoger niveau te tillen. Lever een actieve bijdrage aan architectonische keuzes die de langetermijnkwaliteit en onderhoudbaarheid van de software garanderen.

In de rol van Senior Software Developer combineer je een grondige kennis van softwarekwaliteit met de zelfstandigheid om uitdagende projecten van begin tot eind op te leveren. Ruime ervaring met full-stack ontwikkeling binnen een moderne omgeving, waarbij je vlot navigeert tussen frontend en backend. Uitstekende beheersing van TypeScript en React, aangevuld met grondige ervaring in ten minste één backendtaal zoals Go, Java of Node.js. Affiniteit met geautomatiseerd testen, CI/CD-pipelines en cloud-infrastructuur zoals Kubernetes of Infrastructure as Code is een mooie plus. Een uitgebreid pakket aan extralegale voordelen, waaronder maaltijdcheques en een representatief budget voor dagelijkse onkosten. Een representatieve bedrijfswagen met laadpas of een flexibel mobiliteitsbudget, afgestemd op jouw persoonlijke voorkeur. Maximale wendbaarheid dankzij een hybride werkregeling waarin je de vrijheid krijgt om kantoor- en thuiswerk optimaal te combineren. Een ruim aantal jaarlijkse vakantiedagen om geregeld de batterij weer helemaal op te laden. Talloze mogelijkheden om je verder te ontwikkelen via trainingen, workshops en het bijwonen van vakgerichte conferenties. Solliciteer zeker en we contacteren je ASAP.

title: Communications Consultant 4 (CC4/COM) - Project
description:
Description

Communications Consultant 4 – Project


This project position is funded through October 30th, 2030.


This recruitment is open to Washington State residents only.


The Opportunity

This Communications Consultant 4 (CC4) functions as a senior-level communications consultant responsible for developing, implementing, and coordinating strategic communications that support SPI’s policy and health system transformation work. The position exercises a high degree of professional judgment and independence in planning, producing, and advising on communications for complex, high-visibility initiatives with statewide impact.


Key Responsibilities Include:

  • Develop and implement comprehensive communications strategies that identify audiences, messaging, channels, risks, timelines, and success measures.
  • Plan and produce high-quality communication products – including fact sheets, web content, presentations, talking points, press materials, and stakeholder updates – that meet federal grant requirements and support program goals.
  • Translate complex policy and delivery-system concepts into clear, accessible materials tailored for rural providers, partners, and community audiences.
  • Ensure all communications align with federal requirements, including CMS guidance, branding standards, accessibility expectations, and required disclaimers.
  • Develop and implement communications plans aligned with legislative, policy, and operational priorities.
  • Advise leadership and program staff and leadership on audiences, key messages, channels, timing, and purpose (5 Ws).
  • Build and maintain relationships with HCA leadership, grant providers, contractors, COM team members, and other HCA staff.
  • Serve as backup to the Policy Communications team, including Office of Tribal Affairs, Medicaid Transformation Project, and Legislative Affairs communications.

Why You’ll Love This Role:

As a Senior Communications Consultant, you will act as a trusted advisor to SPI leadership, enjoying a high degree of autonomy to shape the narrative of critical, federally funded Rural Health Transformation efforts and complex health system policies. This role offers the perfect blend of high-visibility leadership and creative storytelling, allowing you to translate complex policy into clear, accessible campaigns that champion equitable healthcare for rural communities, tribal partners, and the legislature.

What You Bring:

If you are an expert communicator looking to lead digital content strategy across different platforms, mitigate high-stakes public risk, and collaborate with executive-level teams, this position offers the platform, purpose, and professional independence to take your career to the next level.


Required Qualifications

Experience may have been gained through paid or unpaid activities. Please ensure any relevant experience defined below is outlined in your cover letter, resume, and application.

  • Demonstrated understanding and skills in federal funded health transformation initiatives such as Medicaid waiver programs or Rural Health Transformation efforts, or other federally funded programs with significant public or political visibility, including demonstrated ability to apply communications guidance, brand standards, and compliance requirements.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop innovative and effective communication strategies.
  • Excellent writing and editing skills, including the ability to digest and translate complex information into clear, plain-language communications.
  • Demonstrated ability to organize and prioritize workload and to complete work on time and in a fast-moving environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to apply a health equity lens when reviewing and developing communications.
  • Strong collaborative skills, including the ability to communicate editorial changes in a courteous and professional manager.


Preferred Qualifications

While these are not required, having them may help you stand out as an applicant.

  • Seven (7) years professional experience in English, journalism, communications, humanities, public relations, or related field that includes writing and editing.
  • Bachelor’s degree in English, journalism, communications, humanities, public relations, or related field and three (3) years of writing/editing experience; or equivalent education/experience.
  • Experience using enterprise communication tools, including web content management systems (e.g. Drupal), email marketing platforms, and digital content strategies.
  • Experience developing digital content for diverse audiences, such as rural communities, policymakers, and health system partners.
  • Experience working with or for local, state, or federal government or in multi-agency environments, including coordination with executive leadership or high-profile environments.

About the Communications Division (COM)

The Communications Division (COM) provides external and internal communications support for HCA. Reporting to the Policy Communications Manager, the position provides strategic communications support to the Strategy, Policy, and Innovation division (SPI), with the role dedicated to federally funded Rural Health Transformation initiatives. SPI leads HCA’s health transformation work, focusing on value-based, whole-person care and coordinating the agency’s legislative activities to advance statewide health priorities.

Better Health. Better Care. A Healthier Washington

At HCA, we work to ensure people across Washington have access to high-quality health care. As the state’s largest health care purchaser, we serve nearly 3 million Washington residents through Apple Health (Medicaid), public and school employee benefits, and behavioral health programs. Together we’re building a stronger Washington.

We want our employees to have the support, flexibility, and benefits they need to do their best work and build a career that works for their life. Our benefits are designed to support you today while helping you plan for the future. Learn more about why HCA by visiting the Voices of HCA and the "Who we are" section of our website.

Our standard business hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., with alternative work schedules considered based on business needs. In this role you’ll regularly collaborate with colleagues, Agency leaders, state and federal partners, and other external partners or customers. Occasional travel may be required for meetings, training, or other business needs. All employees are required to report to our Olympia office on their first and final day of employment.

Our commitment to inclusion is reflected in how we work together and serve the people of Washington. HCA also supports five voluntary employee led Employee Resources Groups (ERGs), which create opportunities for connection, community, learning, and professional growth.

title: Principal Product Designer, Robot Animation and Character, Fauna
description:
Fauna Robotics is building capable, safe, and delightful robots for everyday life. We are hiring a Principal Product Designer to animate our robots and build a consistent character. This is the person who decides what our robot feels like as a sidekick in someone's home — and the person who animates it to get there.

You are an animator first, at the top of your craft. You will define the robot's personality and its expressive motion vocabulary — how it greets someone, shows curiosity, hesitates, celebrates, or settles into calm — and you will craft the performances that establish it, from first concept through what ships.

This is a hands-on animation and design role. You spend your days animating: blocking performances, refining timing, and dialing in the character. You'll work alongside Design Technologists, HRI researchers, and roboticists who own the tools, pipeline, and hardware — you bring the performance and the personality; they help you land it on a real robot. Our process is iterative and demo-led: block it out, put it on hardware, watch how it reads in the room, and let each pass sharpen the next.

Key job responsibilities
- Craft the robot's key performances — from concept and blocking through final motion — setting the character and the quality bar in the animation itself

- Build the expressive motion vocabulary: locomotion styles, conversational gesture, emotional reactions, idle behavior, and the small moments that make a character feel alive

- Define the robot's personality — its point of view, emotional range, and behavioral signature — and keep it consistent across every animation as the product evolves

- Iterate on real hardware: test how a performance reads in person, from every angle, and refine timing and weight until it lands

- Work with motion capture and reference where it helps, then adapt and refine performances for the robot's form factor and joint constraints

- Capture character intent in animation-ready artifacts — performance references, motion studies, behavioral scripts, and concept videos — so the rest of the team can build on it

About the team
Fauna Robotics, an Amazon company, is building capable, safe, and genuinely delightful robots for everyday life. Our goal is simple: make robots people actually want to live and interact with in everyday human spaces.
We believe that future won’t arrive until building for robotics becomes far more accessible. Today, too much effort is spent reinventing the fundamentals. We’re changing that by developing tightly integrated hardware and software systems that make it faster, safer, and more intuitive to create real-world robotic products.
Our work spans the full stack: mechanical design, control systems, dynamic modeling, and intelligent software. The focus is not just functionality, but experience. We’re building robots that feel responsive, expressive, and genuinely useful.
At Fauna, you’ll work at the frontier of this space, helping define how robots move, manipulate, and interact with people in natural environments. It’s an opportunity to solve hard problems across hardware and software with a team focused on making robotics accessible and joyful to build.
If you care about making robotics real for everyone and building systems that are as delightful as they are capable, we’re interested in hearing from you.

title: Health Coordinator - FT/DAY
description:
If you are looking for employment with a purpose where you can help improve the daily lives of the members of your community, then consider a career with Pioneer Human Services!

We are currently looking for a Health Coordinator (FT/DAY) with a passion for human services. This is an exciting opportunity to be involved with an organization focused on racial justice, second opportunities, diversity, equity and inclusion.

WHO WE ARE
We empower justice-involved individuals to overcome adversity and reach their full potential.

For over 60 years, we have proudly serviced our clients with professionalism and empathy. We are a nationally recognized non-profit with 35+ locations across Washington state that provided a chance for change to over 9,500 individuals in 2024.

WHAT WE OFFER

At Pioneer, our employees are important. That’s why we offer a Total Rewards package that includes compensation and benefits to support employees' health, security, and balance.

Compensation:

New hires start between $20.77 and $23.36 based on experience, qualifications, skills, competencies, internal equity, and market factors. While the full pay range is listed for this position for pay transparency, individual compensation is determined by various factors and may vary within the posted range.

Benefits That Invest in You

At Pioneer, we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and continued growth.

Health & Wellness Benefits

  • Medical coverage
  • Dental coverage
  • Vision coverage
  • Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
  • Dependent Care Flexible Spending Account

Financial Protection

  • Employer-provided life insurance

  • Disability coverage

Invest in Your Future

  • Front-Loaded Tuition Assistance
  • Retirement Plan
  • Employee recognition programs

Join Pioneer and build more than a career. Be part of a team that supports your well-being, recognizes your contributions, and invests in your future.

Benefit eligibility, coverage, contributions, and program provisions are subject to the terms of the applicable benefit plans and policies.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

The Health Coordinator supports Pioneer Human Services’ mission by coordinating and monitoring client physical and behavioral health services within residential treatment facilities. This role assists in ensuring continuity of care by facilitating communication between clients, nursing staff (where present), medical and behavioral health providers, pharmacy services, and program staff.

The Health Coordinator supports the intake process, coordinates internal and external medical and behavioral health appointments (including telehealth), assists with medication monitoring and documentation accuracy in the electronic medication administration record (eMAR/MAR), and gathers and communicates relevant health information to appropriate clinical staff. At sites with licensed nurses, the Health Coordinator works under the direction of nursing staff to support care coordination and implementation of provider orders. At sites without nurses, the Health Coordinator works under the direction of Health & Resource Coordination (HRCU) Manager.

In addition to care coordination, the Health Coordinator provides direct client support within a structured residential environment, including; engaging clients in the milieu, observing and monitoring client changes in physical and in behavioral health status, reinforcing treatment plans and health education, assisting with access to healthcare services, and responding to urgent health concerns by notifying appropriate clinical staff or emergency services as needed.

This role requires strong organization, attention to detail, and the ability to effectively support clients with complex medical, behavioral health, and substance use needs in a structured residential environment.

PRIMARY/ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Client Service:

  • Utilize program-approved screening tools and established procedures to identify and document client risks, needs, and barriers while supporting client and facility safety.
  • Utilize Motivational Interviewing (MI) and other engagement strategies to support client participation and skill development.
  • Interpret and explain program policies and goals to clients during orientation and throughout treatment as needed.
  • Support client education by conducting health education activities and reinforcing self-care skills appropriate to the client’s stage of recovery.
  • Where applicable by site or unit, observe and document client self-administration of medications in accordance with program policies and procedures.
  • Where medication responsibilities are assigned to nursing staff, promptly communicate medication-related concerns, discrepancies, or client requests to the licensed nurse.
  • When applicable to the role at a specific site, review MAR documentation for completeness at shift change and escalate discrepancies according to policy.
  • Maintain a safe and healthy environment which includes maintaining, cleaning, and disposing of equipment and supplies according to policy and procedures (e.g., cleaning medication rooms, disinfecting vital signs equipment, maintaining health services spaces).
  • Where applicable, assist with medication storage, ordering, and returns in accordance with pharmacy services policies and site procedures.
  • Assist clients in meeting health and safety needs in accordance with each individual’s stage of recovery and program policies.
  • Provide basic first aid and serve as the first point of contact for emergency response when needed, notifying licensed nursing staff, providers, or emergency services as appropriate.

title: Principal System Integration and Test Engineer
description:
At Atom Computing, we build quantum computers using arrays of optically trapped neutral atoms. Our systems will give customers access to computational breakthroughs that were out of reach until now. Join a world-class team of scientists, engineers, and business professionals advancing the state of the art in quantum computing.

We are seeking a Principal System Integration & Test Engineer with deep atomic, molecular, and optical (AMO) physics and quantum-computing knowledge. You will be the technical authority for whole-system integration: taking complete neutral-atom quantum computers from assembled subsystems to atom-ready machines, then handing each one to our Quantum Engineers (QEs) for testing with atoms. This is a hands-on technical leadership role reporting directly to the VP of Manufacturing.

Responsibilities

  • Own whole-system integration across optics, laser delivery, vacuum interfaces, radio-frequency (RF) controls, timing, and instrument software for neutral-atom quantum computers.
  • Apply AMO knowledge to define hardware-readiness checks. Agree integration, alignment, and handoff criteria with QEs and Systems Engineering.
  • Work alongside QEs on first-of-a-kind systems to establish repeatable integration sequences, alignment methods, diagnostics, and recovery procedures.
  • Perform and guide system-level optical alignment, laser-delivery checks, controls checkout, and applicable safety checks before atom-based verification begins.
  • Mentor and train integration engineers and technicians. Define the qualification path for new team members, and advise leadership on staffing and on scheduling shared instruments across concurrent builds.
  • Lead cross-subsystem troubleshooting. Work with laser, controls, subsystem, and QE specialists to resolve hardware and interface problems.
  • Support hardware corrections during QE testing. Partner with Manufacturing Engineering to reduce alignment rework and shorten repeat-build cycle time.

Experience & Education

  • PhD in physics, applied physics, optical engineering, electrical engineering, or a closely related discipline, or comparable professional experience.
  • 10+ years of experience in experimental AMO physics, quantum hardware, or precision laser-system integration.
  • 3+ years providing technical leadership on multidisciplinary teams, with demonstrated responsibility for integration readiness, complex fault isolation, and laboratory execution.

Qualifications

  • Strong understanding of neutral-atom quantum computers, including atom trapping, optical addressing, coherent control, and readout.
  • Hands-on capability in optical alignment, laser stability diagnostics, vacuum interfaces, and synchronized RF and control systems.
  • Practical AMO knowledge, including laser-atom interactions and laser cooling and trapping, sufficient to resolve integration issues directly with experimental physicists.
  • Ability to interpret diagnostic data, evaluate automated checkout methods, and isolate hardware or software-interface faults. Laboratory automation experience is preferred.
  • Proven technical leadership and readiness-review discipline, with a record of mentoring colleagues toward qualification while preserving the separate QE acceptance gate.
  • Capable of lifting and moving objects that weigh up to 25 pounds.

Atom Computing provides a wide variety of perks and benefits, including fully paid medical, dental, and vision insurance for our employees and their dependents. Additionally, unlimited paid time off, 401K company matching, short- and long-term disability, FSA, dependent care benefits, and life insurance. We also offer drinks, snacks, and catered team lunches in our offices, every day!

The base salary range for this position is between $200,000 - $230,000, commensurate with experience. In addition to salary, we offer an annual bonus and equity in the company.

title: Sr. Spaceport Designer, Architect (Starbase Development)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. SPACEPORT DESIGNER, ARCHITECT (STARBASE DEVELOPMENT)

As a member of the Starbase Development team you will be directly responsible for designing residential, commercial, and industrial projects that ultimately support the rapid production of Starship. You will directly manage design projects from concept development through execution. You will work with a group of elite architects, engineers and construction project managers across multiple disciplines to build-out the Starbase campus as the gateway to Mars.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Design and build aesthetic and functional architectural projects and associated outdoor spaces, manage all phases of the project from planning to final delivery
  • Partner with cross-departmental teams, stakeholders, and end-users to define requirements and derive design details for all functional and utility needs
  • Define project programming and propose siting and massing options
  • Develop and issue architectural plans, elevations, sections, details, schedules and specifications for bid, permit, and construction documents
  • Produce 3D renders and visualizations to support project design reviews
  • Coordinate project designs with responsible engineers for mechanical, electrical, plumbing, network, audio-visual, fire & life safety systems
  • Write and manage design and construction contracts with subcontractors across multiple disciplines through contract close-out
  • Perform project control tasks, including project scheduling, budgeting, and cost control. Design project to meet target budgets
  • Resolve design and construction conflicts in the field in real time
  • Take on new projects ad-hoc as the business needs

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's or master's degree in architecture, architectural engineering, or other design or technical discipline
  • 5+ years of experience with architectural design
  • Experience with Revit software

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Experience with city planning or master planning for large campuses or developments
  • Experience with designing for industrial, aerospace, or manufacturing projects
  • Experience in modeling and/or rendering software (Rhino, Blender, Sketchup, D5, Enscape, or similar)
  • Experience in AutoCAD suite software and Revu Bluebeam
  • Experience in construction and project management
  • Basic knowledge of photometric analysis and electrical design
  • Knowledge of International Building Codes (IBC)
  • Licensed architect in the state of Texas
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Self-motivated and work autonomously and efficiently in a dynamic team environment

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • This position is based in Starbase, TX and requires being onsite – remote work not considered
  • Must be available to work extended hours and weekends when needed based on site operational needs; flexibility required
  • Must be willing to travel to various SpaceX locations for mission critical projects

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to EEOCompliance@spacex.com.

title: Family Service Coordinator - Rockledge
description:
Salary will be $44,000 per year, includes insurance and time off benefits


Full time position working 40 hours per week, 9:00 am to 5:00 pm


Easterseals Florida is seeking a compassionate and dedicated Family Service Coordinator (FSC) to support families of young children eligible for IDEA, Part C services through our Space Coast Early Steps program. The FSC plays a vital role in empowering families, helping them understand their child’s strengths, needs, and available supports, and serving as the central point of contact from the start to the end of their Early Steps journey.


In this role, you will work with a comprehensive team of professionals to ensure families receive timely evaluations, services, procedural safeguards, and coordinated care. You will serve as a supportive, communicative, and responsive resource to families, helping them navigate resources and advocating for services that promote optimal child development.


What You’ll Do

  • Provide ongoing service coordination for children eligible for Early Steps as the assigned service coordinator
  • Participate in multidisciplinary evaluations, IFSP meetings, and transition planning activities
  • Support eligibility determinations, monitor interventions, and assist families through transitions from IDEA Part C
  • Promote and strengthen the IFSP team’s ability to identify, access, coordinate, and evaluate services and resources
  • Interview families to gather information on routines, strengths, needs, support systems, and developmental concerns
  • Develop timely and comprehensive Individualized Family Support Plans (IFSPs) in collaboration with families and team members
  • Communicate IFSP recommendations with providers, coordinate updates every 6 months, and ensure follow-up for developmental evaluations
  • Coordinate transitions to Part B for families choosing school-based services, including required notifications and planning
  • Assist families not pursuing Part B with developing an appropriate post-Part C plan
  • Maintain accurate case notes, file documentation, and billing practices for CMS Targeted Case Management
  • Travel to family homes or preferred locations to conduct interviews, gather information, and complete coordination tasks


What we offer:

  • Live and on demand Professional Development opportunities
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Plans
  • Paid Holidays, Vacation, Sick, and Personal Time
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Several Supplemental Insurance Policies
  • 401K Savings Plan
  • Easterseals Cares Wellness Program
  • Work Life Balance
  • The Opportunity to Make a Difference in the Community and the Organization


Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university in psychology, social work, early childhood, child development, special education, health education, sociology, or a related field.
  • One year of professional experience working with young children and families in teaching, case management, counseling, or serving individuals with special needs or developmental delays.
  • Ability to secure and maintain a Medicaid Provider Number.
  • Knowledge of community resources, child development, disabilities, and confidentiality/privacy laws.
  • Strong documentation, time-management, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to travel to family homes and adjust schedule to meet family needs.
  • Ability to provide crisis management support when necessary.
  • Demonstrates integrity, tact, strong judgment, flexibility, and a commitment to self-development and quality practices.
  • Commitment to teamwork and to supporting families with empathy and professionalism.
  • Ability to meet our approved driver qualifications in order to drive your personal vehicle, as required, for program-related needs (minimum age of 21 and good driving history)
  • An energetic, resourceful and professional individual who will promote a positive, respectful and team-based environment

title: Senior Engineer, Power Supply
description:
SYSTRA is one of the world's leading engineering and consultancy groups specialising in public transport and sustainable mobility. With over 10,300 employees, SYSTRA's mission is to design safe and sustainable transport solutions to bring people together, develop social inclusion and facilitate access to employment, education and leisure throughout the world.

For 65 years, the Group has been working alongside cities and regions to contribute to their development by creating, improving and modernising their infrastructure and transport systems, throughout the life cycle of their projects. SYSTRA is involved from the earliest stages of design through to the testing, deployment and maintenance phases. The company provides all its services in over 80 countries worldwide and generates 74% of its turnover internationally. With its new services, SYSTRA supports its clients and partners in their digital, ecological and energy transition, in order to invent the mobility of tomorrow.

Context

SYSTRA Taiwan Branch is dedicated to Taiwan and the Group's global rail transit system-related projects, encompassing feasibility analysis, system design, project management, testing and integration, trial operation, and commissioning operations. Currently, we are actively participating in rail transportation projects across Taiwan, with offices located in Taipei and Kaohsiung.

Missions/Main Duties

  • Lead the design, technical studies, and management of railway system projects, including Power Supply System.
  • Develop and review engineering specifications, standards, and procedures for railway system design and construction.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders, including clients, contractors, and regulatory agencies, to ensure compliance with project requirements and regulations.
  • Resolve technical challenges and optimize solutions to meet project objectives within budget and schedule constraints.
  • Mentor and coach junior engineers to foster professional development and knowledge sharing within the team.

What We Offer:

  • Hands-on experience with large-scale railway projects.
  • Opportunities for professional growth, training, and support for certifications.
  • A collaborative and inclusive work environment.
  • Competitive compensation and benefits package.

Profile/Skills

  • Diploma Holder in a STEM Field (Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field is required)
  • Minimum of 10-15 years of experience in railway system preferred.
  • Basic knowledge of railway engineering principles, standards, and regulations.
  • Strong leadership, problem-solving, and decision-making, and analytical skills.
  • Good interpersonal and teamwork skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders.
  • Professional engineering license or certification preferred.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Strong communication skills in both English and Chinese (written and spoken)
  • Excellent organizational and time-management skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks, stay organized, and work independently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Attention to detail and willingness to learn and develop professionally.

Systra is an equal opportunities company; this position is open to all applicants.

Workplace Type

On-site

title: Residential Service Coordinator I
company: Catholic Charities Diocese of San Diego
description:
POSITION TITLE: Residential Services Coordinator I

REPORTS TO: Program Manager

FLSA STATUS: Non-exempt

TIME COMMITMENT: Full-time (40 hours/ week)

SALARY: $25.00 - $27.00 /per hour - DOE


To apply for this position you need to complete this Application

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Residential Services Coordinator’s role is to assist residents at all the properties where Catholic Charities Diocese of San Diego provides services. All Residential Services Coordinators will be working in a hub and spoke model and use a centralized phone and appointment system to offer our clients at multiple residential buildings the opportunity to be assisted in person or virtually, creating equal access to services to all residents and be able to provide specialized services according to their needs. The implementation of a centralized service model enables the Residential Services Coordinators to create standardized processes while reducing the response time for our clients. Residential Service Coordinators will also work with our external partners and other Catholic Charities programs to improve/increase training options as well as expanding the services we offer our clients. Our programs look at all options, especially leveraging social media and technology enhancements, to upgrade and improve our processes.

AGENCY CULTURE:

The business and social environment we operate in has changed. What worked yesterday may not work today and will likely not work tomorrow. To thrive, we must incorporate new ways of thinking and embrace new practices. As part of our individual and agency cultural change process, it is critical that all employees of Catholic Charities aspire to the following:

  • A commitment to the agency’s mission, vision, and values;
  • A commitment to excellence in everything we do;
  • A commitment to excel at performance and quality improvement;
  • A commitment to outcomes and measured results;
  • A commitment to innovation and to what is possible.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Rotate between all the Catholic Charities Diocese of San Diego residential properties and provide quality services to our clients.
  • Become familiar with all of the locations where Catholic Charities Dioceses of San Diego serves clients.
  • Meet regularly with the Residential Services team to review case files and become familiar with the needs of our clients at all of our locations. Look for ways to improve or expand the services we provide them.
  • Train residents on the new appointment process with an emphasis on how to schedule in-person and virtual appointments.
  • Train residents on other ways they can use technology to meet their daily needs or improve their standard of living.
  • Create social opportunities for residents to prevent isolation and create a sense of community among residents.
  • Look at ways to use technology to access services from other Catholic Charities programs to expand services to our clients.
  • Work with external programs to create training opportunities for staff and clients. Work with our Outreach and Communications Department to convert these trainings into webinars and videos so the clients and staff can have access to them at any time.
  • Work with management and the of the Outreach and Communications Department to promote the services provided and help expand the program.
  • Work with management and other team members to regularly review processes and procedures to improve services to the clients.
  • Work with internal and external partners to find ways to improve processes and expand our services to clients.
  • Work in collaboration with all Residential Services Coordinators to provide residents with quality services that enable residents to have a better quality of life.
  • Facilitate conflict resolution among residents, staff, and third parties among all residential buildings served by Catholic Charities Diocese of San Diego.
  • Contribute to a positive and effective teamwork environment with colleagues.
  • Complete all required statistical records, documentation, and reports in a timely manner.
  • Assist with all staff meetings, training sessions, and other appropriate meetings and conferences as required.
  • Assist residents from other properties on an as-needed basis
  • Look at online services and applications, like the Language-Line application, to help enable the team to provide better service to our clients. Language-Line enables us to help clients who need assistance in another language (other than English).
  • Have knowledge of the working of the AASC Online database and phone app. Use these to track appointments and services provided.
  • Maintain records to provide monthly statistical reports (Due every 5th of the month) to the Program Manager and/or Department Director.
  • Be a member of the American Association of Residential Services Coordinators.
  • Acquire 12 Continuing Education Units annually provided by the program.
  • Inform all presumed abuse of residents to the appropriate agency.
  • Build rapport with residents to establish trust.
  • Execute the appropriate evaluation and intake processes to ensure quality delivery of services to clients. Also, look for ways to automate the intake process to make it easier for clients to enter into this program.
  • Facilitate referral and case management for clients to outside services in the case that CCDSD services do not meet the client’s needs.
  • Regularly survey clients to collect feedback on services offered and service satisfaction and collect client input on service improvement opportunities.
  • Collaborate and communicate with all Catholic Charities staff and volunteers to remain consistent in policies and procedures.
  • Adhere to all agency policies and procedures.
  • Complete and submit all required and assigned paperwork in an accurate and timely manner.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Applicants need to be resourceful, and good problem solver
  • Applicants need to be responsible, self-motivated, trustworthy, and able to balance the various requirements of this position so they can help the residents and support their program.
  • Must have a strong desire to help others and should be able to respect, inspire, gain trust, and build confidence among senior citizens and people with disabilities.
  • Needs to be able to communicate and interact with residents with a professional and friendly demeanor.
  • Applicants should have an associate’s Degree (A.A.) in Social Work, Gerontology or a related field.
  • Applicants should have two or three years of experience in social service delivery with seniors and people with disabilities; or a combination of education and experience.
  • Possess knowledge of supportive services for seniors and people with disabilities
  • Ability to advocate, organize, and provide results for those served.
  • Ability to write reports, case notes, business correspondence, and procedure manuals.
  • Possess the ability to effectively present oral and written information and respond to questions from groups of managers, clients, customers, and the public
  • Bilingual in English and Spanish or other languages such as Chinese and Vietnamese (oral and written), preferred.
  • Use of computers, Internet, email, and telephone systems.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Windows, Internet Explorer, and Windows file management.
  • Ability to learn and become proficient with Microsoft Office applications – Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
  • Ability to enter data into a Service Coordinator based software program (training provided).
  • Willingness and aptitude to learn new computer applications and skills as the need arises



PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the requirements of this job. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 40 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include distance vision and watching computer monitors. The employee may need to drive to purchase supplies, attend meetings, and visit residents. This mileage is reimbursed. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.



WORK ENVIRONMENT. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Catholic Charities Diocese of San Diego is a diverse, all-inclusive service organization and employer. We do not discriminate against any candidates on the basis of: race, color, creed, national origin, religion, sex, gender and/or gender reassignment status, age, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy and/or maternity, marriage and/or civil union status, or any other legally protected characteristics.

About the University of Colorado Denver
Millions of moments start at CU Denver, a place where innovation, research, and learning meet in the heart of a global city. We’re the state’s premier public urban research university with more than 100 in-demand, top-ranked bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral degree programs. We partner with diverse learners—at any stage of their life and career—for transformative educational experiences. Across seven schools and colleges, our leading faculty inspires and works alongside students to solve complex challenges and produce impactful creative work. Job Description
* Applications are accepted electronically ONLY at www.cu.edu/cu-careers *

The College of Arts & Media (CAM) at the University of Colorado Denver is seeking a Communications Coordinator to join its marketing team. CAM encompasses three departments on campus- Film & Television, Music & Entertainment Industry Studies, and Visual Arts, and manages the CU Denver Galleries\: the CU Denver Experience Gallery and the Emmanuel Gallery.
This position will contribute stories about our vibrant community to the CAM Press Room, write email and print collateral advertising copy for current and prospective students, and assist in marketing college events. Communications Coordinator

title: Relationsmedarbejder
description:
Relationsmedarbejder med mellemlang videregående uddannelse 28-37 timer Vil du være med til at fremme mening, livskvalitet og lighed i sundhed hos borgere? Ønsker du at bringe din faglighed i spil på nye måder – og ønsker du at være en del af et godt, kreativt og fagligt ambitiøst fællesskab, hvor relationen er en af de vigtigste redskaber? Så er det måske dig, vi søger?

Slotsvænget er et døgndækket socialpsykiatrisk botilbud i Lyngby-Taarbæk Kommune, beliggende i Bondebyen i naturskønne omgivelser, nær Mølleåen. Vi har plads til 21 beboere i alderen fra 18 år og op. Vores beboere har forskellige støttebehov, men fælles for dem alle, er deres behov for at blive set og mødt der, hvor de er og med vores faglige tilgang at fremme levevilkår.

Om jobbet
Vi søger relationsmedarbejdere med lyst og evne til at understøtte en helhedsorienteret indsats. Arbejdsopgaverne vil være alsidige samt kræve faglighed, handlekraft, relationelle og kreative evner.

Hver medarbejder sikrer dagligt samarbejde med bebeboerne via kontakt, samtaler og støtte ud fra mål, aftaler og akut opståede behov. Du kommer til at være en del af en gruppe, bestående af ca. 7 medarbejdere og en teamkoordinator.

Vi sørger for en grundig introduktion og løbende faglig udvikling, hvor du har mulighed for at tilegne dig ny viden inden for forskellige områder som fx Åben Dialog, stemmehøring, CHIME, NADA og mestringsstrategier.

Om dig
Du har minimum en mellemlang videregående uddannelse som eks. pædagog, sygeplejerske eller lign. Du evner at anvende viden og teori i praksis og møde andre mennesker respektfuldt, empatisk, anerkendende og samtidig med blik for det særlige ved den enkelte beboer og dennes livssituation og ønsker for fremtiden. Du bevarer roen, hvis du møder mennesker i højstress og frembringer gode faglige svar og handlemuligheder.

Du har gode samarbejds- og formidlingsevner, og kan arbejde målrettet og systematisk med de forskelligartede opgaver, som favner bredt og du får, i samarbejdet med beboerne, tingene til at ske. Derudover er du aktiv i forhold til at tilegne dig Slotsvængets faglige tilgang, samt udvikling af egne kompetencer og refleksion over egen praksis.

Vi har spurgt vores beboere, hvad der er vigtigt for dem, hos vores nye kollega:
“… er sød ved mennesker, er fagligt dygtig, hjælper med at komme til lægen, forstår både krop og følelser og ikke er fordomsfuld.”

Det er en stor fordel, hvis du har kørekort.

Om os
Vores arbejdsplads er kendetegnet ved at have en støttende og inkluderende arbejdskultur, hvor du ikke blot er en kollega, men en vigtig del af vores fællesskab.

Som bosted har vi en grundlæggende tro på, at psykiske udfordringer kommer fra traumer og gennem samspil med andre. Vi ved, at mennesker med alvorlige psykiske problemer, kan komme sig og udvikle sig positivt.

Det er vigtigt for os, sammen med den enkelte beboer, at skabe alternativer/supplementer til medicinsk behandling fx NADA, samtaler, bevægelse og livshistorisk arbejde. Selvbestemmelse og ligeværd er ydermere grundlæggende værdier i vores arbejde, og vores bosted er kendetegnet ved et lavt konfliktniveau.

Den faste stilling er på 28-37 timer med skiftende vagter primært fordelt på dag- og aftentimer mellem kl. 07-22.15 samt hver 2. weekend. En sjælden gang kan enkelte nattevagter forekomme. Tiltrædelse snarest muligt.

Løn og ansættelsesvilkår sker efter relevant overenskomst. Ansættelsen er betinget af tilfredsstillende straffeattest.

title: Senior Data Scientist
description:
About Arena Club

Arena Club is building the number one digital marketplace for collectibles. We started by reinventing the hobby with the first-ever digital card show, and we are expanding into new categories so collectors can buy, sell, grade, and showcase everything they care about in one place. Spearheaded by 5x World Series Champion Derek Jeter and serial entrepreneur Brian Lee, our fully digital marketplace is grounded in trust, transparency, and fun, featuring grading and authentication, vaulting, and digital pack openings that let collectors build and display their collections in a personalized online showroom from anywhere in the world.

About the Role

We’re seeking a Senior Data Scientist to join us as our first dedicated data science hire. In this key role, you will own our predictive modeling and advanced analytics, turning complex data points into actionable strategies. You will design, build, and deploy the algorithms and statistical frameworks that optimize user behavior, personalization, forecasting, and marketplace dynamics.

This is a unique opportunity for an autonomous, senior-level individual contributor who thrives on transforming ambiguous business problems into rigorous mathematical solutions. Operating at the intersection of product and commerce, you will partner closely with Product, Marketing, and Engineering teams to deliver the core data systems that drive our growth and platform performance.

What You’ll Do

  • Establish the Foundation: Act as the founding data scientist, defining best practices for model development, experimentation frameworks, tracking metrics, and data repository structures
  • Drive Strategic Impact: Partner directly with leadership and cross-functional teams to identify high-value opportunities where predictive modeling and data science can move core business metrics
  • Build & Deploy Models: Design, build, and evaluate machine learning models and analytical frameworks that optimize dynamic pricing, forecasting, curation, and personalization
  • Enhance Product & Discovery: Clean, explore, and analyze user behavior across our Marketplace and Arena Packs to drive data-driven feature decisions, optimize discovery algorithms, and improve recommendation systems
  • Tackle Ambiguity: Translate open-ended, complex business questions into clear analytical problems with measurable success criteria and robust mathematical foundations
  • Lead Experimentation: Design, execute, and interpret A/B tests and causal inference frameworks to rigorously measure the impact of new features, marketing campaigns, and core business initiatives
  • Maintain Clean Workflows: Build reliable, localized data workflows, analysis pipelines, and reusable codebases using Python and modern data tooling
  • Communicate Insights: Present complex technical findings, data visualizations, and strategic recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders across the organization

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field; advanced degree preferred
  • 6+ years of professional experience in applied data science, with a proven track record of designing, shipping, and maintaining models or decision systems in a consumer-facing production environment
  • Practical applied experience across multiple core data science disciplines: product analytics, recommendation systems, user behavior modeling, pricing, forecasting, or revenue/margin optimization
  • Strong foundation in predictive analytics, supervised/unsupervised learning, statistical modeling (regression, classification, clustering), and causal inference (A/B testing, hypothesis testing, lift measurement, business impact interpretation)
  • Expert-level proficiency in Python and the ML ecosystem (Scikit-learn, PyTorch or TensorFlow)
  • Advanced SQL skills for complex data extraction, cleansing, feature engineering, and processing
  • Experience tracking and managing experiments using tools like MLflow
  • Comfort with experimentation and causal inference basics (A/B testing, lift measurement, business impact interpretation)
  • Experience with AWS (EC2, S3, and related services) for data workflows

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in marketplaces, retail or e-commerce, or consumer tech
  • Familiarity with Snowflake and a dbt metrics layer
  • Domain interest in collectibles, trading cards, or hard-asset markets



The base salary range listed is a guideline. Actual compensation is determined based on skills, experience, and the impact you bring. Total compensation includes base salary, bonus, and equity.

Salary Range
$190,000—$250,000 USD

title: Maintenance Assistant
description:
What you'll bring to the team

Imagine using your hands-on maintenance skills to help keep an incredible aquarium running smoothly and looking its best. Does that sound like the kind of role where you will thrive? About You

  • You are a strong communicator who builds positive relationships and works well with different teams and external contractors.

Benefits

  • Corporate benefits including free access to all our attractions worldwide

  • Additional Leave (including birthday and wellbeing) and 3 volunteer days to give back to a social cause you care about

About Us Merlin Entertainments is the company behind iconic brands like SEA LIFE, Madame Tussauds, and Peppa Pig World of Play. We operate in over 140 attractions across 25 countries, delivering memorable experiences to 54 million+ visitors a year.

We’re the leading operator of visitor attractions in Australia and New Zealand, with 10 attractions, including SEA LIFE, WILDLIFE, Madame Tussauds, amongst others.

Merlin Entertainments is driven by a strong social responsibility with the vision to create a world where the global community respects, conserves, and sustainably manages our precious aquatic habitats, wildlife, and natural resources. We strive to achieve this goal through our 3 charities: Merlins Magic Wand, the SEA LIFE Trust, and the WILDLIFE Conservation Fund. So, if you are vibrant and passionate about delivering an amazing service within a great company and in a team who loves what we do – then we want to hear from you!

Competitive

title: Architect
description:
The architect will support the planning, design, and modernization of research and laboratory facilities at Idaho National Laboratory (INL), the Department of Energy's lead nuclear energy research and development site. INL has recently delivered major capital projects such as a new Sample Preparation Laboratory supporting research and qualification of structural nuclear materials, and new mission facilities including the Cybercore Integration Center and the Collaborative Computing Center. Potential work may include developing architectural concepts and construction documents for specialized research laboratories, nuclear and energy facilities, and secure or mission-critical buildings, while ensuring compliance with DOE standards, federal building codes, safety and security requirements, and sustainability goals.

Idaho National Laboratory is hiring a Architect to work on our Facility Design and Project Engineering team. Our team works a 9x80 schedule located out of our Idaho Falls facility with every other Friday off. Regular work at our desert site locations is expected.

Essential Job Functions and Responsibilities:

  • Perform architectural design for building and facility projects, including development of design concepts, space planning, building systems coordination, and preparation of architectural drawings, specifications, and design documents.
  • Ensure architectural designs comply with applicable building codes, accessibility standards, life safety requirements, and DOE/BEA standards.
  • Serve as the primary architectural point of contact and chairman/organizer for design reviews, verification walk-downs, and constructability reviews.
  • Coordinate architectural deliverables with engineering disciplines, vendors, and subcontractors to ensure integrated, code-compliant designs.

  • Provide technical leadership and decision-making for architectural design in conjunction with Project Management inputs.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

  • Knowledge of architectural design principles, building systems, materials, and construction methods.
  • Knowledge of applicable building codes, accessibility (ADA) standards, life safety codes, and related regulatory requirements.
  • Proficiency in architectural design and drafting software (e.g., Revit, AutoCAD, BIM tools).
  • Knowledge of project engineering, project management, and project control activities. Knowledge in project engineering and management tools and DOE work package and change control process and systems.
  • Knowledge of the practical application of architecture, engineering science and technology. This includes applying principles, techniques, procedures, and equipment to the design and production of various goods and services, and building/facility design.

Required:

  • Professional Architecture License: Current license to practice architecture in the State of Idaho (or ability to obtain Idaho licensure by reciprocity within 6 months).
  • Required Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch) or Master of Architecture (M.Arch) degree from a program accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB).
  • Level 3: Bachelor's degree and 5 years of related experience or Master's degree and 2 years of related experience.
  • Level 4: Bachelor's degree and 9 years of related experience or Master's degree and 6 years of related experience.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a “Q” clearance which requires US Citizenship.
  • May be required to receive PMP within two years of selection.
  • May require review and approval by the Engineering Committee.


The ideal candidate will possess:

  • NCARB certification.
  • LEED accreditation.
  • Previous experience working in a federal, state, or other public-sector projects such as those for the Department of Energy (DOE), with demonstrated knowledge of applicable government codes, standards, and compliance requirements.


Physical Requirements:

While performing the duties of this classification, the employee is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, stoop, kneel, bend, and work in an office and field environment, which may include construction sites. The job requires hand/finger dexterity to keyboard or type, handle materials, manipulate tools, and reach with hands and arms. The job requires operation of job-related equipment and driving a vehicle. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 pounds. Sufficient visual acuity and hearing capacity to perform the essential functions and interact with the public is required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Job Information:

  • The pay range for this position is: Level 3 ($79,344 - $162,732) / Level 4 ($95,256 - $195,288). At Idaho National Laboratory compensation decisions are determined using factors such as education, relevant experience, and other credentials.
  • Multi-Level: This is a multi-level posting and you will be placed at the appropriate level dependent on depth and breadth of proven experience and skills.
  • TDP: This is a testing designated position; you will be required to submit to a pre-employment drug screen and periodic drug testing throughout the term of your employment.

title: Sundhedsprofessionel leder til Borgernær Sundhed SUH
description:
Er du en leder, der trives i en hverdag, hvor rammerne ikke er færdigdefinerede? Så er det dig, vi søger

Vi søger en leder til vores nyetablerede afsnit for Borgernær Sundhed Sjællands Universitetshospital (SUH) Køge og Nykøbing F, dækkende for hele optageområdet i Sundhedsråd Østsjælland og Øerne.

Du vil organisatorisk indgå i en afsnitsledelse sammen med oversygeplejerske. Sammen skal I skabe et ledelsesteam med flere perspektiver på arbejdsopgaverne, og samarbejde tæt om udvikling, drift og personaleledelse på tværs af afsnittet. Derudover vil du organisatorisk indgå i et lederteam med to øvrige afsnitsledelser og have et tæt samarbejde med afdelingsledelsen.

Som sundhedsfaglig leder for fremtidens myndighedsområde får du en central rolle i at omsætte Sundhedsreformen til konkret praksis og udvikle myndighedsområdet på tværs af sektorer. Du bliver en nøgleperson i både etablering, drift og videreudvikling af Sundheds- og omsorgspladserne (SOP) – med afsæt i gældende kvalitetsstandard og med fokus på høj faglighed, Patientsikkerhed og borgernær værdi.

Med sundhedsreformen flytter ansvaret for myndighedsområdet og akutsygeplejen til den nyetablerede geriatriske afdeling SUH Køge og Nykøbing F.

Det stiller nye krav til ledelse, koordinering og samarbejde på tværs af sektorer. Derfor søger vi en sundhedsfaglig leder med ansvar for det samlede myndighedsområde i vores sundhedsrådsområde, som dækker over kommunerne: Roskilde, Solrød, Greve, Køge, Stevns, Faxe, Vordingborg, Guldborgsund og Lolland.

Med reference til afdelingsledelsen, får du en afgørende rolle i transformationen og skal sikre, at borgerne oplever en samlet, tilgængelig og højt kvalificeret indsats, der skal styrke det nære og sammenhængende sundhedsvæsen.

Dine primære arbejdsopgaver bliver at:

• lede og udvikle det borgernære sundhedstilbud, på tværs af hospital og kommuner

• sikre høj faglig kvalitet og ensartede standarder i hele optageområdet

• opbygge stærke samarbejdsrelationer mellem hospital, kommuner, almen praksis og øvrige aktører

• drive implementeringen af nye arbejdsgange og organisering som følge af strukturreformen, herunder kompetenceløft af medarbejdere, så kompetencerne matcher den fremtidige opgave

• bidrage til at gøre hospitalet mere udadvendt

• bidrage til strategisk udvikling af det borgernære område

• understøtte en kultur præget af omsorg, omhu, innovation, læring og høj medarbejdertrivsel

Er du en erfaren leder med lyst til at sætte retning, skabe struktur og videreudvikle fagligheden i en afdeling i forandring?

Vi søger en erfaren og visionær leder, der kan navigere i en kompleks organisation og skabe resultater gennem samarbejde. Du skal kunne se dig selv i SUH's værdier: Ordentlighed, følgeskab, fællesskab og nytænkning.

Som sundhedsfagligleder vil du få en fremtrædende rolle i omstruktureringen og organiseringen af de nye opgaver, der kommer i forbindelse med regionsfusion og sundhedsreform

Vi søger en kandidat med følgende profil:

• er sundhedsfagligt uddannet med solid ledelseserfaring – gerne på mellemlederniveau

• har relevant lederuddannelse, fx diplom eller master i ledelse eller tilsvarende

• har indgående kendskab til både hospitalsvæsenet og det kommunale sundhedsområde, herunder sundhedsaftaler og tværsektorielt samarbejde

• har indsigt i de juridiske aspekter af arbejdet i en myndighedsafdeling

• du kan gå ind i i dilemma- og konfliktfyldte situationer med en positiv tilgang og med henblik på at finde den mest optimale løsning for patienten/borgeren

• evner at skabe psykologisk tryghed, så dine medarbejdere tør tale om, når det er svært med samarbejdet med borgere, pårørende eller samarbejdspartnere

• har erfaring med forandringsledelse og implementering af nye organisatoriske løsninger og samarbejdsformer

• arbejder strategisk og nytænkende og formår at omsætte visioner til konkret praksis

• er tydelig, inddragende og handlekraftig i din ledelsesstil

• har stærke relationelle kompetencer og kan skabe tillid på tværs af sektorer

• har evnen til at samle flere matrikler om en fælles kultur

Vi tilbyder:

• en nyoprettet lederstilling med stort ledelsesrum

• en unik mulighed for at præge fremtidens indsatser i det nære

• en central lederrolle i en af sundhedsvæsenets mest markante strukturændringer

• et stærkt fagligt miljø med engagerede medarbejdere og ledelseskolleger

• Et rart arbejdsmiljø med høj trivsel og gennemsigtighed

• En travl hverdag, hvor den gode tone og den gode stemning sættes højt

• En afdeling der ikke går på kompromis med oplæring og uddannelse

• gode muligheder for faglig og personlig udvikling

• en hverdag præget af høj kompleksitet, tempo og stor indflydelse

Om afdelingen

Stillingen er forankret i Geriatrisk afdeling på SUH, som vil bestå af et afsnit dedikeret til Borgernær Sundhed og 2 geriatriske sengeafsnit med tilhørende ambulante funktioner. Afsnit for Borgernær Sundhed etableres for at understøtte Sundhedsreformens ambition om at skabe et mere nært, sammenhængende og lige sundhedsvæsen.

Ansvaret for akutsygeplejen, myndighedsområdet på SOP og implementeringen af speciallægedækning af sundheds- og omsorgspladser, vil ligge her.

I din ansøgning skal du beskrive, hvordan du vil bidrage til at udvikle myndighedsområdet på tværs af hospital og kommuner

Region Sjælland og Region Hovedstaden bliver den 1. januar 2027 til Region Østdanmark som følge af sundhedsreformen. Dit ansættelsesområde vil være Region Østdanmark med alle tilhørende organisatoriske enheder.

Sjællands Universitetshospital er Danmarks nyeste universitetshospital med aktiviteter i Køge, Roskilde og Nykøbing F. Vi er et modigt og udadvendt universitetshospital, hvor vi hver dag arbejder for at skabe et sammenhængende sundhedsvæsen og større lighed i sundhed for borgerne i regionen.

title: Senior Embedded Software Engineer – TCAS / Surveillance Avionics
description:
We don’t just build technology—we engineer the future. From next-gen aerospace to cutting-edge defense systems, we tackle the toughest, mission-critical challenges that keep people safe and push the limits of innovation. This is where problem-solvers, innovators, and big thinkers thrive.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Embedded Software Engineer to develop, integrate, verify, and maintain safety-critical airborne software supporting TCAS/ACAS and surveillance avionics systems. This hands-on role requires strong C/C++, real-time embedded systems, and DO-178B/C experience. The engineer will support requirements, design, implementation, verification, integration, troubleshooting, certification documentation, and FAA certification activities.

Location: Phoenix, Arizona. On-site preferred, 3+ days/week

Citizenship: U.S. Person

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain TCAS/ACAS and airborne surveillance software using C/C++ in real-time and RTOS environments.
  • Design, implement, integrate, and verify safety-critical embedded software.
  • Analyze, modify, integrate, and troubleshoot new and legacy software.
  • Develop and maintain requirements, traceability, design documentation, source code, and lifecycle data.
  • Develop and execute unit and integration tests and perform requirements-based verification.
  • Integrate software with avionics hardware, RF, FPGA/firmware, and aircraft systems.
  • Debug software, perform root-cause analysis, resolve defects, and support JIRA defect burn-down.
  • Participate in code, peer, requirements, design, verification, and Critical Design Reviews (CDRs).
  • Maintain software build environments, toolchains, version control, and configuration management.
  • Support software baselines, releases, and configuration management.
  • Support DO-178B/C, DO-185B, RTCA MOPS, FAA certification audits/reviews, findings, and technical issues.
  • Develop and maintain certification lifecycle data covering planning, requirements, design, implementation, verification/validation, configuration management, and quality assurance.
  • Work with systems, hardware, RF, verification, certification, program, and customer teams to resolve technical issues and drive actions to closure.

Required Qualifications

  • 5–15 years of relevant embedded software engineering experience, preferably in airborne or other safety-critical systems.
  • Strong C and C++ development skills.
  • Experience with real-time embedded systems and RTOS environments.
  • Experience analyzing, modifying, integrating, and troubleshooting existing or legacy embedded software.
  • Strong debugging and root-cause analysis skills.
  • Experience with embedded software and hardware/software integration.
  • Experience developing and executing unit and integration tests.
  • Experience with requirements-based development, verification, traceability, design, implementation, and configuration management.
  • Experience with formal code/peer reviews.
  • Experience with software build environments, toolchains, version control, and configuration management.
  • Experience with JIRA or similar defect-management systems.
  • Experience producing engineering documentation within a controlled software lifecycle.
  • Strong technical communication and ability to drive actions to closure.
  • Direct experience with TCAS/ACAS, ADS-B, transponder, or other airborne surveillance software.
  • Working knowledge of TCAS/ACAS functionality, surveillance concepts, and aircraft interfaces.
  • Experience with DO-178B/C airborne software development and certification.
  • Experience developing/supporting DO-178 lifecycle data, including planning, requirements, design, implementation, verification, configuration management, and certification evidence.
  • Familiarity with DO-185B and applicable TCAS MOPS/test criteria.
  • Must meet U.S. Person requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with FAA certification audits, reviews, or Software Stages of Involvement (SOI).
  • Familiarity with surveillance/collision avoidance RTCA standards and FAA Technical Standard Orders.
  • Experience with requirements-based testing, requirements-to-test traceability, and structural coverage.
  • Experience with safety-critical verification, including:
    • Low- and high-level requirements-based testing
    • Robustness testing
    • Structural coverage analysis
    • MC/DC, where applicable
  • Experience with ARINC 429, AFDX, or other aircraft communication protocols.
  • Familiarity with RF-based surveillance systems and RF/FPGA hardware interaction.
  • Experience supporting laboratory, aircraft integration, qualification, or flight-test activities.

The QDSS Advantage

At QDSS, our advantage is purpose-driven work, collaborative teams, and complex challenges that push boundaries and build lasting impact. You’ll grow your career while contributing to mission-critical programs that demand excellence and shape the future.

What You’ll Find Here
