title: Senior Data & Integrations Engineer – People & Finance
description:
High performance isn't a given. It’s built on standards.

Standards that have driven McLaren for over 60 years.

And if you’re ready for the challenge, that standard is yours to own.

Burning enthusiasm. Constant improvement. The thrill in the pursuit of better.

That’s how we build a legacy. And how you build a career here.

Because racing isn’t just something we do. It’s who we are.

We are racers.

Are you?

Job Description

This is a hands-on technical role within the Business Performance function, helping connect McLaren Racing’s People and Finance platforms with the wider enterprise technology landscape.

Working under the direction of the Associate Director, People & Finance Technology & Data, you will design, build, maintain and improve secure, reliable and scalable integrations. Your work will enable data and transactions to move accurately between Workday and other McLaren systems.

You will also work with enterprise technology teams to clarify system dependencies, ownership, controls and data flows, reducing manual hand-offs and enabling joined-up processes, reporting and decision-making across the organisation.

Principal Accountabilities

Data Engineering and Integration

  • Design, build, test, deploy and support secure inbound and outbound integrations across People, Finance and wider McLaren technologies.
  • Develop and maintain robust data pipelines that provide timely, accurate and trusted datasets.
  • Translate business and technical requirements into scalable integration designs, covering data mappings, transformation logic, scheduling, security, error handling and reconciliation.
  • Extract, transform and exchange data through SQL, APIs, web services, file-based interfaces and approved integration tools.
  • Assess the upstream and downstream impact of changes to systems, processes, data structures and interfaces.
  • Develop monitoring, validation, alerting and reconciliation controls that identify integration failures and data-quality issues.
  • Investigate incidents, complete root-cause analysis and implement sustainable fixes.
  • Replace manual extracts, uploads and reconciliations with controlled, automated integrations where appropriate.

Enterprise Systems Integration

  • Support integrations between Workday and enterprise systems including Salesforce, SmartRecruiters, Clockify, Microsoft Azure and Power Automate.
  • Work with system owners to define sources of truth, integration direction, frequency, data ownership and support models.
  • Contribute to integration architecture, identifying dependencies, transition requirements and opportunities to simplify the application landscape.
  • Support data migration and interface activity associated with Workday Financials and other transformation programmes.
  • Ensure integrations align with McLaren standards for enterprise architecture, security, privacy, data governance and access control.
  • Maintain clear documentation covering interfaces, endpoints, schedules, dependencies, data mappings, runbooks and support procedures.

Collaboration and Project Delivery

  • Partner with People, Finance, IT and Commercial technology teams to deliver joined-up system and data solutions.
  • Support integration discovery with business owners, technical teams, vendors and implementation partners.
  • Translate end-to-end process requirements into integration needs that support the complete workflow.
  • Coordinate integration design, testing, deployment and handover across internal teams and external partners.
  • Support Workday releases, configuration changes and technology deployments through impact assessments and regression testing.
  • Clarify ownership and support responsibilities, escalating material risks, unresolved dependencies and control gaps.
  • Contribute to reusable integration standards, patterns and governance.

Qualifications

You will bring experience as a Data Engineer, BI Developer, Data Analyst or in a similar role within a data-driven environment, or hold a relevant degree or qualification.

You Will Also Have

  • Good SQL skills for data extraction, transformation and troubleshooting.
  • A practical understanding of APIs, REST, SOAP, JSON, XML, SFTP, web services, authentication methods and ETL/ELT patterns.
  • Exposure to data modelling and preparing datasets for reporting environments, ideally Power BI.
  • The ability to build and maintain data pipelines and integrations in structured, repeatable ways.
  • High attention to detail and a strong commitment to data accuracy.
  • An awareness of data privacy, security and the careful handling of confidential information.

Experience with Workday HCM, Workday Financials, Workday Prism or Adaptive Planning would be advantageous. Familiarity with Power Automate or Power Apps would also be beneficial.

Personal Attributes

You will be analytical, organised and proactive, with strong problem-solving and communication skills. You will be able to translate technical data concepts for non-technical People and Finance users and build positive working relationships across teams.

You will remain calm and effective under pressure, adapt quickly to new systems and bring curiosity, attention to detail and a commitment to continuously improving data processes.

Additional Information

Success in racing comes from bringing together talented people with different skills, perspectives and experiences. We're committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone feels supported and empowered to deliver their best work.

Every role has the potential to drive high performance. You'll be part of a team united by a shared ambition to push boundaries and embody our racing mindset. We invest in our people through opportunities to develop and grow, creating an environment where individuals and teams can thrive.

Alongside a range of wellbeing initiatives and development opportunities, we're committed to helping you build a rewarding career and make your mark at McLaren Racing.

description:
Full job description

Job Title: Lead Dog Groomer
Job Type: Full-Time, Non-Exempt
Reports To: Store Manager
Pay: Up to $31 per hour + up to 45% commission and bonuses
Revised: July 2026

Job Summary

We are seeking an experienced and motivated Lead Dog Groomer to provide high-quality grooming services and to offer leadership, coaching, and technical direction to a team of groomers and bathers. This role combines hands-on grooming expertise with team development, quality control, and customer service excellence.

The ideal candidate is a skilled groomer with strong leadership abilities, a passion for pet care, and a commitment to delivering exceptional service and results.

Key Responsibilities

Grooming Services and Client Experience

  • Provide comprehensive grooming services in a salon environment
  • Greet customers and their dogs by name and communicate a best-estimate pick-up time
  • Perform a needs assessment for each assigned dog, evaluating the condition of eyes, ears, nails, teeth, coat, and skin
  • Suggest de-matting services, a short haircut, additional services, and products to customers based on that assessment, as appropriate
  • Describe benefits and options for all suggested add-ons, and communicate knowledgeably about all of Groombar's products and services, including nutrition, training, and dental cleaning
  • Obtain detailed instructions from customers regarding the haircut desired, take comprehensive notes, and record them in each customer's account for future reference
  • Clearly communicate fees associated with all services
  • Notify owners when service has been completed and ensure hourly contact occurs thereafter until the pet is picked up
  • Execute the GOTHEART strategy during every customer check-in, deliver exceptional customer service, and ensure a positive salon experience


Leadership and Team Development

  • Provide day-to-day leadership, coaching, and technical guidance to groomers and bathers
  • Train and support skill development for bathers, and maintain grooming and bathing quality standards across the team
  • Model safe dog handling techniques and customer experience excellence
  • Perform regular quality checks on groomers and bathers
  • Participate in performance meetings and support team performance improvement
  • As needed, manage performance, including rewarding and disciplining employees, addressing complaints, and resolving problems
  • Ensure employee responsibilities, authorities, and accountabilities are defined and understood
  • Address and resolve customer concerns, including making service corrections when needed

Operations and Performance

  • Maintain strong customer service standards and meet or exceed established goals
  • Adapt to changing priorities, including assisting and assigning walk-in grooming services
  • Communicate effectively and professionally with customers and team members

Safety and Additional Duties

  • Ensure accuracy of release forms, kennel cards, and service documentation
  • Monitor pets for stress, health concerns, or behavioral changes and report as needed
  • Ensure kenneled pets are comfortable, safe, and have access to water
  • Check dogs hourly for any signs of stress
  • Communicate any health or safety concerns to management and pet owners
  • Ensure the salon environment is safe, clean, and free of hazards, and that equipment and tools are operating as intended
  • Respond appropriately to personnel or dog injuries, ensuring both employees and dogs receive prompt and appropriate medical care, and injuries are reported
  • Perform other salon-related duties as assigned by Store Manager and Field Leadership, as needed

Salon Maintenance and Compliance

  • Maintain a clean, safe, and organized grooming environment
  • Ensure completion of daily and weekly cleaning and sanitation lists
  • Respond appropriately to any pet or employee incidents, ensuring proper care and reporting

Compensation and Benefits

  • Pay: Up to $31 per hour + up to 45% commission and bonuses
  • Strong earning potential with a competitive commission structure
  • Bonus structure surrounding salon performance and growth
  • Exclusive Professional Development Opportunity:

Participate in bi-weekly, hands-on mentorship and leadership development sessions with a team of multi-award-winning international competition groomers. With over 20 years of experience in advanced grooming techniques, salon leadership, and professional instruction, this mentorship offers a rare opportunity to elevate your craft, refine advanced skills, and grow as a leader in the grooming industry.

title: Senior / Principal Scientist, Molecular Simulations
description:
About the Role:

FL117, a venture-backed stealth AI x bio company, is seeking a Sr. Scientist / Principal Scientist, Molecular Simulations. Here you will build the physics layer of a drug development AI platform. You will characterize how binders engage their targets and validate generated designs before they are committed to synthesis. You will work at the interface of structure-based modeling and generative ML, turning simulation output into training signals. We are looking for a hands-on simulation scientist who is comfortable owning a method end to end in a cross-functional, fast-moving team.

Responsibilities:

  • Binder Characterization: Run and interpret structural and dynamic analysis of ligand–target complexes peptides, macrocycles, nanobodies/VHHs, antibody CDRs.
  • Pocket & Target Assessment: Characterize binding sites, including cryptic and induced-fit pockets, across the target portfolio using MD, enhanced sampling, and pocket detection methods.
  • Design Validation: Triage generated molecules before synthesis through a combination of pose prediction and refinement, docking rescoring, binding-mode stability under MD, ligand strain and conformational ensemble analysis, and define the criteria by which a design advances or gets killed.
  • Free Energy & Affinity Prediction: Build, validate, and own the affinity prediction workflow (relative and absolute FEP, MM-GBSA/PBSA, endpoint methods); establish its accuracy and applicability domain against measured data and report both honestly.
  • Beyond-Rule-of-5 Properties: Model conformational behavior, intramolecular hydrogen bonding, chameleonicity, and membrane partitioning for macrocycles and other non-classical chemotypes to support oral property design.
  • Simulation-to-ML Interface: Convert simulation output into structured signal for the generative platform in close partnership with the AI/ML team.
  • Infrastructure & Throughput: Build reproducible, automated simulation pipelines on GPU cloud or HPC infrastructure; own system setup, parameterization, QC, and analysis at portfolio scale rather than one system at a time.
  • Cross-functional Partnership: Work directly with medicinal chemistry, pharmacology, and external structural biology and assay partners; turn structural hypotheses into testable designs, feed returning data back into corrected models, and flag clearly where predictions are unreliable.

Must-have Qualifications:

  • PhD in computational chemistry, biophysics, chemical physics, structural biology, or a related field; MSc with equivalent industry depth considered
  • 4+ years of post-PhD molecular simulation experience, at least part of it in a drug discovery setting (Sr. Scientist); 6+ years with demonstrated ownership of a method or platform (Principal)
  • Deep hands-on expertise in classical molecular dynamics: force fields and small molecule parameterization (AMBER/CHARMM/OPLS, GAFF/OpenFF), solvation and ion treatment, equilibration protocols, and the characteristic failure modes of each.
  • Production experience with at least one enhanced sampling or free energy framework (relative or absolute FEP/TI, metadynamics, umbrella sampling, replica exchange, or weighted-ensemble MD) including validation against measured affinities.
  • Structure-based drug design fundamentals: docking and pose evaluation, pharmacophore and hot-spot analysis, and critical assessment of experimental and predicted structures.
  • Strong Python, with fluency in simulation toolchains (OpenMM, GROMACS, AMBER, NAMD, or Desmond) and analysis stacks (MDAnalysis/MDTraj, RDKit); version control and reproducible workflows as habit, not aspiration.
  • Demonstrated ability to run simulations at scale on GPU, HPC, or cloud infrastructure through automation rather than manual per-system setup.
  • Judgment about method cost versus decision value: able to say when a multi-week free energy campaign is warranted and when docking plus a short MD run is enough.
  • Consistent record of outstanding technical output reflected in publications, patents, or high impact internal reports

Preferred Experience:

  • Peptide, macrocycle, or other beyond-Rule-of-5 simulation: conformational ensembles, intramolecular hydrogen bonding, chameleonicity, and membrane permeability (ex: water-to-membrane transfer free energies).
  • Experienced with target classes such as: GPCRs, protein–protein interactions, transcription factors, highly dynamic target classes.
  • Working with predicted structures and their limitations (AlphaFold-class models, co-folding methods), and with cryptic or induced-fit pocket discovery.
  • ML-adjacent simulation work: machine-learned force fields and potentials (ANI, MACE, NequIP-class), learned scoring functions, or generating simulation-derived features for downstream generative models.
  • Workflow and infrastructure tooling: Snakemake/Nextflow, Airflow/Prefect/Dagster, Docker, AWS (Batch, ParallelCluster, S3), and experiment tracking (MLflow/W&B).
  • Clear structural communication to non-specialists using PyMOL, ChimeraX, or Mol*. Please send a link to representative figures or your GitHub, if applicable.
  • Strong presence in the computational chemistry or biophysics community through publications and conference proceedings. Please send a list of publications, if applicable.

title: Software Engineer, AI Infrastructure (Starshield)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SOFTWARE ENGINEER, AI INFRASTRUCTURE (STARSHIELD)

At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy the Starshield constellation. Starshield is the world’s largest US government satellite constellation and is tasked with providing immediate access to critical intelligence and national security data for the US government anywhere on the globe. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – receivers that allow users to connect within minutes, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starshield's global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help us further our ambitious goals.

As an engineer focused on Starshield's software and GPU infrastructure, you will design, operate and scale the infrastructure that supports critical national security missions. These positions cover a variety of areas ranging from Site Reliability Engineering, Developer Operations, and GPU platforms. You will develop automation to deploy and manage on-premise compute resources, create highly scalable and maintainable software products, and directly collaborate with engineering across the board.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Manage GPU/CPU infrastructure deployments to Top Secret datacenters
  • Manage and provide support for GPU as a service for external customers on bare metal hardware and virtualized platforms
  • Design, validate, and productize solutions for AI clusters (100k+ GPU scale)
  • Develop automation to deploy and manage on-premise Kubernetes\AI clusters, and operating systems
  • Deploy and manage core infrastructure such as databases, monitoring and distributed storage
  • Closely collaborate with AI engineers to create highly scalable, operable, and maintainable products
  • Engage in and improve the whole lifecycle of services -- from inception and design, through deployment, operation and refinement
  • Monitoring and alerting supporting systems to have high availability
  • Identify areas for improvement and create innovative solutions that enable high system availability

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems/IT, or an engineering discipline and 1+ years of professional experience in site reliability engineering or DevOps; OR 3+ years of professional experience in site reliability engineering or DevOps in lieu of a degree
  • 1+ years of professional experience with Linux operating systems
  • Experience with Terraform, Ansible, or other infrastructure tools
  • Experience with containerization technologies (i.e. OCI containers, Kubernetes)
  • Experience scripting in Bash, Python, or other similar languages
  • Development experience in Python, C++, or Go

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • 1+ years of experience with Python and Python-based development frameworks
  • Experience managing Kubernetes clusters, not just using them
  • Knowledge of Linux boot process and systems configuration
  • Deep understanding of testing, continuous integration, build, deployment & continuous monitoring
  • Understanding of relevant build technologies, such as Bazel and Makefiles
  • Focus on performance bottlenecks and performance improvement techniques
  • Understanding of distributed databases and data modeling
  • Experience with automatically managing thousands of servers (eg: Terraform or Ansible)
  • Strong networking knowledge of TCP/IP
  • Cloud virtualization experience (as the cloud provider)
  • Experience using NVIDIA GPU deployment stacks (Blackwell/Rubin)
  • Excellent communications skills with the ability to communicate with customers, peers, management etc. in both formal and informal situations
  • Active Top Secret, Top Secret SCI, or DOE Level Q clearance

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed
  • Must be willing to travel domestically and globally in the future when needed
  • This position requires successfully obtaining and maintaining a Top Secret Security Clearance as a condition of employment. While the clearance may not be immediately necessary upon hire, we encourage you to initiate the application process promptly upon accepting this offer. Your ability to secure the necessary clearance is essential for fulfilling key responsibilities of the role. Should you be unable to obtain it, SpaceX reserves the right to modify or terminate your employment to align with operational needs.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 1: $125,000.00 - $160,000.00
Level 2: $145,000.00 - $195,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

Those with an active clearance will receive a 10% differential, up to an additional $20,000 annually, once officially briefed into a classified program.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: 2nd Shift Fabricator
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

Fabricators operate various machines and hand tools in the fabrication department that cut, shape or grind sheet metal such as shears, brake press, hand grinders, insert press or punch or drill press. Fabricators use various hand tools to assemble components according to print and specifications. Higher skill levels operate CNC equipment, program, edit programs, and adjust machine controls and set-up work.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Reasonable Accommodations Statement

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable Accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Essential Functions Statement(s)

  • Read work orders on the Job Traveler & follows verbal instructions to determine work instructions & inspection requirements, including materials to be used, dimensions and tolerances. Records time and job information according to company procedures.
  • Read work orders on the Job Traveler & follows verbal instructions to perform basic assembly operations on components or sub-assemblies.
  • Operates various machines in secondary operations including insert press, punch press, straight liners, and hand grinders. Follows safety procedures and work instructions.
  • Monitors own work and records job/production data as instructed. Performs work in accordance with quality & safety expectations.
  • Position, lift, align, and secure work pieces against fixtures or stops on machine beds or on dies.
  • Removes burrs and sharp edges, using portable grinders and Debur hand tools.
  • Measure completed work pieces to verify conformance to specifications, using micrometers, gauges, calipers, templates, or rulers.
  • Examine completed work pieces for defects such as chipped edges and marred surfaces, and sort defective pieces according to types of flaws.
  • Independently handle, lift, move new raw materials, tools, and fixtures in accordance with the physical requirements as stated in this job description.
  • Keeps work area & equipment clean. Follows department procedures for care of equipment.
  • Attends work consistently and is punctual, meeting Company's attendance policy.
  • Level 1 - Entry Level, Operate Only. Performs or operates machine to produce required quantities of parts within specified tolerance limits. Monitors machine performance or works using hand tools. Monitors part quality continuously, reporting problems to Supervisor. Employee works under general supervision. Possess the ability to perform the job tasks to meet expectations on hire, or within the 1st year of employment.
  • Level 2 - Set Up and Operate, established repeat parts. Possess the skills of a Level 1 operator and in addition can set up and operate a variety of machines including CNC Machines, to produce a higher difficulty of part than what would be expected of an entry level worker. Can verify alignment using measurement instruments and can consistently produce repeat parts accurately. Generally requires trade school (or equivalent work experience) combined with some previous on-the-job experience.
  • Level 3 - Set Up and Operate new first run parts. Possess the skills of a Level 1 & 2 however are able to set-up to run first time new parts of a higher complexity level. With respect to CNC equipment, has the ability to enter control panel settings and/or program. Has the ability to work with minimal supervision. Possess problem solving skills and can assist with training new personnel. Generally requires trade school (or equivalent work experience) and significant work experience in fabrication.
  • Level 4 - Set Up, Operate & Resource person. Possess skills of Level 1, 2, 3, and in addition performs the most critical machine duties to produce parts, fixtures and basic tooling. Operates efficiently and expertly most machines in the department. Can produce complex parts from exotic materials and or complex designs. Serves as the go-to person, providing resource and training for others. Has trouble shooting abilities and can solve complex problems; works without Supervision.
  • Level 5 - Set Up, Operate, Resource and Management Decision Making skills. Possess all lower level skill sets and in addition business acumen skills. Has the ability to globally manage department work flow, supervise and mentor others. Requires trade school (or equivalent work experience) and generally five or more years of related industry work experience.

title: Tool Coordinator
description:
Job Title: Tool Coordinator

Company: Loenbro, LLC
Business Unit/Department: Procurement
Location: Centennial / On-site
Reports to: Regional Tool Manager
Employment Type: Full-Time
FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt

About Loenbro

Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.

At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.

Job Summary
The Tool Coordinator is responsible for the overall management, organization, and tracking of tools and related supplies. Responsibilities include maintenance of tools, maintaining an efficient system for tooling, assisting with tooling preparations for upcoming jobs, optimizing costs for purchasing, and helping with calibration duties.

Essential Job Responsibilities

  • Manage the check-in/check-out process for tools using barcode systems or inventory software to maintain accountability.
  • Inspect returned tools for damage, wear, or safety hazards; tag and remove defective equipment from service immediately to meet OSHA safety standards.
  • Coordinate the logistics for the transfer, delivery, and return of tools to and from job sites.
  • Ensure the tool crib/room is a safe environment in line with health, safety, and environmental requirements.
  • Working with Regional Tool Manager on purchases of tools and accessories including end mills, inserts, drills, tool holders, collets, lubricants, oils, etc.
  • Working with Regional Tool Manager on purchases of supplies for production departments from basic department supplies, tools, equipment, fixtures, and materials as appropriate.
  • Manage inventory and allocation of consumable tools, equipment, fixtures, etc.
  • Prepare job boxes for upcoming orders.
  • Research quotes for the more expensive purchases that need approval.
  • Perform routine preventative maintenance on tools and ensure specialized electrical test equipment (such as multimeters and megohmmeters) is properly calibrated and certified for use.
  • Help coordinate outside service technicians for tool maintenance and repairs as needed.
  • Keep tools clean and organized; maintain a logical storage system.
  • Ensure proper value and pricing is obtained on purchases.
  • Maintain records and provide reports on purchases, costs, and expenditures.
  • Properly maintain receipts, invoices, and documentation in an organized manner for accounting.
  • Assist with the calibration of basic measuring tools.
  • Help keep the shop or warehouse clean and organized.
  • Help clean and deburr parts as needed.

Other duties may be assigned as needed to support business operations.

Minimum Qualifications

Required

  • High degree of integrity and honesty.
  • Time management to stay ahead of department needs and schedule.
  • Proficiency in tool management, database software, Microsoft Excel, or ERP systems like SAP for accurate data entry and communication.
  • Meticulous record keeping to prevent loss and ensure compliance with safety and quality standards.
  • High school diploma or GED is standard; additional vocational training in electrical trades or inventory management is preferred.
  • A valid driver's license is required for site deliveries; forklift certification may be necessary.
  • Ability to inspect, measure, and evaluate tools for wear.
  • Ability to repair certain tools if appropriate.
  • Ability to sharpen bits and tools is a plus.
  • Basic Math skills.
  • Work with Regional Tool Manager and assist other staff with duties as assigned.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Work Environment:

title: ICWA Partnership Coordinator and Facilitator
description:
The Technical Assistance Manager II (TAM II) serves as the primary coordinator for all logistics, event planning, and peer participant engagement activities within the Title IV-B ICWA Technical Assistance Collaborative. This position is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing virtual, hybrid, and in-person meetings, trainings, convenings, and technical assistance events that support Tribal, State, and Court child welfare partners.

Serving as the sole logistics coordinator for the Collaborative, the position ensures seamless planning and implementation of all project events, manages communications and participant support, coordinates event resources, and oversees meeting technology and logistics systems. In addition, this role serves as the lead facilitator for on-site events. Additionally, in partnership with the National Tribal Child Welfare Center for Innovation and Advancement (NTCWCIA) and the Center for Legal and Judicial Innovation and Advancement (CLJIA) hosts the Title IV-B ICWA Tribal, State, and Court Peer Networking Group, fostering meaningful peer learning, collaboration, and information exchange.

The position works closely with federal partners, Tribal representatives, State agencies, judicial partners, subject matter experts, consultants, and project leadership to ensure Collaborative events and peer networking activities are culturally responsive, participant-centered, and aligned with the goals and requirements of Title IV-B Indian Child Welfare Act (ICWA) implementation efforts. The position also supports the Collaborative through the development and distribution of meeting agendas, meeting summaries, and project communications.

In this role, the ICWA Partnership and Implementation Logistics Coordinator and Event Facilitator will be expected to:

  • Build and maintain collaborative relationships with Tribal, State/County, and court partners participating in the ICWA initiative.

  • Demonstrate exceptional planning, organization, and execution of complex events and meetings while maintaining attention to detail and participant experience.

  • Create engaging learning environments and successfully facilitate productive discussions among Tribal, State, Court, Federal, and community partners.

  • Assist jurisdictions in translating ICWA requirements into day-to-day practice through policy review, workflow development, implementation planning, and problem-solving.

  • Collaborate with Children’s Bureau (CB) partners and CB funded technical assistance providers to support coordinated cross-center technical assistance.

  • Approach all work with cultural humility, respect for Tribal sovereignty, and an understanding of the unique needs of Tribal communities and partners.

  • Respond effectively to changing priorities, resolve logistical challenges, and identify practical solutions under tight timelines.

  • Provide content input on reports, presentations, implementation plans, and technical assistance products.

  • Communicate clearly, professionally, and effectively across multiple formats and audiences.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

Event Planning and Logistics Coordination:

  • Serve as the sole logistics coordinator for all Title IV-B ICWA Technical Assistance Collaborative meetings, trainings, peer networking activities, and special events.

  • Plan, coordinate, and manage all event logistics for virtual, hybrid, and in-person activities.

  • Coordinate venue selection, registration systems, travel arrangements, meeting materials, audiovisual requirements, and event communications.

  • Develop and maintain event timelines, planning documents, and project tracking systems to ensure successful implementation.

  • Draft, coordinate, and distribute meeting agendas, participant materials, and event communications in collaboration with project leadership and partners.

  • Prepare and distribute meeting summaries, action-item tracking documents, and follow-up communications for Collaborative meetings and events.

  • Manage participant registration, attendance tracking, communications, and follow-up activities.

  • Coordinate with vendors, consultants, partners, and project staff to ensure seamless event execution.

  • Troubleshoot logistical and technology issues before and during events.

  • Maintain event documentation and reporting systems in accordance with project and contractual requirements.

Event Facilitation and Peer Network Leadership:

  • Facilitate in-person, virtual, and hybrid Collaborative meetings, learning sessions, and convenings.

  • Serve, in partnership with NTCWCIA, and CLJIA as host for the Title IV-B ICWA Tribal, State, and Court Peer Networking Group.

  • Develop agendas and facilitate discussions that support peer learning and information sharing related to Title IV-B ICWA planning, implementation, and program requirements.

  • Create welcoming, culturally responsive environments that encourage participation, relationship building, and cross-system collaboration.

  • Coordinate presentations, panels, and facilitated discussions with subject matter experts and project leadership.

  • Support the exchange of promising practices, lessons learned, and implementation strategies among Tribal, State, and Court partners.

  • Manage ongoing membership communications and engagement activities for the Peer Networking Group.

  • Facilitate feedback collection, surveys, and assessments to support continuous improvement.

Communications and Community Engagement:

  • Serve as a primary point of contact for event participants, peer network members, consultants, and project partners.

  • Develop and distribute event announcements, newsletters, resource materials, and participant communications.

  • Coordinate information sharing among Tribal, State, and Court partners and facilitate connections across jurisdictions.

  • Build and maintain positive working relationships with federal partners, Tribal representatives, courts, state agencies, consultants, and community partners.

Project Support and Continuous Improvement:

  • Collect, organize, and maintain event and participant data for reporting and evaluation purposes.

  • Support project reporting, meeting summaries, and data collection activities.

  • Identify opportunities to improve event management processes, participant experience, and peer networking engagement.

  • Support the preparation and organization of facilitation materials, meeting resources, participants packets, and project communications.

  • Maintain adherence to project policies, standard operating procedures, and quality standards.

Minimum Job Qualifications:

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in social work, Human Services, Public Administration, Native American Studies, Education, Communications, Event Management, or a related field.

Experience:

  • At least 5 years of relevant work experience.
  • Demonstrated expertise in coordinating and facilitating meetings, conferences, trainings, technical assistance activities, or large-scale events.
  • Experience working with Tribal Nations, Tribal and State Child Welfare Programs, courts, or human services programs preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience managing multiple complex projects and timelines simultaneously.

Skills:

  • Interact well with others in a positive, courteous, and professional manner; functions well as a member of a team and is also able to work independently and without extensive supervision and follows chain of command to address personnel or management concerns.
  • Understands cultural differences, including being tribally informed.
  • Effective, clear, and professional writing and oral communication skills.
  • Attention to detail.

Language:

  • English Fluency (oral and written)

SECURITY CLEARANCE:

  • Must be able to obtain a Public Trust clearance.

Location:

  • This position is remote eligible. Candidates who live within 50 miles of our North Bethesda, MD or San Mateo, CA offices will be expected to work in a hybrid capacity.

Travel:

  • Travel is 10%-20% of time.

  • Must have the ability to travel independently and support event setup and coordination activities.

Physical Requirements:

  • Extended Computer Use: Ability to sit for extended periods and operate a computer keyboard and mouse
  • Vision: Must be able to see and read computer screens and printed materials.
  • Dexterity: Capable of using hands and fingers to operate equipment and perform tasks requiring precision.
  • Communication: Able to effectively communicate verbally and in writing with team members and partners.
  • Mobility: Frequently required to stand, walk, reach, and bend to access office equipment and attend meetings
  • Lifting: Ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds for short distances
  • Sensory Abilities: Must be able to perceive and interact with the environment using hearing and speaking skills
  • Work Environment: Primarily works in a typical office environment, with exposure to computer screens and moderate noise levels

Preferred job requirements:

Education:

  • Master's degree in a related field.

Experience:

  • Experience supporting implementation of ICWA, Tribal child welfare, Title IV-B, Title IV-E, or related federal child welfare programs.

  • Experience facilitating peer learning networks, communities of practice, or collaborative workgroups.

  • Experience planning conferences, tribal convenings, or national-level meetings.

  • Familiarity with data collection, survey tools, and reporting systems.

Language:

  • Fluency in a language other than English.

Knowledge:

  • Content Knowledge of current and emerging issues for assigned grant program areas
  • Strengths-based approach to delivering T/TA and to working with others
  • Knowledge of federal grants, cooperative agreements, or contract-supported technical assistance initiatives.

Software Proficiency:

Microsoft Office (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint), Zoom, Monday.com

OTHER DUTIES AS ASSIGNED: This position description should not be construed to imply that these requirements are the exclusive standards of the position, nor will it be the sole basis for any subsequent employee evaluations. Incumbents will follow any other instructions and perform any other related duties as may be required by their supervisor.

This position is subject to availability of funds and to any and all restrictions contained in the contract or contracts that provide funding for this position.

title: Senior Scientist I, Cancer Immunology
description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

As a key player in our Cancer Immunology team, you will use your immuno-oncology expertise to help advance Revolution Medicines’ assets in preclinical and clinical development.

Responsibilities:

  • Design, develop, validate and execute in vitro, in vivo, and ex vivo studies to address key translational questions and support immuno-oncology biomarker plans.

  • Identify, evaluate and implement emerging technologies to enhance translational biomarker discovery and mechanistic understanding.

  • Drive reverse translation efforts by formulating and testing hypotheses derived from clinical finding as appropriate to inform clinical development plans.

  • Stay abreast of advances in tumor immunology and immunotherapy, identifying novel combination strategies and contributing to preclinical evaluation.

  • Analyze, interpret, and communicate complex data effectively across internal cross-functional teams and at external scientific meetings.

  • Represent Revolution Medicines at scientific conferences and other external engagements.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

  • D. in immunology, cancer biology, or a related discipline, with deep expertise in tumor immunology, immuno-oncology biomarkers, and/or immunotherapy.

  • Proven track record of research excellence, evidenced by high-impact publications.

  • Expertise in in vivo model design to evaluate the efficacy and mechanisms of action of therapeutic agents and enable biomarker discovery, both internally and via contract research organizations.

  • Strong technical expertise in immunology techniques including multi-parameter flow cytometric analyses, primary human cellular/tissue-based functional assays, cell biology and molecular biology to guide/inform mechanism of action and biomarker discovery.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to independently oversee scientific projects, rigorously analyze and interpret scientific data while maintaining attention to detail.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative, interdisciplinary team setting.

  • 4+ years of relevant biotech or pharmaceutical industry experience in oncology drug discovery and development.

Preferred Skills:

  • Hands-on experience with humanized mouse models is desirable.

  • Familiarity with multiomics analyses and integrating computational insights into experimental designs.

title: Integration & Data Platform Engineer, Senior Analyst
description:
Crown Agents Bank is a vastly growing and regulated UK bank that connects emerging and frontier markets to the rest of the world, using FX and payments technology. We are transforming the way payments and FX move through emerging markets, reducing friction so that more money gets to those who need it. Emerging markets payments are usually challenging, expensive, unreliable and opaque. Our solutions help fix these pain points. Ultimately, we connect traditionally hard-to-reach regions to global financial infrastructure, giving access to the best prices and the fastest, most reliable settlement.

FX and cross-border payments are often complex and expensive, especially when operating in emerging markets. Crown Agents Bank (CAB) wraps its deep and trusted relationships and strength of network around innovative digital capabilities, and cross-border transaction banking solutions to enable fintech, corporates, governments, development organisations and banks to move money to, from, and across often hard-to-reach markets.

Job Description

Role Purpose

Crown Agents Bank connects emerging and frontier markets to the rest of the world, and that depends on software that can reliably integrate CAB's own systems with a wide range of third‑party platforms and internal data consumers. This role exists to help build and maintain the integration solutions and cloud‑native platforms that make that possible – which may include work on the team's Operational Data Store (built on Debezium, Java, Spring Boot and Aurora Serverless v2) as one part of a broader integration engineering remit, depending on project needs. Working under the guidance of the Associate Vice President and the Data and Integration Services Lead, the Senior Analyst works hands‑on, turning agreed designs into working, well‑tested software, and contributing ideas and perspective to the design discussions that shape them. Engineers are expected and encouraged to utilise the latest in AI tooling in their delivery and champion it’s use in our platforms.

Role Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain integration solutions and cloud‑native components across CAB's technology estate – for example the team's Operational Data Store depending on where project priorities lie.
  • Develop integrations with third‑party systems and internal platforms using AWS services such as ECS Fargate, SQS, MSK, S3, IAM, etc., working from designs agreed with the AVP and Lead and contributing improvements along the way.
  • Write production‑quality code and tests, owning delivery of assigned features and integration components from design handover through to release.
  • Contribute practical input and ideas to design discussions, questioning assumptions and flagging risks or alternatives.
  • Build and maintain infrastructure as code using Terraform, and CI/CD pipelines using Git and GitHub Actions, for the services and integrations you own.
  • Support observability and data quality monitoring using Dynatrace, investigating and helping resolve issues as they arise.
  • Use AI coding assistants and LLM‑assisted development practices as a routine part of day‑to‑day delivery, and share useful tools or techniques with the team.
  • Work with stakeholders across Technology and Operations to understand requirements and translate them into working software, escalating ambiguity or risk to the AVP or Lead rather than guessing.
  • Take part in code reviews and design reviews, giving and receiving feedback that raises the quality of the team's work.

Experience

  • Interest in, or early experience using, AI coding assistants and LLM‑assisted development as part of the software development lifecycle; relevant AWS or Anthropic certifications are a plus.

title: Ultrasound Technologist - ACS - Obstetrics and Gynecology
description:
Overview

About the Role

The primary purpose of the Ultrasound Technologist is to provide health care services for patients of the University Hospital/ACC through the applications of non-ionizing radiation (in the form of ultrasound). The technologist performs ultrasound procedures for the interpretation of a licensed practitioner. The patient population ranges from newborn to maturity. Exercises professional judgment throughout the performance of his/her duties and maintains a demeanor that supports the values and mission of the department, ensuring that all interaction with patients, physicians, nurses, administrators, and other members of the hospital staff are professional and in accordance with the established guidelines of the institution.

Responsibilities

What You’ll Do

  • Positions patient in accordance with established protocols or approved physician instructions, employing immobilization devices, as reviewed in random critiques of images by radiologist or QC Technologist.
  • Determines proper and satisfactory ultrasound technique – appropriate probes 98% of the time, as reviewed in random critiques of images by radiologist or QC Technologist.
  • Verified informed consent where required 100% of the time, as indicated by retrospective reviews of consent form presence in the chart for specific special procedures – biopsy exams.
  • Contributes to the achievement of excellence in the department through the adherence to productivity, quality assurance ,customer service, and code of conduct standards established by the department or organization.
  • The technologist will ensure 100% of the time that all procedures performed by him/her are “completed” in the RIS system and “verified” in PACS after the study is complete and finalized. No more than 3 un – “completed” studies will be allowed in any 12-month period, as verified by review of RIS management reports.
  • With conditions permitting as defined by the lead tech, each technologist is expected to perform and complete and average of 10 routine exams over the course of an eight-hour shift 100% of the time, as verified by RIS management reports.

Qualifications

What You’ll Bring

Required:

  • Must be a graduate of an approved Ultrasound Program.
  • ARDMS certification required, and current active registration required.
  • Annual fit testing required.
  • Must maintain valid certification by the American Heart Association in Basic Life Support (BLS)/CPR

What We Offer

  • Dental & Vision Insurance
  • Health Savings Account (HSA) & Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
  • Short- & Long-Term Disability Insurance

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Compensation

In compliance with New Jersey’s Pay Transparency Act, the salary range for this position is TT/9999 - 56.04 per hour. University Hospital considers multiple factors when determining compensation, including (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate’s relevant work experience, education and training, key skills, internal equity, market data, and organizational needs. The expected salary range for this position is in accordance with the New Jersey Pay Transparency Law; final compensation will be commensurate with experience and qualifications.

About Us

University Hospital is one of the nation’s leading academic medical centers. As the principal teaching affiliate of Rutgers New Jersey Medical School and the only state-certified Level 1 Trauma Center in Northern New Jersey, University Hospital is training the next generation of physicians and advancing science to discovery while taking exceptional care of patients, regardless of their financial situation.

Apply Today

title: Overlæge til Almenpsykiatrisk Ambulatorium Frederikshavn
description:
Om jobbet:

Ved Almenpsykiatrisk Afdeling, Nord, Region Nordjylland er der en stilling ledig som overenskomstansat overlæge i psykiatri ved Almenpsykiatrisk Ambulatorium, Frederikshavn til besættelse 1. januar 2027.

Ambulatoriet varetager den almenpsykiatriske behandling af patienter fra Frederikshavn og Læsø kommune. Stilling vil være tilknyttet vores F-ACT-team, psykoseområdet.

Almenpsykiatrisk Ambulatorium i Frederikshavn er et decentralt ambulatorium, hvor de primære opgaver er udredning og behandling af mennesker indenfor hele det psykiatriske spektrum med mulighed for at viderehenvise til specialiserede tilbud på hoved- og regionsfunktionsniveau. Der er differentieret behandling i forhold til diagnose og sværhedsgrad, hvor der tages udgangspunkt i behandlingselementer beskrevet i pakkeforløb.

Behandlingen består af psykoterapi, både gruppe og individuelt, farmakologisk behandling, støttende indsigtsgivende samtaler samt psykoedukation. Der er tradition for gruppebehandling, hvor patienterne kan tilbydes kognitiv depressionsgruppe, psykodynamisk gruppe, recoverygruppe for patienter med psykose, stemmehøregruppe, dobbeltdiagnosegruppe, ADHD-gruppe samt PTSD-gruppe.

Personalsammensætningen i ambulatoriet består af en overlæge, en speciallæge, en specialpsykolog, seks psykologer, 11 sygeplejersker, en socialrådgiver samt to sekretærer. Vi har 18 timer ugentligt ansat en medarbejder med brugerbaggrund i F-ACT.

Ambulatoriet har uddannelsessøgende læger indenfor såvel psykiatri som almen medicin samt sygeplejestuderende, paramedicinerstuderende og psykologstuderende. Ift. uddannelsessøgende læger ligger der en væsentlig uddannelsesmæssig opgave knyttet til stillingen. Speciallægerne deltager i Klinik Nords mødeaktiviteter og fælles undervisning for Almenpsykiatrisk afdeling Nord og Syd og evt. forskning.

Der er bagvagtsfunktion knyttet til stillingen. Bagvagten har i hverdage tilstedeværelse i almindelig arbejdstid og i weekender fra kl. 08-14, hvorefter vagten varetages fra hjemmet med fremmøde ved behov.

Funktionsbeskrivelse Frederikshavn

Om dig:

Vi søger en speciallæge i psykiatri:

  • Med en imødekommende væremåde, som indbyder til et ligeværdigt patientsamarbejde i rammen af ”patientens team”

  • Som arbejder målrettet og struktureret med planlægning og dokumentation efter retningslinjer

  • Som bidrager til et udviklende fagligt – og kollegialt fællesskab samt et godt arbejdsmiljø

  • Som er engageret og motiveret for faglige refleksioner

  • Som har evnen til selvledelse og kan træffe selvstændige beslutninger i en hverdag med højt patient flow, skiftende politiske dagsordener og omskiftelige arbejdsvilkår

Vi tilbyder:

Personalet arbejder tværfagligt i to teams og har psykoterapeutiske uddannelser inden for kognitiv, psykodynamisk og mentaliserings baseret terapi.

Holdningsmæssigt vægter vi mødet med det enkelte menneske og patientinddragelse bl.a. via Patientens Team, hvor betydningsfulde samarbejdspartnere omkring patienten inddrages.

Der er bagvagtsfunktion knyttet til stillingen. Bagvagten har i hverdage tilstedeværelse i almindelig arbejdstid og i weekender fra kl. 08-14, hvorefter vagten varetages fra hjemmet med fremmøde ved behov.

Stillingen vil være en fuldtidsstilling, men med mulighed for deltid.

Forvagten er tilstedevagt/11 skiftet.

Bagvagten er 15 skiftet rul.

Løn og ansættelsesvilkår iht. overenskomst mellem Danske Regioner og Foreningen af Speciallæger/Foreningen af Yngre Læger alt afhængig af kvalifikationer.

Om os:

Vi har en holistisk tilgang. Det betyder, at vi ser patienten som et unikt menneske. Vi ser

Ikke kun en patient med symptomer og problemer, men ønsker at levendegøre patienten

ved at forstå og lære personen at kende. Vi lægger desuden stor vægt på at inddrage

pårørende.

Vi vægter det tværfaglige og tværsektorielle samarbejde i komplicerede patientforløb. Derfor har vi et tæt samarbejde med andre specialiserede afdelinger i Psykiatrien for at sikre, at vores patienter får den bedst mulige behandling.

Desuden er der et veludbygget tværsektorielt samarbejde med Frederikshavns Kommune, herunder Center for unge, støttecentre, kommunale sagsbehandlere, rusmiddelcenter med flere.

Du kan læse mere om Almenpsykiatrisk Afdeling, Nord på hjemmesiden

Ønsker du yderligere information om stillingen eller om muligheden for et fokuseret besøg, er du velkommen til at kontakte, cheflæge, Anders Meinert Pedersen, tlf. 20362627, mail a.meinert@rn.dk

eller ledende oversygeplejerske, Kathe Kjær Lyng 97644000/29243296.

Det praktiske:

Du kan læse mere om Almenpsykiatrisk Afdeling, Nord på hjemmesiden Psykiatri i Region Nordjylland (rn.dk)

Du sender din ansøgning ved at trykke på ”Søg Job” knappen og udfylde den formular, som kommer frem. Du kan vedhæfte ansøgning, CV og eventuelle bilag. Vi modtager udelukkende ansøgninger via linket i stillingsopslaget. Ansøgninger sendt på mail, vil ikke blive behandlet.

Regionsrådet har vedtaget, at man før ansættelse på Aalborg Universitetshospital skal give tilladelse til indhentning af straffeattest.

  • Vi indhenter referencer på den person, vi ønsker at ansætte. Er det påkrævet for stillingen, indhenter vi også straffeattest og børneattest

  • Løn og ansættelsesvilkår efter gældende overenskomst

  • Stillingen er som udgangspunkt på 37 timer pr. uge, men hvis et andet timetal ønskes, kan det aftales

  • Uddannelse af studerende og elever er en af Psykiatriens kerneopgaver, som alle medarbejdere bidrager til

  • I Region Nordjylland har vi røgfri arbejdstid.

  • Løn- og ansættelsesvilkår efter gældende overenskomst.

    Ansættelse: 1. januar 2027 eller efter aftale.

    Ansøgningsfrist: 22. oktober 2026.

title: Activity Therapist - Full Time
description:
Position Type: Full Time

Schedule and Hours: Monday-Friday 8 AM – 4:30 PM
Location: Long Beach, CA

Benefits

Physical & Environmental Requirements

  • Ability to sit or stand for extended periods of time.
  • Must be able to operate standard office and/or clinical equipment requiring repetitive hand movements, manual dexterity, and fine finger coordination, including the use of computers, telephones, and related devices.

Special Conditions

  • Employment is contingent upon successful completion of Live Scan fingerprinting, background check clearance, and verification of required licenses, certifications, and education

POSITION SUMMARY

The Resident Services Coordinator I (RSC I) is the frontline anchor of EHRSI's revitalization strategy, delivering tiered service bundles (universal, targeted, intensive) to residents at single or multiple assigned properties. The RSC I provides first level support across all service domains—housing stability, economic mobility, health & wellness, digital inclusion, and youth/family engagement—using trauma-informed, coaching-based practice to advance resident stability, mobility, and wellbeing outcomes.

Working under supervision of the RSM, the RSC I delivers Tier 1 universal programs directly (workshops, wellness checks, community events), provides coaching-based first level support to residents across domains, and facilitates warm handoffs to partner-delivered specialists when intensive or specialized services are needed. The role ensures accurate documentation in EHRSI's CRM (Salesforce), embeds equity and resident voice into daily practice, and contributes to EHRSI's partnership-enabled, cost-neutral service delivery model.

Impact: The ability to effectively coordinate first level support and facilitate appropriate specialist referrals directly impacts EHRSI's mission by allowing residents to maintain housing stability for longer periods, enhancing quality of life, and advancing equity and opportunity for all.

Role Parameters

Caseload Ratio: Approximately 25-60 active resident relationships at across assigned properties (aligned to 1:150 family, 1:125 senior, 1:100 PSH ratios)

Deployment: Site-based; assigned to one property (family, senior, or supportive housing)

Location: Varied property locations across EHRSI portfolio

Transition Note: In 2026, RSC I roles operate within existing staffing, focusing on tiered bundle delivery and accurate outcome tracking. From 2027 onward, RSC I becomes part of a regional operations structure supported by Partner-Delivered Specialists (Youth, Health, Financial Coaching) and central functions (Training & QA, Outcomes & Analytics, Resident Voice, Partnership Development).

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Service Delivery & First Level Support (Across Domains)

Deliver Tier 1 Universal Programs directly:

  • Facilitate community-building activities: workshops, wellness checks, social clubs, community events
  • Coordinate afterschool programs, youth activities, and parent engagement workshops
  • Provide technology access support, digital literacy training, and basic troubleshooting
  • Deliver financial literacy workshops and employment readiness activities
  • Organize health fairs, food distribution, and preventive wellness initiatives

Provide coaching-based first level support across all service domains:

  • Housing Stability: Support lease compliance conversations, mediate with property management, connect residents to emergency rental assistance, and provide housing transition guidance
  • Economic Stability: Facilitate basic budgeting conversations, support job applications, assist with benefits enrollment (CalFresh, SNAP, Medi-Cal), and connect residents to employment resources
  • Health & Wellness: Help residents enroll in health insurance, schedule appointments, provide medication adherence reminders, conduct wellness checks, and identify when clinical intervention is needed
  • Digital Inclusion: Troubleshoot basic technology issues (WiFi, email, passwords), teach digital literacy skills, connect residents to internet subsidy programs (ACP, Lifeline), and provide homework help
  • Youth & Family: Deliver after-school programs, facilitate parent workshops, connect families to school resources, and identify developmental or behavioral concerns requiring specialist support

Recognize when first level support is insufficient and initiate referrals to partner-delivered specialists under supervision (legal aid, clinical health navigation, behavioral health counseling, intensive employment services, specialized youth programming). When other service organizations are not available, may deliver direct services within scope of practice and under supervision.

2. Crisis Response, Safeguarding & Conflict Resolution

  • Respond to resident crises and urgent situations using trauma-informed de-escalation techniques
  • Report child, dependent adult, and elder abuse and neglect according to California State law as a mandated reporter
  • Work with property staff, families, and community agencies to identify and address resident problems before they reach crisis proportions
  • Follow established escalation protocols, involving Supervisor immediately for high-acuity, complex cases, or concerns about resident or child wellbeing
  • Mediate conflicts between residents or between residents and property management
  • Document crisis incidents accurately in CRM within 24 hours and participate in post-incident debriefs
  • Maintain safety protocols and professional boundaries during high-stress situations

3. Community Resource Navigation & Partnership Coordination

  • Build and maintain relationships with local service providers and community partners
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of local resource directories and eligibility requirements
  • Obtain appropriate releases to interact with others on behalf of residents; maintain confidentiality appropriately
  • Execute warm handoff protocols under supervision: assess resident needs, make quality referrals, introduce residents to partner staff
  • Conduct follow-up with residents after referrals to ensure service connection and satisfaction
  • Support residents with application processes, paperwork assistance, and eligibility screening for community programs
  • Participate in partnership coordination meetings as directed by Supervisor
  • Develop and maintain a comprehensive list of available community resources (employment, education, social service agencies, etc.) for residents

4. Trauma-Informed Care & Resident Relationship Building

  • Build trust-based relationships with residents through consistent presence, active listening, and non-judgmental support
  • Apply trauma-informed, strengths-based approaches in all resident interactions
  • Use motivational interviewing basics to help residents identify goals and overcome barriers
  • Support resident self-efficacy: provide information and options rather than making decisions for residents
  • Maintain confidentiality and professional boundaries at all times
  • Recognize signs of trauma, mental health concerns, or crisis and respond appropriately with supervisor guidance
  • Integrate resident voice into program adjustments and service planning discussions

5. Data, Outcomes & Accountability

  • Accurately document all resident interactions, referrals, service delivery, and outcomes in EHRSI's CRM (Salesforce) within 48 hours
  • Track attendance, participation rates, and service utilization for all programs
  • Submit reports in an accurate and timely manner
  • Maintain all reporting requirements set by funding and/or governmental agencies
  • Monitor progress toward resident outcome KPIs: housing stability, economic mobility, health & wellness, digital inclusion
  • Support equity analysis by ensuring demographic data is accurately captured and disaggregated
  • Maintain program files and records with required completeness (equal or greater than 95%)

6. Property Management Collaboration & Site Team Integration

  • Serve as an active member of the site team, working collaboratively with property manager and other site staff to meet property needs and resolve resident problems
  • Assist residents and property operations staff in understanding resident needs
  • Work with residents to resolve conflicts with neighbors
  • Coordinate recreational, cultural, and social activities in coordination with property operations staff and residents, as needed
  • Attend all staff meetings, training sessions, and other appropriate meetings and conferences as required

7. Team Collaboration & Organizational Learning

  • Participate actively in reflective practice sessions, peer learning, and case consultations
  • Share relevant resident updates and service information with colleagues
  • Contribute insights from frontline delivery to inform continuous improvement and program refinement
  • Participate in relevant local, regional, state and/or national organizations as assigned
  • Actively participate in EHRSI's culture of inclusivity

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

None directly; may coordinate volunteers for specific events

title: Complaints and PSEA Advisor
description:
Location: home-based; ideally South Africa or another location in similar time-zone
Duration of contract: 1 year (possibility for extension)
Supervisor: Global Coordinator for PMER, Complaints and Safeguarding

Start date: as soon as possible

Lutheran World Federation (LWF) World Service
LWF World Service is the humanitarian and development arm of the Lutheran World Federation. We are a widely recognized, international, faith-based organization working in more than 20 countries globally. We seek to bring people of all backgrounds together in the common quest for justice, peace, and reconciliation in an increasingly complex and fragmented world. A commitment to the human rights of every individual, regardless of their status, guides our work, actions, and operations. We are particularly known for our timely, compassionate, and professional humanitarian work, and for our field presence in hard-to-reach areas. Our work is people-centered and community-based. Above all, we work with the most vulnerable, and to claim and uphold their rights, we engage proactively with local government and community structures. For additional information, please see LWF World Service.

Purpose
Complaints and PSEA Advisor supports the Global Coordinator PMER, Complaints and Safeguarding in the implementation and strengthening of complaints handling and PSEA systems across LWF World Service.

The position provides operational and technical support in complaint intake and case management, investigations, CRM monitoring and reporting, PSEA, capacity strengthening, and digital and knowledge management. The position requires a high level of confidentiality, sound judgment and the ability to work independently while knowing when matters need to be escalated to the Global Coordinator.

The Advisor works closely with CRM and PSEA Focal Points in LWF Country Programs to support consistent implementation of LWF policies, systems and requirements across the Country Programs. The position also works with relevant Geneva-based functions, when required.

Required qualifications
University degree in a relevant field such as social sciences, law, human rights, international development or another related field.
Recognized training or certification in investigations.

Knowledge and experience
At least 3 years of relevant professional experience in complaints handling, investigations, PSEA, safeguarding or related areas.
Practical experience in complaint intake, assessment, referral and case management.
Good knowledge of complaints handling, PSEA and safeguarding standards and practices in humanitarian and development contexts.
Experience conducting workplace or misconduct investigations, including interviews, evidence review and investigation reporting.
Experience providing training, coaching or technical support, preferably in humanitarian or development settings.
Experience working with digital information systems, databases or collaboration platforms.

Language skills
English required: fluent

French and/or Spanish are an asset

LWF Core Skills

Achieving results – advanced*

Accountability – resourced

Working effectively with others - advanced
Analytical thinking - advanced
Initiative - advanced

Leadership - resourced

LWF Functional Skills

Attention to detail - advanced

Capacity building / Training – advanced

Confidentiality Management – advanced
Analytical Thinking - resourced

Information Management – advanced

  • LWF 3 skills levels are: basic - advanced – resourced

Main duties
Complaints Handling and Investigations
Supports the day-to-day management of the LWF Complaint mailbox, including acknowledgment, initial assessment, referral, intake analysis, registration and follow-up of complaints.
Reviews and analyses complaints and recommends appropriate handling or escalation in line with LWF policies and procedures.
Maintains accurate and confidential case information in the complaints database and supports CRM Focal Points with complaint handling and documentation.
Conducts or supports investigations when assigned, including planning, interviews, evidence review and preparation of investigation reports.
Acts as the designated backup for the LWF Complaint mailbox during the absence of the Global Coordinator and ensures continuity of complaint handling.

CRM Monitoring, Systems and Implementation
Supports the monitoring of CRM implementation across Country Programs and follows up identified gaps with CRM Focal Points.
Coordinates the quarterly CRM reporting process, reviews the quality and completeness of submissions and follows up where information is missing or incomplete.
Supports the review and improvement of the CRM quarterly reporting tool and process.
Supports the rollout and consistent use of ActivityInfo for complaint recording and monitors the quality and completeness of information recorded by Country Programs.
Reviews CRM information and complaint data to identify recurring gaps, trends and areas requiring additional support.

PSEA
Supports the Global Coordinator with the review, update and rollout of the LWF World Service PSEA Policy.
Provides technical support to PSEA and CRM Focal Points on the implementation of PSEA requirements at Country Program level.
Supports and follows up PSEA self-assessments and UN PSEA assessments, including review of evidence, identification of gaps and follow-up of agreed actions.
Develops and delivers PSEA induction, training and refresher sessions and supports focal points in strengthening staff awareness.
Identifies recurring PSEA gaps and brings significant or systemic issues to the attention of the Global Coordinator.

Capacity Strengthening and Technical Support
Supports the induction and onboarding of new CRM Focal Points and provides ongoing coaching and technical support to CRM and PSEA Focal Points.
Develops and delivers practical training and refresher sessions on complaint handling and CRM based on identified needs.
Supports focal points in strengthening complaint mechanisms and related processes and facilitates learning and exchange between focal points when useful.

Digital Systems and Knowledge Management
Reviews and organizes existing CRM, complaints, investigation and PSEA resources, helping to reduce duplication, archive outdated materials and simplify the resources available to Country Programs.
Supports the development and maintenance of a structured SharePoint site where Country Programs can easily access current guidance, templates, training materials and other resources related to Complaint and PSEA.
Supports the effective use of ActivityInfo, SharePoint and other relevant digital systems and works with Data & Analytics and other colleagues when technical support is required.

Major Challenges
Handling sensitive and confidential information while managing several priorities at the same time.
Supporting more consistent implementation of CRM and PSEA requirements across different Country Program contexts.
Turning policies and technical requirements into practical and user-friendly approaches.
Managing multiple priorities, taking initiative and ensuring timely coordination on sensitive or complex matters.

title: Hardware Systems Integration Engineer (Robotics)
description:
The Company
We believe general-purpose, generally-intelligent robots will be built in our lifetimes. Robots will work in our factories, move our goods, walk on our streets and eventually be in our homes. To build that future, research and deployment must work in lockstep: real-world operation must make the technology better and better technology must make deployment easier. We're looking for the thinkers, builders, and researchers who want to be part of that loop.
As an AI robotics company that deploys its inventions directly into the facilities that need them, on state-of-the-art hardware, every line of code written at Tutor has a direct impact on the global, physical economy.
Our Culture
We believe that something truly special can happen when talented, motivated people work together; at Tutor, every member of our team is empowered to have real impact in everything that they do. We're characterized by both technical excellence and next-level collaboration and respect.
About the Role
Our robots are built from hardware we design and hardware we buy, and many of our suppliers are in China. We're looking for an engineer to evaluate that hardware, integrate it into our robots, and work directly with the suppliers who make it.
You will test new components, find where they fall short, and work with suppliers' engineers, in Mandarin, to get the changes we need. You will be based in Watertown and spend a large part of your time at supplier sites. As this work grows, there is room to hire and lead other engineers doing it.

What You'll Do

  • Evaluate new hardware: Test arms, actuators, sensors and other components from suppliers against what our robots need
  • Integrate and test: Bring new hardware up on our robots, find where it falls short, and see the problems through to a fix
  • Work with suppliers' engineers: Spend time at their sites, agree on changes, and keep the work moving between visits
  • Carry our requirements: Make sure the people building for us understand what we need and why
  • Build prototypes: Run small prototype builds and bring what you learn back to the design team
  • Travel: Spend roughly a third to half of your time in China

What We're Looking For

  • Experience developing hardware with suppliers or factories in China: You have taken a product from prototype toward production with them
  • Fluent Mandarin and English: You can hold a technical discussion and write a specification in both
  • Broad hands-on skill: You can debug a system that has mechanical, electrical and firmware parts, and you know when to bring in a specialist
  • Comfortable in a lab: You build test setups, take measurements, and write up what you found
  • Willing to travel: Long and frequent trips are part of the job

Nice to Have

  • Experience with robot arms, actuators or motor drives

  • Time spent living and working in China
About Our Roles & Titles
At Tutor, we believe great engineers and researchers are defined by what they build and the impact they have — not where they sit in an org chart or what title they have. Therefore, everyone in our R&D org holds the title Member of Technical Staff (MoTS). Our job postings use standard titles so you can find us, but if you join Tutor, you'll be a MoTS — with a level that is determined through the interview process.
That also means we hire people, not slots. Work at Tutor evolves every quarter, and we set the expectation of flexibility from day one — it's common for people to start on one thing and shift to another based on where the team needs them most. A high technical bar across the board is what makes that flexibility possible: it's what allows people to contribute meaningfully whatever problem they take on.
