title: Senior Data Platform Engineer
description:
Who we are

Neros is a defense technology company rebuilding America’s drone industrial base. We design and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are tested in combat, iterated at startup speed, and built at massive scale. Our team culture is fast, hands-on, and obsessed with closing the gap between design and deployment.

As drones transform the character of warfare, Neros is delivering the systems the West needs to compete on the modern battlefield and deter the adversaries of democracy. We’re hiring engineers, operators, and builders who want to move fast, take on extreme ownership, and get capability into the hands of warfighters in months, not years.

What you will be doing

The Data Platform Engineer owns the autonomy data pipeline end to end: recovering flight data from vehicles in the field, landing it in the cloud, and making it searchable and replayable at scale. This is a greenfield role. You will stand up the storage, catalog, and query infrastructure that every autonomy test, simulation run, and machine learning dataset at Neros depends on, and you will own its architecture, operating cost, and compliance posture.

Responsibilities

  • Build the path that brings flight data back from the field, including triggered capture on the vehicle, prioritized upload so the highest-value flights return first, and resumable transfer with integrity verification.
  • Turn raw logs into a usable corpus: decode, time-align multi-sensor and video streams, validate, and quarantine malformed data before it reaches downstream users.
  • Design the catalog and tag model that index the corpus, and stand up the cloud storage and database that hold it
  • Build the query layer so an engineer can retrieve every flight matching a condition, for example loss of target lock at terminal stage under high glare within the last 90 days, and get playable video back in seconds.
  • Serve logs to the evaluation harness with stable ordering, exact time alignment, and reproducible results across runs, so a regression job can run over thousands of flights at once.
  • Build versioned, immutable datasets from catalog queries, with lineage recorded so any model training set can be rebuilt exactly months later.

You should have the following

  • 5+ years building production data or backend infrastructure, including at least one system you owned end to end from initial design through ongoing operation
  • Direct experience with large-scale log or sensor data: multi-terabyte and growing, with video and multiple synchronized sensor streams (rosbag, MCAP, HDF5, Parquet, or equivalent formats), rather than row-oriented business data
  • Designed and owned a data schema, index, or catalog that other engineers queried daily, and lived with the consequences of that design, including at least one migration
  • Strong Python, plus SQL and working ownership of a relational database (PostgreSQL or equivalent) used in production
  • Practical experience with cloud object storage and compute (Azure, AWS, or GCP) and the ability to provision and operate it independently, without a dedicated platform or DevOps team
  • Experience with distributed or parallel batch processing and job orchestration (Spark, Ray, Dask, Airflow, Dagster, or equivalent) across large volumes of recorded dat
  • Working knowledge of time synchronization and alignment across sensor streams, and of deterministic, reproducible processing of recorded data
  • A track record of building internal tooling that other engineers adopted, including at least one case where you changed the design based on how it was actually being used

Nice to have

  • Log or data infrastructure built for robotics, autonomous vehicles, aerospace, or defense programs, where replay determinism, time alignment, and multi-sensor logs are native problems rather than new ones
  • Experience handling video at scale, including transcoding, frame-accurate seeking, and streaming playback of recorded footage to engineering users
  • Direct Azure experience, infrastructure defined as code (Terraform or Bicep), and prior responsibility for a cloud budget where storage tiering and egress costs mattered
  • Prior work in export-controlled, GovCloud, or IL4/IL5 environments, or familiarity with CMMC and ITAR data handling obligations
  • Experience connecting a data pipeline to a labeling vendor or internal labeling tooling, or to model training, experiment tracking, and model registry workflows

US Salary Range

$163,500 – $228,500 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are considered part of Neros' total compensation package.

title: Network and Computer Systems Administrator
description:
Innovative Technology Partnerships LLC (ITP) seeks an on-site Network and Computer Systems Administrator to support NAVAIR PMA-290 MOSS at the Integrated Test Facility (ITF), NAS Patuxent River, MD. The SA serves as the primary integration specialist maintaining, operating, and configuring mission-critical Ground Support Stations (GSSs) for the ITF and deployable squadrons. The position manages the full media lifecycle—baseline image ingestion, mirror drive duplication, post-cloning cryptographic verification (SHA-256), NIST SP 800-88 sanitization, and physical delivery of aircraft payloads.   • Duplication, Verification & Sanitization: Operate hardware duplicators (e.g., Logicube SuperSonix-NG), perform 100% SHA-256 hash verification, and execute NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 1 sanitization per ITF SOPs.
  • Field Deployment & Vendor Support: Act as technical liaison for software deliveries, support squadron detachments with site checkouts and training, and manage secure media chain-of-custody hand-offs.
  • Documentation & Lab Operations: Author PSOPs, work instructions, and checklists while maintaining lab turnaround benchmarks for save, restore, and tape archiving.

title: U.S Operations Intern
description:
About us:

Kiva is a global nonprofit, founded in 2005, with a mission to expand financial access and help underserved communities thrive. Kiva unlocks capital for borrowers through crowdfunded loans supported by individuals around the world. Lenders on Kiva can start with as little as $25 to support causes that matter most to them, whether that’s gender equity and support for women, refugees, climate change, small businesses, agriculture, and more. Since our founding, over two million people have invested over $2 billion in real dreams and real opportunity, spanning more than 100 countries and over 5 million borrowers.

As we work toward our mission, Kiva invests in building and retaining a global team of talent to add to our values-driven and digital-first culture. Our organization is supported by over 700 volunteers and 130+ full-time employees dispersed around the world, as well as within team hubs located in San Francisco, Nairobi, Bogota, and Bangkok. Kiva’s team is growing as we pursue exciting new opportunities to scale our impact and create a financially inclusive world.

Kiva's values:

Impact first - This is why we exist. This is the drumbeat we march to. Every day.

Extreme ownership - Own it; you, your relationships, your impact. Insist that others support you and hold you accountable.

Be curious and bold - Never stop learning. Question assumptions. Take Risks and dream big.

Inclusion. Equity. Diversity. - Without reservation and without caveat. In our hiring, in our workplace and in our impact in the world.

Honor and integrity - Do the most right thing in the most right way. Cherish diversity and respect each other.

Love and kindness always - Say what you mean. Mean what you say. And don't say it mean. Clarity. Courage. Kindness.

Internship Program

Since its founding, volunteerism has been an integral part of Kiva's foundation and success. As a Kiva Intern, you will contribute your passion, drive, ideas, and expertise to expanding our reach and impact while taking on immediate and significant responsibilities within your team. In addition to learning on the job, you'll partake in a variety of educational, social, and professional development workshops and events that will accelerate your professional growth while learning about Kiva and the non-profit, technology, and microfinance sectors.

Through this volunteer internship, we hope to provide a high-caliber learning experience. With the completion of our internship program, you will take away many in-demand job skills. Additionally, all Kiva interns will gain exposure to foundational microfinance concepts and ongoing professional development tailored to your career goals. This position will also put you in contact with a wide array of employees around the world, giving you a jump start on networking opportunities.

This Kiva internship is a 6-month, part-time (24 - 32 hours per week), United States-based, remote volunteer position.

Department overview:

Kiva U.S. is an innovative direct-to-borrower lending program. Launched in 2011, Kiva U.S. has experimented with different approaches to bring 0% capital to financially excluded entrepreneurs throughout the U.S.. With the mission to help underserved communities thrive, the Kiva U.S. program seeks to:

  • Expand access to capital to traditionally underestimated entrepreneurs including women, people of color, and the underbanked
  • Lower the cost of that capital (by offering 0% interest, no fee loans)
  • Enable borrowers and local technical assistance providers to connect more directly so that borrowers receive application support and plug into local resources

Your Role:

As a Kiva U.S. Operations Intern, you will work closely with our Operations team. The U.S. Operations team is responsible for all operations supporting the U.S. program— from the borrower application to credit underwriting to fundraising support to loan disbursal to risk assessment and repayment. We maintain the tools used by the U.S. team and our partners and strive to leverage them to meet our team’s needs as well as to better support both our borrowers and partners.

This intern will be responsible for driving forward the way we support entrepreneurs during the loan origination process (from the moment they start an application for a Kiva loan until they complete their fundraising campaign on ) and manage delinquency of our borrowers.

This role calls for the intern to gain a deep understanding of the entire borrower experience, take part in the review process of loan applications, and own process improvements to our system. The intern will also assist in analysis and project-based work (in areas including but not limited to: communications, data analysis, product, partner success, strategic partnerships, impact) help us continue to develop the U.S. program and drive greater impact for small business entrepreneurs in the U.S.

At this time, we can only consider applicants with authorization to work in the United States on a permanent, full-time basis; unfortunately we cannot provide visa sponsorship.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Screening and approving loan applications alongside our review team.
  • Supporting borrowers via text and phone calls throughout their fundraising campaign.
  • Managing delinquency of borrowers and establishing action plans to work with borrowers to get them back on track.
  • Piloting process and infrastructure improvements to our operations.
  • Collaborating with our U.S. Partnerships colleagues to improve the Kiva U.S. partner experience.
  • Taking on additional special cross-functional projects aimed at increasing the value entrepreneurs receive from Kiva.
  • Collecting, synthesizing, and implementing internal and external changes based on feedback from Kiva U.S. loan applicants, borrowers, and partners alike.
  • Sourcing Kiva U.S. borrower stories and supporting cross-functional Kiva U.S. impact storytelling initiatives.
  • Improving training materials and resources for Capital Access Managers

Preferred qualifications:

  • At least 21 years of age or older by January 12, 2027
  • Able to commit to the full 6-month term
  • Strong critical thinking, with an eye for detail and ownership of your work
  • Enjoys problem-solving and relationship-building
  • Strong written and verbal communication
  • Highly proactive and able to work independently
  • Highly organized individual with an aptitude for working in a start-up environment.
  • Intermediate skills in Google Docs, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint

What we offer:

  • Professional development and skills workshops
  • Access to Kiva’s network of Kiva Fellowship and Internship Alumni
  • Optional participation in Kiva’s Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) and social activities such as happy hours and coffee chats
  • References are gladly given for successful participants

Kiva's Internship is a part-time volunteer position, however, to help offset some expenses, Kiva will provide a modest stipend of $800 a month (before taxes) to its volunteers. Please note that the stipend is considered taxable income and we expect interns to do their own research as to how this may affect their personal/tax implications.

The weekly time commitment for a Kiva Internship is 24-32 hours per week, from January 12th, 2027 - June 30th, 2027. Please ensure you have the availability to commit to the entire internship period before submitting your application.

A diverse and inclusive workplace where we learn from each other is an integral part of Kiva's culture. We actively welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer and a great place to work. Join us and help us achieve our mission!

We will only accept applications directly from candidates. Kiva will not be responsible for any recruiting agency fees, absent a formal agreement.

title: Brand Design Lead
description:
WHO WE ARE.

Glossier is a people-powered ecosystem, brought to life by engaging online and offline experiences. In 12 years, we have built an iconic brand that goes far beyond beauty. Our brand is built on trusted emotional connection, empathy, and consistency in how we show up for people every day.

We are woven into everyday moments of people’s lives, becoming part of their routines, their self-expression, and their confidence. We are defined not just by what we make, but by how we make people feel and the relationships we build over time.

Our north-star values are to be Human, Curious, Playful, and Helpful. We are driven by a shared mission to become the most loved lifestyle brand in the world.

OVERVIEW

We are looking for a multidisciplinary Senior Brand Designer to join the Glossier Creative team and help bring the next chapter of the brand to life across digital, print, product, retail, and experiential design.

Reporting to the Director of Campaign & Design, this role will be a close creative partner across Glossier’s 360° campaigns and brand moments, helping develop big ideas and carrying them through to thoughtful, highly crafted execution across every touchpoint.

This person is equally excited by building a campaign world from the ground up and obsessing over the details that make that world feel complete. They have a sharp understanding of visual language, typography, image-making, materials, composition, and systems, and know how to translate an idea seamlessly from a screen to a billboard, piece of merchandise, retail environment, or unexpected IRL experience.

We are looking for someone who thinks beyond traditional graphic design and is excited about where design is going next. They should be constantly looking at culture, technology, physical spaces, emerging tools, culture, fine art, and new ways for people to experience brands. They are curious by nature, highly collaborative, comfortable solving problems, and excited to experiment while maintaining an exceptional level of craft.

WE ARE LOOKING FOR:

  • Partner closely with the Director of Campaign & Design to concept and execute Glossier’s 360° campaigns, product launches, collaborations, and key brand moments across digital, print, OOH, retail, experiential, product, and merchandise.
  • Translate campaign concepts into cohesive visual identities and scalable design systems that can live across channels while maintaining a clear, recognizable point of view.
  • Work closely with Art Direction, Copy, Brand Marketing, Product Marketing, Retail, Production, and other cross-functional partners to solve creative challenges and bring ideas to life.
  • Design physical brand expressions that push how Glossier shows up in the physical world, including our retail flagships, activations, events, signage, merchandise, mailers + seeding, and other 3D brand touchpoints.
  • Bring a strong understanding of typography, composition, color, image-making, materials, and production to every project, with an exceptional eye for detail.
  • Work fluidly between conceptual and executional thinking, and own projects through final production, including preparing mechanicals and production-ready files.
  • Build thoughtful and organized working systems across Figma and Adobe Creative Suite that allow ideas and campaigns to scale efficiently across the broader Creative team.
  • Continually research new materials, technologies, creative tools, workflows, and modes of expression that can expand what design at Glossier looks and feels like.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5+ years of design experience, preferably within beauty, fashion, lifestyle, culture, or creative studio.
  • A portfolio demonstrating exceptional brand design and conceptual thinking across multiple mediums, with strong examples of both digital and physical work.
  • Experience developing visual identities and design systems across 360° campaigns including print, digital, mailers, merchandise, retail, and experiential or environmental design.
  • A sophisticated understanding of typography, composition, color, image, hierarchy, materials, and visual storytelling.
  • Expert proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite and Figma, with a strong understanding of both digital and print production workflows.
  • Experience collaborating with fabricators, printers, vendors, producers, developers, or other external partners to translate design intent into physical execution.
  • Strong conceptual and problem-solving skills with the ability to take an ambiguous brief, ask the right questions, and turn it into a compelling creative solution.
  • Highly detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a fast-paced creative environment.
  • A collaborative working style and the ability to partner closely with designers, art directors, copywriters, marketers, producers, product teams, retail teams, and external creative partners.

BONUS POINTS

  • Experience with 3D design, rendering, spatial design, or environmental visualization.
  • Familiarity with motion design, After Effects, Premiere, or other moving-image tools.
  • Experience working directly with fabricators and translating creative concepts into built environments.
  • A demonstrated interest in emerging creative technology, AI, generative tools, or other new approaches to design and image-making.

In accordance with the applicable law, the following represents a good faith estimate of the minimum and maximum compensation range for this position:

  • The estimated annual pay range for this role is $106,000.00–$138,000.00.
  • There may be future opportunities for continued pay progression based on continued strong performance in the role.
  • Full-time positions are also eligible for a competitive compensation and benefits package that include medical health insurance, 401K, equity in the form of Restricted Stock Units, Paid Time Off, Short Term and Long Term Disability leave, and a range of other benefits.
  • Learn more at the Glossier Career page.

description:

I further attest that all information I submit in my employment application is true to the best of my knowledge.

Job Description

The GCM HR Transition Lead is responsible for transition methodology and tools for supporting central tracking and program-level project management on behalf of the GCM Transition Head, while defining, maintaining, and enabling the transition methodology, standards, tools, and frameworks that underpin the GCM transition program. The role ensures consistent execution quality across all transition waves by providing teams with the guidance, templates, and reporting infrastructure they need.


Accountabilities:


Project Management Support

  • Support central program-level project management activities, including maintenance of the integrated transition plan, milestone tracking, dependency management, and issue/risk registers across the full portfolio
  • Coordinate cross-wave planning and sequencing, identifying interdependencies and resource conflicts and flagging these to the GCM Transition Head for resolution
  • Design and maintain program-level transition tracking dashboards and reporting frameworks
  • Consolidate status reporting from all transition waves and BU/BFs into integrated programme-level views for governance forums, senior leadership, and external stakeholders

Methodology & Standards Ownership

  • • Own and continuously improve the end-to-end GCM transition methodology
  • • Build and maintain the standardized tools and trackers used to track transition progress, milestones, dependencies, risks, and readiness status across all waves and BU/BFs, ensuring teams have a single, reliable source for tracking
  • • Embed stage-gate governance criteria and readiness assessment frameworks, ensuring all transition teams apply them consistently before progressing through phases

Enabling & Guidance

  • Act as the primary centre of expertise for transition methodology, providing guidance, training, and coaching to Transition Functional Leads, Wave Managers, and KT PMOs on how to apply standards and tools effectively
  • Establish and maintain a central library of approved transition artefacts, ensuring all teams have access to up-to-date templates, frameworks, and reference materials
  • Identify and close methodology gaps based on learnings from live transitions, continuously refining tools and standards to reflect best practice

Continuous Improvement & Lessons Learned

  • • Capture and synthesise lessons learned from completed transitions, translating insights into updates to methodology, toolkits, and guidance for future waves
  • • Drive continuous improvement across the transition program by identifying opportunities to improve efficiency, and embedding learnings systematically

Education & Competencies (Technical and Behavioural):


Experience

  • 7+ years of experience in programme management, PMO, or methodology/standards roles within large-scale global transformation or shared services environments
  • Proven track record of designing and implementing transition or programme management methodologies, frameworks, and toolkits applied across multiple workstreams or business units
  • Experience working in or supporting a PMO function with responsibility for central reporting, governance frameworks, and cross-program tracking
  • Experience in GBS/GCC or shared services transition environments, with strong understanding of KT frameworks, readiness assessments, and stage-gate governance models


Technical Competencies

  • Deep expertise in program and project management methodologies and the ability to translate these into practical transition frameworks
  • Strong ability to design and build program-level dashboards, governance reporting packs, and integrated tracking tools across complex, multi-wave transition portfolios
  • Proficiency in project management and collaboration tools and ability to drive adoption of standardised tooling across transition teams

Behavioural Competencies

title: Debitorbogholder på deltid til Modström
description:
Vi søger en erfaren debitorbogholder på deltid, der har styr på debet og kredit og trives med ansvar, struktur og kundekontakt. Har du samtidig erfaring fra fashionbranchen, er det en klar fordel.

Modström er et dansk fashionbrand med salg til både det danske og internationale marked. Vi søger en deltidsbogholder med erfaring fra en lignende stilling, som har godt styr på debitorbogholderi og trives med at kommunikere med både danske og udenlandske kunder.

Du bliver en del af vores økonomifunktion og får en central rolle i den løbende håndtering og opfølgning på vores debitorer. Du vil have en bred kontaktflade på tværs af organisationen, herunder særligt salg, og kundeservice.

Kendskab til ERP-systemer (anvender Navision) og grundlæggende færdigheder i Excel er en fordel. Det vigtigste er dog, at du har en god regnskabsmæssig forståelse, arbejder struktureret og har lyst til at tage ansvar for dine opgaver.

Stillingen er på 22,5 timer om ugen, med mulighed for at påvirke, hvordan timerne fordeles i løbet af arbejdsugen.

Dine opgaver vil blandt andet inkludere:

  • Varetage den daglige debitorbogføring, herunder håndtering af indbetalinger og afstemning af relevante bankkonti

  • Opfølgning på forfaldne tilgodehavenderDialog med danske og internationale kunder om udestående betalinger

  • Håndtering og opfølgning på kreditmaks og kreditforsikring, samt inkassosager

  • Samarbejde med salg og kundeservice omkring kunderelaterede og kreditmæssige spørgsmål

  • Løbende afstemning og kvalitetssikring af debitordata

  • Bidrage til at optimere og effektivisere arbejdsgange inden for debitorområdet

Vi ser gerne, at du har følgende kvalifikationer:

  • Du har en regnskabsmæssig baggrund og praktisk erfaring med debitorbogholderi

  • Du arbejder selvstændigt, struktureret og med sans for detaljen

  • Du tager ejerskab for dine opgaver og følger dem helt til dørs

  • Du er komfortabel med kundekontakt på både dansk og engelsk

  • Kendskab til eller erfaring fra fashionbranchen er en fordel, men ikke et krav

  • Du er samarbejdsvillig, serviceminded og fleksibel

  • Du har gode IT-kompetencer og
    gerne erfaring med ERP-systemer og Excel

  • Du er nysgerrig på forbedringer
    og ikke bange for at udfordre måden, vi gør tingene på

Bliv en del af Modström

Hos Modström bliver du en del af en dynamisk organisation med en uformel omgangstone og engagerede kolleger. Vi arbejder tæt sammen på tværs af organisationen og lægger vægt på ansvar, samarbejde og en pragmatisk tilgang til opgaverne.

Som debitorbogholder får du en vigtig rolle i økonomifunktionen og kommer samtidig til at arbejde tæt sammen med vores kommercielle organisation. Du får derfor mulighed for både at arbejde med de klassiske debitoropgaver og få indsigt i de økonomiske processer i en international fashionvirksomhed.

Du refererer til CFO Jesper Almstrup.

Arbejdsstedet er Modströms kontor på Danneskiold-Samsøes Allé i København.

Vi glæder os til at læse din ansøgning

Er du interesseret i stillingen, så send din ansøgning og dit CV til jal@modstrom.com. Vi behandler ansøgningerne løbende og lukker søgningen, når vi har fundet den rette kandidat.

CFO Jesper Almstrup

Education:

Performance will be evaluated against agreed annual targets for on time submissions; compliance and review quality; proposal milestone completion; budget adherence; content accuracy and reuse; staff development; and implementation of lessons learned. Win rate and awarded value will be assessed jointly with capture and business development leadership, recognizing their shared responsibility for opportunity selection and competitive positioning.

description:

Protocol & Workflow Management

title: Director, Consulting Practice Management and Operations
description:
About PCDC

Quality primary care is transformative and a cornerstone of healthy, thriving communities. PCDC is a nationally recognized 501(c)(3) community development financial institution that provides capital financing, expertise, and advocacy to expand primary care access and advance health equity in the communities that need it most. Built on 30 years of experience, PCDC is a statewide convener and primary care expert that brings safety net providers together to develop the care models and business practices they need to remain strong, sustainable organizations.


About the Role

PCDC is seeking a Director of Consulting Practice Management and Operations to strengthen the daily, functioning operations of the consulting practice. This is not a back-office role. It is a true thought partner to practice leadership: Someone who owns pricing, capacity planning, client tracking, ad-hoc engagement management, and the systems and culture that let an evolving consulting practice operate well.

Our consulting work spans different funding types, including fee for service client engagements and grant funded programs. This role builds and refines the operational foundation that supports both. You will work closely with practice leaders and staff across the team to keep the business running smoothly while helping it grow.


Key Responsibilities


Strengthening How the Practice Runs

  • Build standard pricing practices across consulting engagements, connecting cost, capacity, and margin so pricing decisions are consistent.
  • Develop capacity planning: know current and future capacity of consulting and delivery staff, so staffing decisions are based on real availability.
  • Own client engagement tracking: follow engagements from scoping through delivery and keep the CRM accurate and up to date.
  • Build and maintain the system and related guidance to capture client outcomes, learning, and feedback to inform the design of new work and creation of content/approaches
  • Implement and lead a data-informed, continuous quality improvement process throughout the unit and service lines, focusing on systems/process improvement. Promote regular and ongoing opportunities for all staff to give feedback on unit operations.
  • Keep teams working with efficient synchronicity across the practice, so different parts of the business support each other instead of duplicating work.
  • Proactively identify areas of improvement; determine solutions; implement enhancements/changes to improve client delivery.


Team and Practice Health

  • Support clear, effective communication across the practice.
  • Contribute to professional development and career growth planning for practice staff, including how roles evolve as the practice grows.
  • Enable collaboration across consulting team members, regardless of their function.
  • Help the practice function and feel like one team.


Supporting Growth

  • Partner with the team on developing new products and services for the practice.
  • Collect and organize client and market signals picked up by client facing staff, so ideas about new services do not stay scattered.
  • Support quality checks on outgoing proposals before they reach clients or funders.
  • Own the process for testing new service ideas before they launch: piloting at a small scale, checking whether the practice can deliver and afford it, and flagging when a new offering needs an outside partner. This is feasibility work, not sales.
  • Work with PCDC’s External Affairs and Advancement (marketing/communications) team to enable increased team visibility and engagement with target audiences/markets.
  • Evaluate helpful tools and technology for coaches and project managers as part of ongoing systems work.
  • Support the planning and data gathering for impact-oriented collateral (i.e. dashboards, compliance reporting, annual report, newsletters, webinars, etc.)

Infrastructure and Cross Team Coordination

  • Build the operational and administrative infrastructure the practice needs to run well, while serving as a key point of contact with PCDC's central Operations, Finance, and HR teams.
  • Work directly with Central's operations, finance, and HR leaders as a partner on shared processes.
  • Work with staff and leadership to fully understand and organize Consulting’s current impact measurement efforts. Act as advisor, teacher, and resource for staff on impact measurement for ourselves and our clients.
  • Design systems and processes with an eye toward long term growth and stability.


Team Leadership

  • Lead and develop the staff (project/engagement managers) who report to this role; grow the team's capabilities as the practice matures.

Portfolio Management Support

  • Plan and manage multiple project work plans, meeting internal and external deliverables in an efficient and timely manner.
  • Manage vendor and consultant contract execution, compliance management, and vendor management.
  • Manage portfolio of hourly-billed engagements, ensuring accuracy and efficiency.
  • Contribute to strategies to address pressing large program challenges.

How to Apply

*For serious consideration, please submit a thoughtful cover letter, resume, and complete online application.


No Calls/No Agencies

title: PRETRIAL SERVICES OFFICER II
description:

Thurston County Pretrial Services seeks a Pretrial Services Officer II as part of its Pretrial Screening and Supervision Team. This team provides information to Thurston County courts and supervises justice-involved clients with the goals of ensuring that these individuals successfully appear in court and remain arrest-free while on pretrial release.

Essential functions may include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Conducting screenings for individuals involved in criminal cases by conducting record checks, verifying information, and completing pretrial risk assessments.
  • Supervising clients on pretrial release based on risk classification system.
  • Monitoring client compliance with court ordered conditions of release and files violation reports as needed. Submitting written reports to the Court and counsel.
  • Making referrals to community service providers.
  • Verifying that court orders have been followed, including documenting compliance and recommended actions.
  • Accessing criminal history databases.
  • Maintaining accurate files and ensuring court documentation is filed in a timely manner.
  • May assign cases to Pretrial Services Officers.

To view the full job classification, click here Pretrial Services Officer II

Thurston County values the diversity of the people it hires and serves. title: Head of Publishing
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Head of Publishing based in Germany.

This is a hands-on leadership opportunity to build a publishing function from the ground up.
You will own the strategy, deal flow, commercial economics, portfolio, and team development.
In the early stages, you will act as a player-coach, personally sourcing studios and negotiating the first deals.
You will establish a structured greenlight process to validate and scale promising mobile game titles.
As the portfolio grows, you will build and lead a dedicated publishing team, starting with the first Publishing Producer hire.
You will work closely with senior leadership and have a direct mandate to shape the direction of the function.
The role combines entrepreneurial ownership, industry relationships, commercial decision-making, and hands-on execution in a remote-first environment.

Accountabilities

  • Build and own the publishing function, defining its strategy, operating model, priorities, and growth roadmap.

  • Develop a strong deal flow by sourcing external studios, managing the pipeline, leading negotiations, and closing publishing partnerships.

  • Personally lead the first studio discussions and transactions, leveraging an established industry network and market reputation.

  • Define deal structures and economics, including revenue-share models, unit economics, profitability assumptions, and payback forecasts in collaboration with analytics.

  • Establish and operate a clear greenlight framework for evaluating titles through testing, soft launch, and scaling stages.

  • Oversee the publishing portfolio alongside the Publishing Producer, including roadmaps, LiveOps initiatives, performance management, and studio relationships.

  • Recruit and develop the publishing team, beginning with the hiring of a Publishing Producer and expanding the function as the portfolio grows.

  • Deliver the first-year objectives, including a signed studio portfolio, an active deal pipeline, 2–3 validated titles progressing toward scale, a functioning greenlight process, and a core publishing team.

    • Requirements

    • Proven experience building a publishing function from scratch or at an early stage, rather than primarily managing an established organization.

    • A strong personal network of game studios and an established reputation within the mobile games market.

    • Hands-on experience negotiating publishing deals, including term sheets, revenue-share structures, and founder-level negotiations.

    • Strong command of publishing economics, including eROAS, payback periods, cohort models, and independent financial analysis.

    • Professional experience with casual or mid-core mobile games on Google Play and iOS.

    • Strong strategic thinking combined with a hands-on, entrepreneurial approach to execution.

    • Excellent negotiation, communication, relationship-building, and stakeholder-management skills.

    • Ability to operate autonomously, make commercially informed decisions, and build processes where none currently exist.

    • English proficiency at B2 level or above.

    • Experience with publishing platforms or SDK products, team hiring and development, alternative app stores, or subscription monetization is a plus.

      • Benefits

      • Opportunity to build and own a publishing function from the ground up with a direct mandate from senior leadership.

      • Access to a proprietary technology platform supporting faster game validation, transparent analytics, and user-acquisition infrastructure.

      • Market-competitive base salary plus a performance-based bonus linked to the success of the publishing function.

      • Fully remote, remote-first working environment across Europe.

      • High level of autonomy with minimal bureaucracy and fast decision-making.

      • Opportunity to shape strategy, partnerships, processes, team structure, and portfolio growth from an early stage.

As an intern at DLR Group, you’ll be part of our Emerging Professional Experience (EPX) Program, designed to give you a meaningful introduction to life within an integrated design firm and a strong foundation for your career in the AEC industry.

Working alongside electrical engineers and professionals across architecture, engineering, interiors, and other disciplines, you will gain hands-on experience with the design process from early concepts and system development through documentation and construction administration.

Our Summer Internship Program is a paid, full-time opportunity running May 18 through August 6, 2027, and interns are expected to participate for the duration of the program. title: Security Officer
description:
Overview

Our team members are the heart of what makes us better.

At Hackensack Meridian Health we help our patients live better, healthier lives — and we help one another to succeed. With a culture rooted in connection and collaboration, our employees are team members. Here, competitive benefits are just the beginning. It’s also about how we support one another and how we show up for our community.

Together, we keep getting better - advancing our mission to transform healthcare and serve as a leader of positive change.

The Security Officer will assume responsibility for the safety and well-being of patients, team members, physicians, visitors, students and Medical Center property. These responsibilities include but are not limited to continuous surveillance, reporting and documenting all incidents and remaining sensitive to the need for delivery of quality guest services and assistance to all persons visiting the Medical Center.

Responsibilities

A day in the life of a Security Officer at Hackensack Meridian Health includes:

  • Make continuous patrols throughout the Medical Center to observe and take corrective action regarding violations and detrimental conditions related to security and safety of patients, visitors, team members, students and property either on foot or in a vehicle. Security Team Members act as visible deterrence to crime and prohibited activities.
  • Respond to calls and codes for security assistance by any person within the Medical Center and take proper action including responding quickly and effectively to emergent and non-emergent situations including all Codes in a timely manner.
  • Provide continuous coverage of the Medical Center, controlling access to the area and assisting patients and visitors as necessary. Challenges unauthorized persons in a professional and courteous manner, issues appropriate passes, and enforces policies and procedures of the Medical Center.
  • Maintain and control access to all facilities owned or operated, leased or owned by Hackensack Meridian Health.
  • Expedite and ensure safe flow of traffic through the Medical Center parking lots while enforcing parking regulations.
  • Conduct preliminary and/or detailed investigations of all unusual occurrences falling under the realm of security matters including but not limited to interviewing witnesses, obtaining signatures and collecting accurate information.
  • Respond to fire drills and perform fire watches; facilitate fire department inspections scheduled by regional safety function
  • Provide escorts to team members and visitor vehicles as requested within jurisdiction.
  • Report for duty in a clean and complete Medical Center issued uniform, including photo identification badge and security officer breast badge.
  • Make continuous inspections of outer buildings, grounds, and parking lots. Works with facilities for detection of fire and life safety hazards
  • Inspects all packages leaving the Medical Center when necessary and according to policy.
  • Prepares and submits computerized security incident reports before the end of shift.
  • Completes and submits a daily activity log at completion of tour of duty.
  • Maintains all departmental security equipment in good operating condition and reports all damage immediately to the Security Leader.
  • Always keeps Security Leaders informed of all matters pertinent to safety and security conditions.
  • Has knowledge of and abides by all Medical Center Code of Conduct regulations and departmental procedures and policies including parking regulations.
  • Completes all in-service training, lectures and programs as assigned.
  • Attend all mandatory meetings (departmental or special).
  • Subject to all weather conditions; will be required to work in all areas of the Medical Center, including parking lots, grounds and outer buildings as requested.
  • Will be required to perform duties as assigned by Security leadership and execute physical security component of emergency management plan upon occurrence of an emergency
  • Other duties and/or projects as assigned.
  • Adheres to HMH Organizational competencies and standards of behavior.

Qualifications

Education, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Required:

  • High School diploma, general equivalency diploma (GED), and/or GED equivalent programs.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proficient computer skills that may include but are not limited to Microsoft Office and/or Google Suite platforms.

Education, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Preferred:

  • 2 years of college credits.
  • Previous experience as Security Officer or Law Enforcement experience.

Licenses and Certifications Required:

  • Possession of a valid driver's license
  • Full scale State, County, Federal, and License Check will be conducted every other year.

If you feel the above description speaks directly to your strengths and capabilities, then please apply today!

Minimum rate of $21.78 Hourly

title: Optical Assembly and Alignment Engineer
description:
At Atom Computing, we build quantum computers using arrays of optically trapped neutral atoms that will empower customers to achieve unprecedented computational breakthroughs. Join a world-class team of scientists, engineers, and business professionals to advance the state-of-the-art in quantum computing.

We are seeking an Optical Assembly & Alignment Engineer to build, align, and verify optical breadboards and laser-delivery assemblies for neutral-atom quantum computers. This hands-on role delivers tested optical subsystems and alignment records to the system integration team.

Responsibilities

  • Assemble optical breadboards and optomechanical hardware from released layouts, drawings, bills of materials, and work instructions.
  • Install and align lenses, mirrors, polarization optics, and fiber-coupling assemblies to establish the required beam paths and subsystem interfaces.
  • Measure optical power, beam profile, polarization, and coupling performance; use wavefront measurements where required by approved test procedures.
  • Troubleshoot optical loss, clipping, alignment drift, and polarization errors; document findings and perform approved adjustments or rework.
  • Work with Optical Bonding Technicians to establish pre-bond alignment and verify that curing or fastening has not disturbed optical performance.
  • Maintain optical cleanliness, protect sensitive coatings, and follow approved handling and laser-safety practices throughout assembly and test.
  • Complete subsystem verification and maintain component, alignment, and measurement records; support resolution of optical issues found during system integration.
  • Learn first-of-a-kind methods alongside Engineering and improve repeat-build alignment instructions, fixtures, and assembly sequences with Manufacturing Engineering.

Experience & Education

  • BS in optics, optical engineering, physics, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant optical-engineering experience; advanced degree preferred.
  • 5+ years of hands-on optical assembly, free-space alignment, fiber coupling, and characterization of precision laser or photonics hardware.
  • Experience building from controlled optical layouts and recording repeatable measurements for subsystem acceptance.
  • Experience with neutral-atom quantum-computer optics, atomic, molecular, and optical (AMO) laboratory systems, or precision scientific instrumentation preferred.

Qualifications

  • Strong practical knowledge of free-space beam alignment, polarization control, fiber coupling, and the relationship between component placement and optical performance.
  • Proficiency with optical power meters, beam-imaging cameras, and related bench metrology; wavefront-measurement experience preferred.
  • Ability to interpret optical layouts and optomechanical drawings and work safely with delicate coated optics.
  • Systematic troubleshooting and careful recordkeeping so another engineer can reproduce alignment and verification results.
  • Ability to work closely with bonding, verification, and integration teams; familiarity with measurement-data analysis or laboratory scripting preferred.
  • Capable of lifting and moving objects that weigh up to 25 pounds.

Atom Computing provides a wide variety of perks and benefits, including fully paid medical, dental, and vision insurance for our employees and their dependents. Additionally, unlimited paid time off, 401K company matching, short- and long-term disability, FSA, dependent care benefits, and life insurance. We also offer drinks, snacks, and catered team lunches in our offices, every day!

The base salary range for this position is between $140,000 - $170,000, commensurate with experience. In addition to salary, we offer an annual bonus and equity in the company.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
About Crunchyroll

Founded by fans, Crunchyroll delivers the art and culture of anime to a passionate community. We super-serve over 100 million anime and manga fans across 200+ countries and territories, and help them connect with the stories and characters they crave. Whether that experience is online or in-person, streaming video, theatrical, games, merchandise, events and more, it’s powered by the anime content we all love.

Join our team, and help us shape the future of anime!

About the Role

We're looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer to embed with teams across Crunchyroll and build AI solutions that materially change how work gets done.

You'll go where the work is. You'll sit with teams, understand how their workflows actually operate, identify where AI or automation can create meaningful value, and rapidly build solutions alongside the people who will use them. This role combines strong business judgment and consultative problem-solving with hands-on engineering. You'll take problems from ambiguity through prototype, production, and adoption.

You'll be part of AI Enablement in the Executive Office, working across Crunchyroll to turn high-value business problems into practical AI-powered solutions, including agents, workflow automation, and other applied AI systems. You'll connect models to the systems, tools, and data teams already use, and build the context, evaluations, guardrails, and human checkpoints required for them to work reliably in the real world.

The goal is not to build AI for its own sake. You'll focus on problems where AI can materially improve speed, quality, cost, or the employee experience, and you'll measure whether what you build actually delivers that impact.

You'll work closely with Engineering, Enterprise Technology, Data & Insights, IT, Security, and other partners to ensure solutions are scalable, secure, and maintainable. Every engagement should also leave behind reusable components, patterns, and lessons that make the next solution faster to build.

In this role, you will:

  • Embed deeply with business teams. Sit alongside them as work happens, map the real workflow rather than the documented one, and understand the pain points, decisions, systems, and handoffs that shape how work gets done.
  • Identify where AI can create meaningful business value. Start with the problem, not the technology, and be willing to conclude that AI is not the right answer.
  • Determine the right technical approach for each problem, whether that is an agentic system, generative AI, RAG, classical ML, deterministic automation, or a simpler software solution.
  • Translate ambiguous business problems into clear technical plans, including architecture, data flows, integration points, permissions, tool usage, success criteria, and build vs. buy vs. integrate decisions.
  • Prototype quickly to test whether an idea works before over-engineering it. Know when to build something in days to learn and when a problem warrants production-grade infrastructure.
  • Design and build reliable AI systems end-to-end, including tool use, orchestration, context and prompt engineering, state and memory, structured outputs, APIs, enterprise integrations, and human-in-the-loop workflows.
  • Engineer for the real world, not the demo. Anticipate failure modes, tool errors, hallucinations, retries, permission boundaries, latency, cost, security constraints, and graceful degradation.
  • Build evaluations and observability from the start. Define task-level success criteria and eval sets, and instrument tracing, logging, monitoring, cost, quality, and drift so performance is measurable in production.
  • Define the expected business outcome before you build and measure whether the solution actually improves the workflow after launch.
  • Work directly with business and technical leaders, translating between business needs and technical reality, setting clear expectations, surfacing risks early, and keeping stakeholders aligned as the solution evolves.
  • Stay close to users after launch. Observe how solutions perform in real workflows, iterate based on usage and feedback, and partner with the broader AI Enablement team on adoption and change management.
  • Build for handoff and scale. Establish clear ownership, documentation, monitoring, and maintenance paths so successful solutions can transition to the appropriate long-term owner.
  • Create reusable components, patterns, tools, and learnings that make future AI solutions faster and easier to build across Crunchyroll.

You have:

  • 6+ years of software engineering experience, including significant recent experience building and shipping applied AI or LLM-powered systems in production.
  • Demonstrated experience designing, building, and deploying AI systems that interact with APIs, enterprise systems, data sources, or external tools to complete multi-step tasks.
  • Strong Python skills and deep experience with modern LLM application development, including tool and function calling, orchestration, prompt and context engineering, structured outputs, RAG, model APIs, state management, and enterprise integrations.
  • Experience taking AI solutions end-to-end, from an ambiguous problem statement through architecture, prototyping, implementation, deployment, and iteration.
  • Experience engineering AI systems for reliability, including failure handling, human-in-the-loop controls, guardrails, permissions, monitoring, cost management, and latency management.
  • Strong technical judgment on when to use an agent, RAG, classical ML, automation, or conventional software, including the discipline to avoid unnecessary complexity.
  • Proven ability to work directly with non-technical stakeholders, understand how their work actually happens, and translate business needs into practical technical solutions.
  • Strong product and business judgment. You can distinguish an interesting technical problem from a problem worth solving.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguous, early-stage environments where you are expected to define the problem as much as solve it.
  • The ability to move between rapid experimentation and production engineering, knowing when speed matters and when reliability, security, and scale matter more.

A plus if you have:

  • Experience in a forward-deployed, embedded, solutions engineering, applied AI, or highly cross-functional engineering role.
  • Experience building tool-using or agentic systems that plan and execute multi-step workflows.
  • Experience with APIs, MCP, event-driven systems, enterprise SaaS integrations, and internal data systems.
  • Experience building internal platforms, SDKs, reusable tooling, or shared components adopted by other engineering teams.
  • Experience evaluating and observing LLM or agent systems, including eval design, tracing, monitoring, and drift detection using tools such as Datadog, LangSmith, Langfuse, or similar platforms.
  • Experience designing multi-agent systems, planner/executor architectures, specialized agents, or other orchestration patterns where they are appropriate.
  • Familiarity with workflow analysis and process mapping, particularly in complex operational environments.
  • Exposure to AI governance, security, privacy, and legal review processes, including risks related to data access, permissions, prompt injection, tool use, autonomous actions, and sensitive information.
  • Experience in media, entertainment, streaming, consumer technology, or another environment with complex content and operational workflows. Familiarity with areas such as localization, marketing operations, content operations, customer support, rights management, or commerce is a plus.

How You'll Work

You won't operate from a centralized backlog waiting for requirements. You'll move toward the highest-value problems, embed with the teams experiencing them, and work alongside those teams until a solution is delivering measurable value.

title: Senior Python Data Scraping Engineer (Freelance)
description:

  • At least 5+ years of relevant experience in data engineering, web scraping, automation, or software development (required).

Academic and/or Professional Experience

Candidates should have a strong technical foundation and practical experience with scripting, automation, and data extraction workflows. We are looking for specialists who can solve non-trivial problems, work confidently with modern development tools and technologies, and systematically collect, structure, and validate data from diverse sources. A methodical, detail-oriented approach and the ability to work independently are essential.

Technical Skills (Essential)

  • Strong experience in Python web scraping (BeautifulSoup, Selenium or similar), including dynamic content (JS, AJAX, infinite scroll) and APIs via proxies
  • Proven ability to extract data from complex structures (hierarchies, archived pages, inconsistent HTML)
  • Solid background in data cleaning, normalization, and validation, delivering structured datasets (CSV, JSON, Google Sheets)

Additional requirements

  • Demonstrated experience handling anti-bot mechanisms and dynamic site structures at scale
  • Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS or equivalent) and containerization (Docker) as part of real workflows
  • Hands-on experience with LLM frameworks (LangChain, OpenRouter, or similar) applied to automation tasks
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy
  • Self-directed work ethic with ability to troubleshoot independently
  • A link to GitHub is a plus
  • English proficiency: Upper-intermediate (B2) or above (required)

Project time expectations

For this project, tasks are estimated to require around 10–20 hours per week during active phases, based on project requirements. This is an estimate, not a guaranteed workload, and applies only while the project is active.

Compensation

On this project, contributors can earn up to $25 per hour equivalent, depending on their level and pace of contribution. Compensation varies across projects depending on scope, complexity, and required expertise. title: Trade Compliance Investigator
description:

In this role, you will impact Honeywell by leading and managing a team of investigators to conduct security investigations, including theft, fraud, and other security-related incidents. You will develop and implement investigation strategies and protocols to ensure thorough and effective investigations. You will coordinate with internal stakeholders, such as HR, Legal, and Compliance, to gather information and evidence for investigations. You will conduct interviews with employees, witnesses, and other relevant parties to gather information and statements. You will collect and analyze evidence, including reviewing surveillance footage, financial records, and other relevant documents. You will prepare detailed investigation reports, including findings, conclusions, and recommendations for corrective actions. You will collaborate with law enforcement agencies, as necessary, to support criminal investigations and prosecutions. You will stay updated on industry trends and best practices in security investigation techniques and tools. You will provide guidance and support to security staff and other employees on security-related matters. You will ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements related to security investigations.

  • Lead and conduct investigations related to potential trade compliance, export control, import, customs, sanctions, and antiboycott violations.
  • Collaborate with internal teams such as Legal, Compliance, Finance, Global Trade, Supply Chain, and business stakeholders to gather evidence and support investigations.
  • Analyze transaction data, trade documentation, shipment records, screening results, communications, and other relevant information to identify potential violations and control gaps.
  • Prepare clear investigation reports with findings, conclusions, root cause analysis, and recommendations for corrective and preventive actions.
  • Conduct investigations consistent with applicable legal, regulatory, and company policy requirements, including confidentiality, privilege, evidence handling, and documentation standards.
  • Stay updated on evolving trade compliance regulations, enforcement trends, and investigation best practices.
  • Provide guidance and training to employees on trade compliance investigation processes, reporting expectations, and policy requirements.

YOU MUST HAVE

  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in trade compliance, export controls, import/customs, sanctions, or related investigative roles.
  • Strong knowledge of international trade regulations, including export controls, import/customs, sanctions, antiboycott, and related regulatory frameworks.
  • Experience as the lead investigator conducting complex investigations involving potential trade compliance violations of the ITAR and/or EAR, restricted party screening, OFAC sanctions violations, diversion concerns, classification, licensing, customs, or recordkeeping matters.
  • Experience as a lead trade compliance investigator drafting initial and final disclosures and other regulatory filings related to voluntary disclosure of trade compliance violations to the government.
  • Proficiency using trade compliance systems, case management tools, screening platforms, and data analysis tools.
  • Experience in developing and guiding corrective action implementation across enterprise-wide processes and systems.
  • Ability to work independently, manage sensitive investigations, and communicate findings with attention to detail, discretion, and sound judgment.

WE VALUE

  • Bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice, International Business, Supply Chain, Finance, Law, or related field.
  • Experience with trade compliance systems including OCR EASE, Kharon, Sayari, SAP, etc.
  • Knowledge of EAR, ITAR, and OFAC regulations.
  • Knowledge of non-US export control and sanctions regulations.
  • Professional certifications such as CFE (Certified Fraud Examiner), CUSECO, CES, CCS, or other trade compliance or investigations certifications.
  • Experience managing investigations across multiple jurisdictions and coordinating with regional trade, legal, and compliance teams.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Knowledge of digital evidence collection, data privacy considerations, and investigation documentation practices.

title: Supporting Independence Recovery Coordinator – Partnered Recovery- Hastings
description:
Supporting Independence Recovery Coordinator – Partnered Recovery

  • Support recovery journeys that improve independence, wellbeing and participation.

About us | Mō mātou ACC is a trusted and high‑performing organisation, providing care, supporting recovery and promoting injury prevention, now and into the future.

You can find more about ACC and the work we do at www.acc.co.nz

About the role | Mō te tūranga mahi

As a Supporting Independence Recovery Coordinator (Levels 1 and 2), you'll play a pivotal role in helping people rebuild their lives after injury. Acting as the primary point of contact for clients with complex or sensitive needs, you'll support individuals and whānau to overcome barriers, access the right services, and achieve greater independence, wellbeing, and quality of life.

Your caseload focuses on clients who are not participating in paid employment and whose recovery goals are centred on living independently, staying connected to their communities, and improving their quality of life rather than returning to work. This includes supporting children, students, superannuants, beneficiaries, and others whose rehabilitation needs are focused on everyday living.

No two days are the same. One conversation may involve helping a young person access supports that enable them to fully participate at school, while another may focus on assisting an older client to remain independent at home following a significant injury. Working alongside clients, family/whānau, healthcare providers, community organisations, schools, support services, and aged-care providers, you'll coordinate personalised recovery plans that create meaningful and lasting outcomes.

This is a role where your empathy, judgement, and relationship-building skills can have a genuine impact. You'll help people regain confidence, maintain independence, and participate more fully in the things that matter most to them, all while contributing to keeping Kiwis safe at work, at home, and everywhere in between.

title: Lead Document Controller
description:
Job Description

Saylor Consulting Group is seeking a full-time Lead Document Controller (Administrative Document Control Specialist) to support our client, the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC). The role provides document control, records management, and administrative services for the Moccasin Dam and Reservoir Long-Term Improvements Project, as part of an anticipated multi-year construction management contract. Work must be done in person. Under the contract, all services are performed onsite, full-time, at the project site in Moccasin, California (Tuolumne County), and remote work is allowed only at the SFPUC Regional Construction Manager's discretion.

The Lead Document Controller will support construction management of a major water infrastructure project within the SFPUC's Hetchy Capital Improvement Program. The project will increase spillway capacity at Moccasin Dam, an earth and rockfill dam built in 1930. Planned work includes utility relocation, heavy excavation, retaining walls, a new concrete spillway, a concrete bridge, and downstream creek improvements. The project uses the Construction Manager/General Contractor (CM/GC) delivery method, with construction expected from late 2028 through 2032.

Working under the SFPUC Regional Construction Manager and the Resident Engineer, the Lead Document Controller will run document control and records management for all documentation received or generated during construction. The role keeps the project record complete, organized, and audit-ready. It also supports labor compliance through review of the contractor's certified payroll. All work follows the HCIP Construction Management Plan and SFPUC CM procedures.

Daily Duties

  • Implement and maintain document control and records management procedures for all project documentation, in line with the HCIP CM Plan.
  • Administer the project's Construction Management Information System (CMIS). This includes logging, filing, and distributing incoming and outgoing correspondence, submittals, RFIs, change documents, reports, and other project records.
  • Review and audit the contractor's certified payroll for completeness and compliance with prevailing wage and contract requirements, and track and follow up on deficiencies.
  • Support administration of the Project Labor Agreement (PLA) by maintaining the related labor compliance records.
  • Maintain document logs, transmittals, and tracking reports, and flag overdue items to the Resident Engineer and Office Engineering staff.
  • Coordinate with the Lead Office Engineer and Assistant Office Engineer on routing and filing of submittals, RFIs, Requests for Substitution, and contract document revisions.
  • File and track daily inspection reports, materials testing records, survey records, and other quality documentation produced by the inspection team.
  • Support the Field Contract Administrator by keeping change order documentation and correspondence organized and retrievable.
  • Help assemble monthly and quarterly progress reports, monthly CM consultant status reports, and contractor payment application packages.
  • Schedule meetings, manage calendars, and prepare and distribute agendas, sign-in sheets, and meeting minutes for weekly progress meetings and other project meetings.
  • Track team training and safety certifications, including Cal/OSHA 10-hour and 30-hour compliance after Notice to Proceed.
  • Support project office mobilization and demobilization, including setup of filing systems and records storage.
  • Coordinate with environmental compliance staff to file and retain environmental inspection reports, monitoring records, and regulatory correspondence.
  • Support project closeout by organizing turnover documentation, warranties, and record drawings, and by preparing and transferring all project files for archiving in accordance with SFPUC requirements.

Minimum Qualifications

  • At least 3 years of experience as an Administrative Document Control Specialist (or equivalent document control role) in construction management of heavy civil construction projects for a public utility.
  • Experience as the Administrative Document Control Specialist on at least one completed, verifiable water infrastructure project of similar type and scope (e.g., dams, reservoirs, spillways, or other water infrastructure).
  • The project must have had a construction value over $10 million and been completed within the past 10 years.
  • At least 2 years of experience within the last 5 years using office management software, such as a Construction Management Information System (CMIS), Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook (email and calendars).
  • Experience reviewing and auditing contractors' certified payroll.
  • Valid driver's license issued by any U.S. state.
  • Ability to obtain Cal/OSHA 10-hour safety training certification within 30 days of contract Notice to Proceed, if not already held.
  • Exceptional organization and attention to detail, with the ability to manage high document volumes accurately.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, and comfortable working with owner representatives, contractors, engineers, and inspectors.
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines and priorities in a fast-paced construction environment.
  • Familiarity with California prevailing wage requirements and Project Labor Agreements.
  • Experience with construction management platforms such as Procore, e-Builder, Unifier, or similar systems.
  • Experience on projects using alternative delivery methods, especially Construction Manager/General Contractor (CM/GC).
  • Familiarity with SFPUC or other public agency records management and construction management procedures.

Featured Benefits

401(k), Medical Insurance, Dental Insurance, 100% employer paid premiums

Additional Information

Saylor Consulting Group (SCG) is a great place to work where your opinion matters, where you can grow with a supportive staff and make a difference in our project outcomes. We are proud to be an advisor on some of the largest, most technically complex projects in the nation. Our business is thriving and we offer unlimited opportunities for growth and career advancement. Additionally, we offer a competitive rate, flexibility, and an environment that recognizes and rewards hard work, with unlimited opportunities for professional development and advancement. Salary is commensurate to education and experience and we offer a competitive full benefits package to full-time employees.

We seek like-minded professionals who have a passion for estimating, drive to achieve results, creative problem-solving ability, and a dedication to client service and relationship management. We want our people to succeed both in work and life. To support this we promote a healthy, productive and flexible working environment that respects work-life balance. Come join us and partner with our world-class team and do your best work.

Please apply by emailing a brief cover letter and CV to nsaylor@saylorconsulting.com. We look forward to hearing from you! Saylor Consulting Group is an equal opportunity employer and makes hiring decisions solely on the basis of merit.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Ride Hailing Product
description:
Who We Are

Nuro believes self-driving vehicles are the most immediate and profound opportunity for AI to drive positive change in the physical world. Safer streets, more time for what matters, and easier access to the world around us, that’s why we’re building a universal autonomy platform: self-driving for all roads and all rides.

Founded in 2016, Nuro is a physical AI company developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology for a wide range of vehicles, use cases, and markets. Powered by the Nuro Driver™, our universal autonomy platform enables the global mobility ecosystem to deploy autonomy at scale, from robotaxis and logistics fleets to personal vehicles.

With years of real-world deployment experience and a flexible, partner-led business model, Nuro is working toward a future where millions of autonomous vehicles powered by our technology help make everyday life safer, easier, and more connected. Nuro has raised over $2B in capital from Uber, NVIDIA, Google, Softbank, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, and other leading investors.

About the Team

A rider taps "request ride" and within seconds, an autonomous vehicle is matched, dispatched, and on its way. The On-Road Experience team owns the systems that make that moment happen. The On-road Experience team builds the real-time distributed system behind Nuro's ride-hailing product. This is foundational infrastructure where correctness and performance have consequences on a real road.

About the Role

This is the perfect role if you love architecting performant, reliable distributed systems, processing real-time vehicle data, and building the foundational APIs that enable seamless product experiences. The position demands technical excellence, a deep understanding of system design, and a knack for solving tough problems. Come join us in defining the future!

What you'll own

  • Backend services for ride planning, vehicle matching, and real-time trip execution
  • Partner API integrations (Uber and others) routing ride requests to Nuro vehicles
  • Telemetry pipelines surfacing live vehicle state to riders and operations

About You

  • 6+ years of backend engineering experience
  • Experience designing and operating distributed systems where reliability isn't optional
  • End-to-end product ownership — from requirements through launch and iteration
  • Solid hands-on experience with GCP (CloudSQL, BigQuery, Redis, or equivalent)
  • A track record of technical leadership: setting the bar, mentoring others, making hard trade-offs

Great to have: dispatch, fleet, location, or delivery/ride platform experience. Even better if you've built systems where the physical world is the end user.

Bonus Points

  • Domain Expertise: Experience with backend services related to vehicles, location, dispatch, inventory, or order/ride/delivery.
  • Product and Business Acumen: A keen interest in the "why" in addition to the "how." You are eager to understand and contribute to product and business requirements, capable of identifying high-impact projects from a list of potential initiatives.

At Nuro, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package. For this position, the reasonably expected base pay range is between $176,000 and $264,000 for the level at which this job has been scoped. Your base pay will depend on several factors, including your experience, qualifications, education, location, and skills. In the event that you are considered for a different level, a higher or lower pay range would apply. This position is also eligible for an annual performance bonus, equity, and a competitive benefits package.

At Nuro, we celebrate differences and are committed to a diverse workplace that fosters inclusion and psychological safety for all employees.
