title: DevOps Lead/Architect
description:
Position Details:

Job Title: DevOps Lead/Architect

Job Type: Full-time

Location: Remote

Dynanet Corporation Overview:

Dynanet started with a focus on IT infrastructure and operations, helping organizations enhance their networks and overcome the limitations of 1990s technology. From strengthening communication channels to introducing innovative ways to collaborate and share information, Dynanet played a crucial role in shaping the early stages of digital transformation. The company’s efforts helped organizations build the very fabric of connectivity that now powers our modern world. Over the last three decades, Dynanet has grown into a trusted partner for organizations looking to innovate boldly and transform seamlessly. While technology continues to evolve and unlock new opportunities, for nearly 30 years, Dynanet remains committed to delivering cutting-edge solutions that drive lasting change for its customers. Through agility, foresight, and an unwavering dedication to excellence, Dynanet continues to empower organizations to thrive in a rapidly changing digital landscape. Our story is more than just a story of technology – it’s a story of vision, growth, and transformation that has shaped the past and continues to pave the way for the future.

About the Role:

Dynanet is seeking a DevOps Lead / Architect to serve as designated Key Personnel on an upcoming federal health agency program providing enterprise DevSecOps platform services.

This role owns the technical architecture and security posture of an enterprise DevSecOps platform estate - artifact repository and binary analysis, test case management, dashboarding and visualization, static code analysis, and managed performance testing - along with the supporting AWS infrastructure, operated across separate accounts spanning development, test, implementation, and production environments.

The position carries architectural authority and compliance accountability. You will maintain continuous Authority to Operate for the platform boundary, define the Infrastructure as Code and observability standards the platform runs on, and serve as the technical interface to the client's information system security officer and to the independent quality assurance contractor.

Roles & Responsibilities:

  • Own the architecture of all managed DevSecOps platforms, establishing a uniform operating pattern for provisioning, identity, backup and restore, observability, and security across every managed tool.
  • Define and maintain the Infrastructure as Code standard using Terraform, including a versioned, peer-reviewed module catalog designed for consumption by delivery teams, with drift detection and remediation.
  • Implement policy-as-code preventive controls on infrastructure and Kubernetes manifests, and apply GitOps workflows for declarative environment management of Kubernetes-based services.
  • Maintain continuous Authority to Operate for the platform boundary by inheriting and sustaining the existing security posture, maintaining security documentation in the client's designated compliance repository and supporting automated compliance narrative and inventory generation.
  • Implement compliance-as-code and documentation-as-code practices so that control evidence, scan results, configuration baselines, and software bills of materials are produced continuously by the pipeline rather than assembled ahead of assessment.
  • Support automated security control assessment processes, security impact analyses, and penetration testing, maintaining the system security plan, risk assessment, contingency plan, and plan of action and milestones on the cadence the client directs.
  • Operate and maintain the artifact repository and binary analysis platform, including project-level repository segregation, retention and quota policy, scan policies and watches aligned to OWASP, CVE, and CWE frameworks, and remediation workflows with SLA tracking.
  • Define the observability architecture spanning application performance monitoring, centralized log aggregation, OpenTelemetry instrumentation, and a metrics and dashboarding layer serving as the correlation and reporting surface.
  • Establish Site Reliability Engineering practice across the platform estate, including service level indicators and objectives, error budgets that govern release velocity, toil reduction, and capacity planning tied to SLOs.
  • Design and maintain the disaster recovery playbook including failover and failback procedures, automated recovery drills, and documented and validated recovery time and recovery point objectives.
  • Implement Zero Trust alignment across the platform estate, including network segmentation, identity-aware access, least-privilege role design, and secrets management with rotation through AWS Secrets Manager, Parameter Store, or equivalent.
  • Lead FinOps and cost optimization practice, including tagging standards, rightsizing, discounted pricing coverage, non-production auto-scheduling, anomaly detection, and recurring cost reporting by service, workload, environment, and system boundary.
  • Maintain architecture documentation as code, including architecture decision records, C4 model diagrams, and API contracts in version control, and evaluate and recommend architecture visualization tooling.
  • Serve as the technical interface to the independent quality assurance contractor under the applicable joint operating agreement, providing timely access to platform configurations, environments, and documentation, and promptly sharing security findings with the client and its security officers.
  • Participate in a 24x7x365 on-call rotation and lead quarterly resilience and security exercise events.

Required Professional Skills:

  • Deep AWS architecture experience in a multi-account environment, including VPC and network design, IAM boundary design, and account segmentation across environments.
  • Expert-level Terraform experience, including modular design, state governance, remote backends, and drift detection at an organizational scale.
  • Strong Kubernetes architecture experience, preferably AWS EKS, including workload design, Helm, and container security practice.
  • Demonstrated ownership of security compliance for a federal system boundary, including maintaining or supporting an Authority to Operate and the associated documentation set.
  • Hands-on experience with artifact management and binary analysis platforms, preferably JFrog Artifactory and Xray.
  • Practical observability architecture experience across metrics, logs, and traces, including OpenTelemetry and at least one enterprise application performance monitoring platform.
  • Demonstrated Site Reliability Engineering practice, including defining service level indicators and objectives and operating against error budgets.
  • Experience designing and testing disaster recovery and backup strategies with validated recovery time and recovery point objectives.
  • Experience with cloud cost optimization practice, including tagging governance, rightsizing, and utilization-driven decision making.

Preferred Professional Skills:

  • Prior architecture ownership within a federal health environment.
  • Familiarity with agency compliance documentation repositories, automated inventory tooling, and federal security control baselines.
  • Experience with compliance automation frameworks such as InSpec, OSCAL-based control authoring, or continuous controls monitoring.
  • Familiarity with NIST SP 800-218 (SSDF), NIST SP 800-53, and Zero Trust reference architecture under OMB M-22-09.
  • Experience with policy-as-code tooling including Open Policy Agent and Conftest.
  • Experience operating Grafana, Prometheus, SonarQube, TestRail, or Apache JMeter as managed enterprise services.
  • Relevant certifications such as AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional, Certified Kubernetes Administrator, CISSP, or HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate.

Dynanet Team Requirements and Expectations:

  • Possess Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Highly organized with the ability to prioritize, balance, and effectively advance multiple competing priorities in a high-volume, fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to interact in a professional and collaborative manner with fellow Dynanet Teammates and the clients, and business partners that we work with.
  • Ability and desire to challenge and educate yourself to support and advance IT services delivery in the Federal agencies we serve.
  • Excellent judgment and creative problem-solving skills.
  • Respond to team member and client requests via email, MS teams, or other communication means during core business hours.
  • Active listening skills to understand clients' needs, and collaboration skills to work with other developers and designers.

Education/Experience Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical discipline. Additional directly relevant experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
  • Minimum of ten (10) years of infrastructure, DevOps, or cloud engineering experience, including at least four (4) years in an architecture or technical lead capacity.
  • Minimum of three (3) years supporting federal systems subject to FISMA and Authority to Operate requirements.
  • Candidates must be able to provide a resume suitable for submission as designated Key Personnel.

Employee Benefits Overview:

  • Industry Competitive Compensation
  • Medical and Dental Insurance
  • Paid Time Off/Holidays
  • 401(k) Retirement Plans with Matching
  • Remote Work*
  • Paid Training
  • Employee Referral Program
  • Employee Development Program?

title: Robotics Engineer Intern
description:
Robotics Engineer Intern

Job Description

We are seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Robotics Engineer Intern to join our dynamic team at Ricoh USA for summer 2027. As a Robotics Engineer Intern, you will gain hands-on experience with advanced robotic systems, work directly with cutting-edge technologies, including simulation-driven robot training in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, and contribute to projects that push the boundaries of industrial automation.

Responsibilities

  • Assist in the design, development, and testing of robotic systems and components, with an emphasis on collaborative robot (cobot) platforms.
  • Contribute to the development of control architectures using ROS2, enabling higher-level autonomy and digital twin integration.
  • Develop and integrate sensor fusion techniques across multiple sensing modalities (e.g., cameras, depth sensors, LiDAR) for perception and safety.
  • Support algorithm development for computer vision, object detection, and pose estimation.
  • Assist in training, fine-tuning, and evaluating deep learning models for object detection and pose estimation using frameworks such as PyTorch, extending existing computer vision algorithm development work.
  • Collect and curate large-scale synthetic training data in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, leveraging domain randomization and automatic ground-truth labeling for bounding boxes, segmentation masks, depth, and object poses.
  • Support robot training in NVIDIA Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab, including reinforcement learning and imitation learning experiments for grasping, manipulation, and cobot motion tasks.
  • Contribute to sim-to-real transfer by validating simulation-trained perception models and policies on physical cobot hardware, and iterating on scene fidelity and randomization ranges to close the sim-to-real gap.
  • Contribute to system development on x86 platforms with NVIDIA GPU acceleration, while also evaluating embedded options (e.g., Jetson Orin) for potential cost, packaging, and performance benefits.
  • Support initiatives using NVIDIA Omniverse for visualization, simulation, and digital twin environments.
  • Support hardware and software integration across robotics, vision, production printers, and workflow systems to deliver cohesive automation solutions.
  • Document project progress and contribute to proof-of-concept demonstrations integrating robotics, vision, and simulation.

Qualifications

  • Enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master’s program in Robotics, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering, or related field.
  • Strong interest in robotics, automation, and applied AI.
  • Proficiency in Python and C/C++, with experience in robotics and vision libraries (e.g., ROS2, OpenCV, PCL).
  • Coursework, research, or project experience with deep learning for computer vision, including hands-on use of a framework such as PyTorch to train and evaluate models.
  • Understanding of sensors (cameras, LiDAR, depth) and hardware/software integration on robotic platforms.
  • Excellent problem-solving ability and attention to technical detail.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams.

Preferred Skills

  • Familiarity with collaborative robots (e.g., UR series) and robotic arm kinematics.
  • Experience with ROS2 middleware, simulation frameworks, and motion planning libraries.
  • Exposure to object detection and pose estimation methods for manipulation and localization tasks, including training or fine-tuning your own models rather than only running pretrained ones.
  • Hands-on experience with NVIDIA Isaac Sim or Isaac Lab, including synthetic data generation, domain randomization, or automatic ground-truth labeling.
  • Familiarity with reinforcement learning or imitation learning for manipulation and grasping, using toolkits such as Isaac Lab, Gymnasium, or Stable-Baselines3.
  • Awareness of sim-to-real transfer challenges and techniques for closing the gap between simulated and physical robot behavior.
  • Experience with GPU-accelerated computing on x86 and interest in exploring embedded platforms (e.g., Jetson) for optimized deployments.
  • Knowledge of computer graphics concepts and digital twin applications (e.g., NVIDIA Omniverse).
  • Research or project experience in embodied robotics and reinforcement learning.

Join us and be part of a passionate team advancing robotics automation, vision, simulation-based robot training, and digital twin technology for next-generation industrial solutions.

Ricoh is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer -- Minorities/Women/Protected Veterans/Disabled.

title: Cancer Center Director
description:
Director, Cancer Center

Jefferson Healthcare | Port Townsend, Washington
$128,082 to $192,117 DOE | Full-Time

This is rural healthcare leadership at its best.

Jefferson Healthcare is looking for an experienced and collaborative Director, Cancer Center to lead Oncology, Infusion, and Radiation Oncology services in Port Townsend, Washington.

And this is a special opportunity.

Cancer care is deeply personal. For patients and families living in rural communities, having excellent care available close to home can make an extraordinary difference.

Jefferson Healthcare understands that.

This role is an opportunity to lead and continue developing a comprehensive, patient-centered cancer program within a community-focused health system that believes strongly in quality, collaboration, access, and taking care of the people who call the Olympic Peninsula home.

The Director will provide strategic and operational leadership across cancer services while working closely with physicians, advanced practice providers, nursing, pharmacy, ancillary departments, and organizational leadership. The position is responsible for supporting safe, high-quality care while strengthening access, patient experience, operational performance, employee engagement, and the continued growth of oncology and infusion services.

The Opportunity

This is much more than overseeing the day-to-day operations of a department.

Jefferson Healthcare is looking for a leader who can see the bigger picture while never losing sight of the patients and families at the center of the work.

The Director will help lead the continued development of cancer services through:

  • Strategic planning and program development
  • Operational leadership across Oncology, Infusion, and Radiation Oncology
  • Patient access, quality, safety, and experience
  • Team leadership, mentoring, and employee development
  • Financial stewardship, budgeting, and resource management
  • Workflow improvement and operational efficiency
  • Regulatory and accreditation readiness
  • Physician, provider, and interdisciplinary collaboration
  • Community partnerships, education, prevention, and outreach
  • Identification of opportunities to expand and strengthen cancer services

The role includes responsibility for annual operating and capital budgets, departmental productivity and staffing, program growth, financial performance, quality improvement, and long-term strategic planning for oncology and infusion services.

What You'll Bring

Jefferson Healthcare is looking for an experienced cancer care leader who knows how to build relationships, develop people, manage complex operations, and move a program forward thoughtfully.

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Nursing, Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, or a related healthcare field
  • 7 years of cancer care experience
  • 5 years of progressive leadership experience in oncology, infusion services, ambulatory care, or related healthcare operations
  • Strong leadership, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills
  • Knowledge of oncology and infusion operations
  • Experience collaborating across multidisciplinary healthcare teams

The position reports to the Chief Nursing Officer and carries supervisory responsibility for the cancer services team.

Preferred:

  • Master's degree in Nursing, Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, or a related field
  • Oncology Nursing Certification (OCN)
  • Nurse Executive Certification (NE-BC or NEA-BC), or another applicable leadership certification
  • Experience with oncology program development and strategic service-line growth
  • Experience with clinic or ambulatory healthcare operations

Jefferson's internal position description specifically emphasizes strategic planning, program development, financial management, quality improvement, regulatory knowledge, and the ability to build collaborative relationships across multidisciplinary teams.

Why Jefferson Healthcare?

There are healthcare organizations that simply happen to be located in rural communities.

And then there are organizations that truly understand what it means to serve one.

Jefferson Healthcare is a community-focused health system serving East Jefferson County on Washington's Olympic Peninsula. Its teams work collaboratively across departments and disciplines with a shared commitment to excellent patient care and continuously improving how healthcare is delivered locally.

For the right leader, this is an opportunity to join an organization where your work can be both strategic and deeply personal.

You will have the ability to develop people, strengthen systems, expand services, build partnerships, and help shape the future of cancer care for a community that depends on it.

Why Port Townsend?

Port Townsend is one of those places that is difficult to describe without wanting to visit it.

Located on Washington's Olympic Peninsula, the community offers a remarkable combination of water, mountains, trails, outdoor recreation, arts, culture, history, and small-town connection.

It is a place where you can build an important career without giving up the kind of life many people spend years trying to find.

For a cancer care leader looking for meaningful work, an exceptional community, and the opportunity to make a visible difference, this one deserves a serious look.

Work Where It Matters.

At Rural Staffing Services, we believe rural healthcare deserves exceptional people.

Not simply someone who meets the qualifications on paper.

Someone who understands the responsibility, the opportunity, and the people behind the work.

If you are an experienced cancer care leader and this sounds like the kind of work you have been looking for, we would love to learn more about you.

Apply below to connect with Rural Staffing Services and tell us your story.

About the role

We have an opportunity for a Platform Owner to be part of our Policy Pipeline, Technology and Communication Services Command. The role is responsible for the strategic management and overall success of technology platforms within NSW Police Force with a primary focus on overseeing the life cycle of the platform, from initial planning and design to ongoing operations and continuous improvement.

View the relevant role description for more information on this role (e.g. essential requirements, key accountabilities, key challenges and capabilities required for the role)

This role is responsible for driving the successful delivery and continuous improvement of policy-focused digital solutions that support operational, corporate and legislative requirements across NSW Police Force. The position works with policy owners, operational stakeholders and delivery teams to translate complex policy, legislative and business requirements into digital capabilities that improve compliance, process efficiency and customer experience. The role ensures product priorities align with organisational objectives, regulatory obligations and evolving business needs.

Unique Aspects

  • Owns and manages the product direction, roadmap and backlog for policyrelated

    digital services and platforms.

  • Works closely with policy owners, business representatives and operational stakeholders to understand current and future policy requirements.
  • Translates complex policy, legislative and procedural requirements into prioritised product features and business capabilities.
  • Leads stakeholder engagement activities across diverse business areas to ensure solutions support operational outcomes and compliance obligations.

  • Evaluates current business processes and identifies opportunities to

    improve, automate or digitise policy-driven activities.

  • Facilitates the prioritisation of competing business requirements, balancing risk, compliance, value and delivery effort.
  • Supports the delivery of technology solutions that improve policy implementation, governance and decision-making.
  • Monitors legislative, regulatory and organisational changes that may impact product direction and customer needs.
  • Uses business insights, customer feedback and operational data to identify improvement opportunities and measure product performance.
  • Works collaboratively with analysts, architects, developers and vendors to ensure delivery outcomes align with policy intent and business objectives.
  • Supports change adoption activities through stakeholder engagement, communication and continuous feedback.
  • Contributes to strategic planning and future-state service design across policy and business transformation initiatives.
  • Ensures solutions appropriately manage sensitive information and comply with NSWPF governance requirements.


What we can offer you

At NSWPF our people have access to a range of benefits that help balance life at work and at home. Some of the benefits available when you join the NSWPF include\:

  • competitive salary;
  • flexible work options;
  • opportunity to purchase leave;
  • annual leave loading;
  • corporate wellbeing programs including seminars and the Fitness Passport;
  • free annual influenza vaccination;
  • salary packaging options via superannuation contributions or a novated vehicle lease;
  • convenient location for public transport and to shops etc; and
  • in-house gym facilities.

How to Apply

Applications can only be submitted electronically via the I Work for NSW website.

To be considered for this role, attach a cover letter (2 pages maximum) and an up-to-date resume that clearly details your skills & experience as relevant to this role.

Please do not attach copies of qualifications, certificates or documentation (other than what has been requested) - you can bring these if called for interview.

Please address each of the following Target Questions (500 words per question) in the text boxes provided in the online application or attach as a separate document.

Target Question 1\:

Tell us about a time you led the assessment of a significant business or legislative change. How did you analyse the business processes, determine the impacts across systems and stakeholders, and translate the requirements into a solution approach and delivery work packages?

Target Question 2\:

Describe a time you led a multidisciplinary agile team to deliver changes across complex or legacy technology platforms. How did you balance
delivery time frames, technical debt, user experience, and operational requirements while ensuring successful outcomes for users and the organisation?

Your application must stand on its own merits, and the completeness and relevance of your application will determine if you proceed through to the selection process.

If you require any further information about this opportunity, please contact Manish Choyal via 0426 659 354.

To be eligible to apply for this role, you must meet one of the following statuses\:

  • an Australian Citizen;
  • a permanent resident of Australia; or
  • a New Zealand citizen.

Prior to commencement, the successful candidate will be required to undergo a rigorous National Police (criminal history) Check and obtain and maintain a Security Clearance as determined by the NSW Police Force.

Our commitment to Diversity\:

At the NSW Police Force, we are proud to be an employer of a diverse range of people. We are committed to reflecting the diverse community we serve and creating an inclusive and respectful workplace for all employees where differences are embraced, contributions are valued, and everyone has a sense of connection and belonging.

We welcome applications from individuals with diverse skills, experiences, and backgrounds including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, LGBTQIA+ individuals, people with disability, neurodiverse individuals, those from culturally and linguistically diverse communities, and people of all ages.

We understand that the recruitment journey may present unique challenges. If you\:

For more information on applying for roles with the NSW Police Force click here

title: Enterprise Systems Consultant
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Enterprise Systems Consultant based in Germany.

This is a senior technology advisory role focused on helping investors and business leaders make high-impact decisions about enterprise systems and technology operations.
You will lead technology diligence and value-creation engagements, often in fast-moving transaction environments where clear judgment and practical expertise are essential.
Your work will span enterprise applications, business processes, infrastructure, managed services, data, controls, and operating models.
You will assess complex technology environments, identify the issues that materially affect transactions or transformation plans, and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
You will work directly with investors, boards, executives, and management teams, communicating technical conclusions in clear business terms.
Beyond diligence, you may develop post-close technology roadmaps, support vendor selections, govern transformation programs, or step into interim leadership assignments.
The role offers significant autonomy and variety, with opportunities to collaborate with specialists across cybersecurity, data and AI, software, integration, and carve-out services.

Accountabilities

  • Lead sell-side technology diligence engagements, including evidence review, management interviews, buyer-readiness assessments, remediation priorities, and responses to buyer questions.

  • Lead buy-side technology diligence, assessing enterprise systems, infrastructure, organizations, vendors, contracts, technology spend, scalability, resilience, and future investment requirements.

  • Evaluate ERP, warehouse management, WMS, CRM, PSA, and related enterprise applications, including process fit, customization, integrations, data quality, reporting, controls, adoption, licensing, vendor support, and lifecycle risks.

  • Assess end-to-end business processes such as order-to-cash, project-to-cash, procure-to-pay, record-to-report, month-end close, recruit-to-retire, warehouse operations, fulfillment, and IT service management.

  • Conduct process walkthroughs, management and user interviews, evidence reviews, and operating-metric analysis to identify weak handoffs, control gaps, manual workarounds, data issues, key-person dependencies, and scalability constraints.

  • Assess traditional and hybrid infrastructure, including data centers, colocation, networks, identity, end-user computing, backup, disaster recovery, hybrid cloud, and migration of packaged applications to cloud infrastructure.

  • Evaluate MSP and MSSP arrangements, including service scope, pricing, contracts, service levels, operational performance, transition risks, and governance.

  • Assess IT operating procedures covering service desk operations, incidents, problems, changes, access management, onboarding and offboarding, asset management, configuration management, escalation, and service-level reporting.

  • Identify and quantify material technology investments, including system replacements, deferred upgrades, infrastructure remediation, provider transitions, and additional staffing or capability requirements.

  • Translate technical and operational findings into concise, evidence-based conclusions relevant to investment theses and understandable to senior non-technical stakeholders.

  • Develop practical post-close technology and systems roadmaps, and where appropriate support vendor selection, delivery governance, operational improvements, or interim leadership requirements.

  • Collaborate with specialists across cybersecurity, data and AI, product and software, integration, and carve-out services when deeper expertise is required.

  • Contribute to methodologies, benchmarks, training, and service development based on client and operational experience.

    • Requirements

    • At least 15 years of relevant experience across enterprise systems, IT operations, technology leadership, systems transformation, transaction advisory, or a combination of these areas.

    • Proven experience leading multiple sell-side, buy-side, or comparable rapid technology assessments for private equity, corporate M&A, or portfolio-company environments.

    • Leadership-level knowledge across enterprise applications such as ERP, warehouse systems, PSA, CRM, traditional infrastructure, and managed services.

    • Deep hands-on operating or delivery experience in at least two of these technology domains.

    • Direct accountability for major business-process or systems outcomes, transformation programs, budgets, service providers, or IT operations.

    • Demonstrated ability to conduct process walkthroughs and assess end-to-end business processes across multiple business functions.

    • Practical experience across several processes such as order-to-cash, project-to-cash, procure-to-pay, record-to-report, month-end close, recruit-to-retire, warehouse and fulfillment operations, and IT service management.

    • Experience selecting, implementing, upgrading, recovering, or rationalizing enterprise systems, with a strong understanding of process and data dependencies.

    • Experience with traditional and hybrid infrastructure, including data centers, colocation environments, and migrations of packaged applications to cloud infrastructure.

    • Experience selecting, transitioning, managing, or materially renegotiating MSP or MSSP services.

    • Strong analytical and financial judgment, including the ability to estimate one-time and recurring technology investments.

    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage investors, boards, executives, functional leaders, and technical teams.

    • Strong ability to distinguish symptoms from root causes and assess whether challenges originate from processes, systems, data, controls, organization, training, governance, or service-provider performance.

    • Ability to work effectively with incomplete information, make uncertainty explicit, and identify the evidence needed to reach sound conclusions.

    • Self-directed, hands-on working style suited to fast-moving, remote client engagements.

    • Experience as a CIO, VP of IT, Head of Enterprise Applications, enterprise systems program leader, technology operating partner, or senior M&A technology advisor is a plus.

    • Experience in professional services, technology-enabled services, distribution, logistics, manufacturing, or other operationally intensive sectors is a plus.

    • Experience with Salesforce, professional-services automation platforms, WMS, warehouse operations, or eCommerce is a plus.

    • Experience translating diligence findings into systems roadmaps, vendor selections, implementation governance, or interim leadership assignments is a plus.

    • A bachelor's degree in information systems, computer science, engineering, business, or a related field is preferred; relevant professional experience is valued more highly than a specific degree or certification.

      • Benefits

      • Remote position serving clients across Europe.

      • High level of autonomy and ownership across varied technology advisory engagements.

      • Opportunity to work directly with private equity investors, boards, executives, and senior technology leaders.

      • Exposure to complex technology environments spanning enterprise applications, infrastructure, business processes, managed services, and transformation.

      • Opportunity to contribute to both transaction-focused diligence and longer-term value-creation initiatives.

      • Collaboration with specialists across cybersecurity, data and AI, software, integration, and carve-out services.

      • Variety of engagements across industries and business models.

      • Opportunity to influence methodologies, benchmarks, training, and the development of advisory services.

      • Environment centered on service, curiosity, credibility, commitment, and creativity.

      • Flexible remote working environment designed for experienced professionals who can operate independently.

title: Senior Data Analyst
description:
Senior Data Analyst


Unity is committed to providing meaningful, compassionate care to patients and families at the end of life. We are looking for a Senior Data Analyst who is passionate about using data to improve care, support our teams, and help drive better business decisions. Our culture is built around Excellence, Collaboration, Integrity, Compassion, and Accountability.


ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Senior Data Analyst will play a key role in building and supporting Unity’s reporting and analytics capabilities. This position will work closely with leaders and teams across the organization to turn clinical, financial, and operational data into useful information and insights.


The Senior Data Analyst will help lead the development of our analytics platform, support data governance and quality, create meaningful dashboards and reports, and help teams use data to make informed decisions.


This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys both the technical side of data and working directly with people to solve problems and improve how an organization uses information.


SCHEDULE:

This is a salaried, exempt position with a Monday–Friday schedule. Typical hours are between 7:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., with flexibility based on business needs.


WHAT YOU’LL DO:

• Lead the development and ongoing support of Unity’s reporting and analytics platform.
• Work with leaders and teams to understand their data and reporting needs.
• Create and maintain dashboards, reports, and data solutions using tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or similar platforms.
• Write SQL queries and work with databases to extract, organize, and analyze data.
• Support data interfaces and data flows between internal and external systems.
• Help ensure data is accurate, complete, secure, and reliable.
• Support data governance efforts, including data standards, access, and quality.
• Work with vendor partners and internal teams to troubleshoot and improve data systems.
• Analyze clinical, financial, and operational data to identify trends, opportunities, and areas for improvement.
• Use data to help leaders make informed decisions and improve patient care, quality, and operational performance.
• Explore the use of AI and other new technologies to improve analytics and reporting.
• Develop training and resources to help employees use reporting and analytics tools effectively.
• Present data and findings in a clear and easy-to-understand way to both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Lead and manage analytics projects from planning through completion.
• Build strong relationships with leaders and teams across Unity.


WHY JOIN UNITY?

At Unity, your work has a direct connection to the patients, families, and teams we serve. You’ll have the opportunity to use your data and analytics experience to make a meaningful impact while working with leaders and teams across the organization.

We value people who are curious, collaborative, accountable, and passionate about finding better ways to use data.

title: Production Planner II
description:
As a Production Planner II here at Honeywell Aerospace, you will be supporting globally across the supply chain network to gather and manage information about our businesses' capacity to meet customer demand.

In this role, you will support and improve the supply chain planning & execution process within the business. You will create and maintain a valid master schedule for material and capacity by effectively balancing supply and demand. You will ensure emerging program master production schedules are executable and material resource planning profiles are complete. As the Master Scheduler, you will lead the activities related to the purchase of material, material planning, production planning, inventory control, and shipping/receiving. You will support work autonomously to achieve organizational objectives and drive functional excellence and continuous improvement. You will collaborate among global cross-functional teams to support complex projects.

You will report directly to Materials Mgmt Manager, and you’ll work out of our San Jose, CA location on a Hybrid work schedule. You will be required to work onsite for the first 90 days.

KEY RESPONSIBLITIES

  1. Fulfill demand requirements by examining Material Requirements Planning (MRP) indications
  2. Communicate material availability to procurement and ensure that need dates are met to release production orders
  3. Maintain configuration and serial control of production hardware
  4. Ensures the generation of pick lists, packing slips, and other shipping document as required
  5. Flag and communicate production problems
  6. Responsible for requesting Customer Source Inspection (CSI) of hardware shipments
  7. Assure that planning data items are properly maintained in SAP, and are compatible with applicable program plans and schedules
  8. Support production programs by working with the program managers and production leads
  9. Collaborate in team meetings and activities
  10. Participate in safety training and actively comply with safety policies and practices

YOU MUST HAVE

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in Material Requirements Planning (MRP) in a manufacturing environment
  • This position requires access to technology, materials, software or hardware that is controlled by US export laws. In order to be eligible for this position, you must be a “US Person” under US export laws (or eligible for approval under a U.S. Government export license).

WE VALUE

  • Bachelor’s Degree.
  • Experience with Supply Chain concepts such as Purchasing, Logistics, etc
  • Intermediate Computer skills including Excel and Word
  • Excellent organizational, presentation and communication skills
  • MRP Experience: SAP or Oracle experience preferred.
  • Advanced to Expert level in Excel and Power Point.
  • Manufacturing, Electronic or Aerospace industry background.
  • Knowledge of FAR or recent experience supporting a government contractor environment.

ABOUT HONEYWELL AEROSPACE

Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.
Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

THE BUSINESS UNIT

Honeywell Aerospace’s Performance Materials and Technologies (PMT) business unit delivers innovative solutions that improve the efficiency, safety, and sustainability of industrial processes worldwide. We provide advanced materials, process technologies, automation solutions, and services that help customers optimize their operations and meet evolving market demands.

Honeywell Aerospace is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will be considered without regard to age, race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, marital status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, nationality, sex, religion, or veteran status. Learn more about inclusion and diversity.

BENEFITS OF WORKING FOR HONEYWELL AEROSPACE

Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:
• Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
• Short-term and long-term disability coverage
• 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
• Employee assistance program and educational assistance
• Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
• Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits: https://honeywellaerospacebenefits.com/

The annual base salary range for this position is $76,000 - $95,000. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Principal DevOps Engineer (PeopleFluent) based in India.

This is a senior infrastructure leadership role focused on designing, automating, and operating hybrid environments across on-premises data centers and AWS. You will set the technical direction for compute, networking, and platform services while driving scalability, security, reliability, and cost efficiency. The role combines hands-on engineering with architectural ownership and end-to-end delivery of complex infrastructure initiatives. You will work closely with engineering and product teams to define requirements and communicate technical trade-offs. As a subject matter expert, you will contribute expertise across areas such as virtualization, cloud architecture, and observability. The position also provides opportunities to mentor engineers and shape how modern hosting infrastructure is built and operated.

Accountabilities:

The Principal DevOps Engineer will own the technical evolution, automation, reliability, and operational effectiveness of the hosting infrastructure. Key responsibilities include:

  • Own and maintain PeopleFluent hosting pipelines and infrastructure automation.
  • Define the technical vision and architecture for hosting infrastructure across compute, networking, and platform services.
  • Ensure infrastructure architecture supports long-term scalability, security, reliability, maintainability, and cost-effectiveness.
  • Proactively identify opportunities to optimize infrastructure performance, capacity, reliability, and operational efficiency.

      • Experience working in Agile and Scrum environments.

      • Experience working in startup or fast-paced technology environments.

title: Hybrid Board Certified Behavior Analyst - Telehealth Option Available
description:
Title: Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) Hybrid Remote

Location: The Woodlands, TX and Surrounding Areas (Hybrid Option Available)

At Cortica, our Board-Certified Behavior Analysts (BCBAs) use a strength-based, holistic approach to clinical programming for children with autism and other neurodevelopmental differences. Our valued BCBAs are leaders who make a difference and create a supportive environment where all clinicians in our transdisciplinary team can thrive, grow, and make a meaningful, long-term impact for families.

You’ll provide groundbreaking, neurodiversity-affirming care, while enjoying the flexibility and support you deserve.


Why Choose Cortica?

We’re excited to support your continued professional development, growth, well-being, and ability to make a meaningful impact as part of a transdisciplinary team. That's why our compensation and benefits package has been designed to support you personally and professionally:

  • Earning Potential (Salary +Productivity Bonus): $90,000 - $112,000
    • Plus earn up to an additional 10% of your monthly salary with our second bonus – that’s right, TWO bonuses to increase your earning potential!

  • Generous Time Off to Recharge and Maintain Work-Life Balance: Up to 22 days off in your first year, increasing to 26 days after 12 months.
  • Flexible Hybrid Role: We offer remote flexibility, allowing you to balance your clinical work and administrative tasks on your terms. Telehealth is determined by the BCBA when it's clinically effective for the client and BT.
  • CEU Stipend: $2,000 annually to support your continued professional development.
  • License Reimbursement: We cover the cost of your BCBA license renewal.
  • 401(k) Matching: Helping you plan for your future with matching contributions.
  • Comprehensive Health Coverage: Including medical, dental, vision, life, disability insurance, plus pet insurance—because we care about your entire family, furry friends included!
  • Set Scheduling: Predictable work hours help you balance your work and personal life.

Your Role and Impact

As a BCBA at Cortica, you’ll play a pivotal role in overseeing neurodiversity-affirming clinical programming for patients receiving ABA treatment. You'll lead a team of behavior technicians (BTs) empowering them to make a lasting difference in the lives of children with developmental differences.

What you’ll love about this role:

  • Achievable Targets: You’ll average 26 billable hours per week, with reduced targets during shorter weeks to ensure a manageable workload.
  • Industry-Leading Dual Bonus Program: Enjoy two separate bonus opportunities that reward your impact and leadership.

- Productivity Bonus: Increase your earning potential through flexible productivity incentives designed to reward additional billable hours while maintaining work-life balance.

-ABA Caseload Bonus: Earn additional monthly bonus opportunities based on ABA direct service hours billed and converted within your POD, with bonus potential up to 10% of monthly base salary.

  • Growth and Advancement Opportunities: You'll have the chance to advance through BCBA levels I, II, III, and IV, increasing your leadership impact along the way. At BCBA levels III and IV, productivity targets are reduced to 22, allowing you to focus on developing leadership skills, cultivating other talents, and exploring broader professional interests.
  • Autonomy over Your Schedule: You’ll have full control over when and where you supervise your cases, empowering you to design a schedule that works for you.
  • Administrative Support: Focus on what you do best—clinical care—while our dedicated team handles scheduling, billing, and credentialing, leaving you with more time to focus on your work and patients.

Qualifications and Requirements

  • Master’s degree in human services or a related field.
  • Current BCBA (Board-Certified Behavior Analyst) Certification required.

What Makes Cortica Different from Other ABA Companies?

At Cortica, we believe in going beyond traditional ABA practices to offer a more comprehensive, patient-centered approach that is different from other ABA companies:

  • A Transdisciplinary Approach to Care: Unlike many ABA companies that focus solely on behavior therapy, Cortica offers a holistic, multidisciplinary model of care. Our team includes experts from a wide range of fields—occupational therapy, speech pathology, pediatrics, and more—allowing us to address the whole child and deliver more integrated, effective care.
  • Focus on Collaboration: At Cortica, we don’t just implement therapy—we collaborate with families, caregivers, and other clinicians to create individualized care plans that empower everyone involved. This approach ensures that each child’s unique needs are met, and that the entire team is aligned in their goals for success.
  • Quality Over Quantity: We take pride in value-based care partnerships with health plans that prioritize quality over quantity. Our patients benefit from the time we dedicate to collaborative, integrated care, and our clinicians are supported with more time for thoughtful clinical decision-making. Unlike other providers, we are reimbursed based on outcomes, not just the number of sessions delivered.

By joining Cortica, you’ll be part of a team that’s redefining ABA therapy—combining compassion, innovation, and collaboration to deliver results that matter.

Ready to make a difference? Apply today to learn more.

title: Polarion Architect
description:
Polarion Architect

Company Overview

From start-ups to blue-chip enterprises, Saratech helps companies engineer and manufacture complex products. Saratech is a leading Siemens Digital Industries Software partner and engineering services company specializing in digital transformation initiatives across aerospace, defense, space launch, automotive, industrial equipment, and high-tech industries.

Our team delivers Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), Polarion ALM, Digital Thread, Digital Twin, Model-Based Enterprise (MBE), and systems integration solutions that enable customers to connect engineering, manufacturing, and business processes. We help organizations integrate critical platforms such as Teamcenter, Polarion ALM, ERP, MES, CRM, EDA, and MCAD systems to improve collaboration, data governance, and operational efficiency.

Job Description

Saratech is seeking an experienced and highly motivated Polarion Architect to join our growing Engineering Excellence team. The ideal candidate will possess a strong combination of software development expertise, enterprise architecture experience, knowledge of Siemens Digital Industries Software, and depth in the engineering domain.

The Senior Polarion Architect will lead the design and delivery of Siemens Polarion Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) solutions for customers managing complex product development, software engineering, and regulated processes.

This role combines hands-on technical expertise, solution architecture, and customer consulting. The architect will translate business needs into scalable solutions that connect requirements, development, testing, change management, and product lifecycle information. The position will also provide technical leadership to delivery teams and support the growth of our Polarion services business.

The successful candidate will work directly with customers, sales teams, project managers, and technical consultants to define Digital Thread strategies, develop technical solutions, and support successful deployment of digital transformation initiatives.

We are looking for an individual who enjoys solving complex technical challenges, working directly with customers, mentoring technical resources, and helping drive the future of Digital Thread enablement.

Key Responsibilities

Solution Architecture and Consulting

  • Lead customer discovery workshops to understand business objectives, engineering processes, compliance needs, and existing systems.
  • Define Polarion solution architectures, implementation roadmaps, and configuration standards.
  • Design requirements management, test management, defect management, change control, and end-to-end traceability processes.
  • Establish approaches for project structures, reusable templates, baselines, permissions, reporting, and governance.
  • Advise customers on standard capabilities, configuration, and custom development, balancing business value with long-term maintainability.

Implementation and Integration

  • Lead and perform Polarion configuration, customization, deployment, migration, and upgrade activities.
  • Design and oversee integrations with Teamcenter, development tools, test automation platforms, and other enterprise systems.
  • Define data migration strategies, including mapping, cleansing, validation, and reconciliation.
  • Develop or oversee extensions, scripts, reports, and dashboards using supported Polarion interfaces and development methods.
  • Address performance, scalability, availability, security, and operational support requirements with customer IT teams.
  • Diagnose complex technical issues and lead resolution through testing, root-cause analysis, and corrective action.

Technical and Delivery Leadership

  • Serve as the technical authority for Polarion engagements, maintaining alignment between requirements, architecture, and delivered functionality.
  • Develop technical estimates, implementation plans, assumptions, and scope for proposals and statements of work.
  • Identify dependencies, delivery risks, and architectural decisions early in the project.
  • Review solution designs and implementation quality; mentor consultants and developers.
  • Create reusable implementation assets, technical documentation, and delivery standards.
  • Support customer demonstrations, technical presales discussions, training, and knowledge transfer.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, information systems, or equivalent professional experience.
  • At least seven years of relevant experience in ALM, software engineering tools, or enterprise systems implementation, including substantial hands-on Polarion experience.
  • Demonstrated experience leading Polarion architecture and implementation across multiple customer engagements or complex enterprise programs.
  • Strong knowledge of requirements engineering, verification and validation, configuration management, and lifecycle traceability.
  • Experience configuring Polarion workflows, work items, documents, permissions, templates, and reporting.
  • Experience with enterprise integrations, APIs, scripting, and software development; proficiency in Java and relevant web technologies.
  • Ability to translate complex technical topics into clear recommendations for business leaders, engineers, and IT stakeholders.
  • Strong consulting, documentation, problem-solving, and technical leadership skills.

Preferred

  • Experience integrating Polarion with Siemens Teamcenter and supporting digital thread initiatives.
  • Experience in aerospace and defense, automotive, medical devices, energy, or other regulated industries.
  • Familiarity with applicable safety, quality, and development standards and how lifecycle tools support compliance evidence.
  • Experience with enterprise deployment, authentication, disaster recovery, and controlled or restricted environments.
  • Relevant Siemens Polarion training or certifications.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package
  • Remote work flexibility
  • Opportunities for professional growth and technical leadership
  • Exposure to Siemens technologies and innovative digital transformation projects
  • Access to customers across aerospace, defense, industrial, automotive, and high-tech manufacturing
  • Collaborative and supportive team culture
  • Professional development and training opportunities
  • A culture focused on innovation, customer success, and technical excellence

Retirement Plan: All employees can enroll in the company's 401k with company matching.

Paid Time Off: All full-time regular exempt employees are eligible for our Discretionary Time Off vacation policy after 90 days from their start date, Discretionary Time Off plan is a non-accrual plan for employees. All full-time regular non-exempt employees are eligible for our Paid Time Off Plan policy after 90 days, Paid Time Off plan is an 3.33 hours accrual per pay period for employees.

Paid Sick time: All full-time employees will receive 32 sick hours per year. Part time employees will receive 24 hours or minimum sick time required by the state.

description:
Government Employees Health Association, Inc. (G.E.H.A) is a nonprofit member association that provides health and dental benefits that millions of federal employees and retirees, military retirees and their families have counted on since 1937. Offering one of the largest health and dental benefit provider networks available to federal employees in the United States, G.E.H.A empowers health and wellness by meeting its members where they are, when they need care.

G.E.H.A has one mission: To empower federal workers to be healthy and well.

The Associate National Accounts Specialist supports G.E.H.A Solutions Inc.’s clients, and network partners by responding to service inquiries, researching provider participation, and assisting with provider referral and nomination processes. This position supports the National Accounts team, helping ensure inquiries are resolved according to contractual requirements, and escalate concerns that may impact department key performance indicators to the Supervisor.

•Responds to incoming service inquiries regarding network providers and nomination requests.
•Researches, analyzes, and documents service inquiries to support timely and accurate resolution.
•Provides administrative and operational support to National Accounts Specialists and department leadership.

SKILLS

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Provides timely and professional responses to service inquiries received from clients and network partners.
  • Use department applications, databases, and provider directories to verify provider participation and assist callers with accurate information.
  • Creates, updates, and tracks service inquiries in accordance with department procedures and contractual requirements.
  • Submits provider nominations received through calls, website contact forms, and other approved channels.
  • Monitors shared department resources, including voicemail and website Contact Us email inboxes, and routes inquiries to the appropriate team member or department.
  • Supports National Accounts Specialists with follow-up activities, documentation, reporting, and special projects as assigned.
  • Maintains a high level of confidentiality, accuracy, and professionalism when handling member, provider, client, and business information.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; two years of college coursework may be considered in lieu of related work experience.
  • Entry-level experience (0-2 years) in a call center, customer service, healthcare, insurance, dental office, billing, claims, clerical, or administrative support environment preferred.
  • Ability to communicate clearly and professionally with customers, providers, clients, and internal stakeholders.
  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to review information accurately and follow established procedures.
  • Basic problem-solving and critical-thinking skills, including the ability to identify when an issue should be escalated.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks, prioritize work, and meet established timelines in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience using Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel, Salesforce, or similar customer relationship management and tracking systems.
  • Previous clerical or administrative experience in healthcare, insurance, account management, dental services, or customer service.
  • Familiarity with provider networks, dental terminology, service inquiries, or claims-related processes.

Must reside in the Kansas City Metro

Work-at-home requirements

  • Must have the ability to provide a non-cellular High Speed Internet Service such as Fiber, DSL, or cable Modems for a home office.

  • A minimum standard speed for optimal performance of 30x5 (30mpbs download x 5mpbs upload) is required.

  • Latency (ping) response time lower than 80 ms

  • Hotspots, satellite and wireless internet service is NOT allowed for this role.

  • A dedicated space lacking ongoing interruptions to protect member PHI / HIPAA information

How we value you

  • Competitive pay/salary ranges

  • Incentive plan

  • Health/Vision/Dental benefits effective day one

  • 401(k) retirement plan: company match – dollar for dollar up to 4% employee contribution (pretax or Roth options) plus a 6% annual company contribution

  • Robust employee well-being program

  • Paid Time Off

  • Personal Community Enrichment Time

  • Company-provided Basic Life and AD&D

  • Company-provided Short-Term & Long-Term Disability

  • Tuition Assistance Program

While this is a remote opportunity, at this time G.E.H.A does not hire employees from U.S. territories or the following states: Alaska, Hawaii, California, Washington, Oregon, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, New York, Connecticut, Vermont, Pennsylvania, Maine.

Please note that the salary information is a general guideline only. G.E.H.A considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, as well as, market and business considerations when extending an offer.

The target hiring range for this position is $54,614 - $69,090 USD. At G.E.H.A, the current maximum salary for this role is $76,986 USD. While initial compensation may vary based on experience and qualifications, there is a path to work toward this top rate through performance and continued growth within the organization.

G.E.H.A is an Equal Opportunity Employer, which means we will not discriminate against any individual based on sex, race, color, national origin, disability, religion, age, military status, genetic information, veteran status, pregnancy, marital status, gender identity, and sexual orientation, as well as all other characteristics and qualities protected by federal, state, or local law. G.E.H.A will not discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their compensation or the compensation of another employee or applicant. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

G.E.H.A is headquartered in Lee's Summit, Missouri, in the Kansas City area. We recognize the importance of balance and flexibility and offer hybrid and work-from-home options for many of our roles.

title: Quality/Risk Coordinator
description:
Quality/Risk Coordinator Career Opportunity


Highly regarded and valued for your Quality/Risk expertise
Are you seeking a career that not only utilizes your skills but also aligns with your personal values, providing a profound sense of belonging and the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in patients' lives? Look no further than Encompass Health, the nation's leader in in-patient rehabilitation care. As a Quality/Risk Coordinator, you will assist in the administration of the quality and risk functions, including but not limited to working with hospital administration, departments and the medical staff to monitor and evaluate the quality of delivery of patient care services within the hospital. Join a team that values collaboration, support, and inclusivity, and embark on a rewarding career close to home and close to your heart, complete with access to cutting-edge equipment and technology and a comprehensive benefits package from day one.


A Glimpse into Our World
At Encompass Health, you'll experience the difference the moment you become a part of our team. Being at Encompass Health means aligning with a rapidly growing national inpatient rehabilitation leader. We take pride in the growth opportunities we offer and how our team unites for the greater good of our patients. Our achievements include being named one of the "World’s Most Admired Companies" and receiving the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® Award, among other accolades, which is nothing short of amazing.


Starting Perks and Benefits
At Encompass Health, we are committed to creating a supportive, inclusive, and caring environment where you can thrive. From day one, you will have access to:

  • Affordable medical, dental, and vision plans for both full-time and part-time employees and their families.
  • Generous paid time off that accrues over time.
  • Opportunities for tuition reimbursement and continuing education.
  • Company-matching 401(k) and employee stock purchase plans.
  • Flexible spending and health savings accounts.
  • A vibrant community of individuals passionate about the work they do!

Become the Quality/Risk Coordinator you've always aspired to be

  • Partners with the Director to assess compliance regulatory and accreditation standards.
  • Assists in writing corrective action plans and assessments (i.e. TJC PPR).
  • Uses current statistical tools and techniques in an effort to identify improvement opportunities.
  • Assists in establishing and maintaining performance improvement activities.
  • Handles daily risk management activities and compliance processes.
  • Collaborates with other departments to coordinate care and promptly solve customer concerns.
  • Maintains appropriate documentation of performance improvement and Governing Body activities.
  • Uses a variety of applications to identify improvement opportunities and generate reports.
  • Maintains and facilitates the time review of the hospital contract services provider log.

Qualifications

  • Licensed or certified according to individual state requirement.
  • Bachelor’s degree in healthcare or related field preferred.
  • Quality and/or risk management experience, including performance improvement activities, regulatory compliance, conflict resolution and risk management activities.

title: Social- og sundhedsassistent eller social- og sundhedshjælper i nattevagt søges til Ældrecenter Fynsgade
description:
Vi søger 1 SSA eller SSH i nattevagt, med opstart hurtigst muligt.
Stillingen er i udgangspunktet på 28 timer/gns. om ugen, men vi er fleksible, hvis du har andre ønsker til dit ugentlige timetal. Såfremt du ønsker en ansættelse på et højere timetal, vil det kræve, at du kan gå i blandede vagter.
Du vil skulle indgå i et rul med fast weekendvagt om natten hver 2. weekend.


Ældrecenter Fynsgade:
Fynsgade er centralt beliggende i Hjørring med 42 boliger fordelt på 3 etager med kun somatiske pladser, hvor vi har fokus på at fungere som et samlet hus.

Nattevagt i Fynsgade:
Som SSA eller SSH i nattevagt vil du altid være sammen med en fast makker. Vi er 2 nattevagter til at dække vores hus.


Hvorfor skal du vælge Fynsgade:
Vi er et hus har stort fokus på stabilitet. Vi har eksempelvis vores eget faste team af stabile afløsere, hvilket er med til at skabe en tryg og forudsigelig hverdag for både vores ansatte og beboere. Da vi kun har kendte folk i huset, sparer vi tid og ressourcer på at oplære eksterne vikarer. Den sparede tid bruger vi på at være i mødet med vores beboere, hvor vi arbejder professionelt med vores kerneopgave:
”At sikre, beboerne får mulighed for at leve et trygt og værdigt liv”.

Vi har valgt at prioritere sådan, da tryghed og forudsigelighed betyder meget for os.


Vi er optaget af, at du ønsker at blive en del af vores team og vores gode arbejdsfællesskab samt at du gør dig umage hver dag, du møder ind i vores hus. Vi ønsker også en kollega, som både kan sige til og fra og som kender sig selv godt. Vi har mange kompetencer i vores hus og er overbeviste om, at vi kan lære dig meget, så længe du har tilliden til, at vi arbejder som et team. Vi er ligeledes overbeviste om, at du kan lære os meget og vi vil gerne lytte og lære af dig.
Derfor er en god indstilling og ønske om at være en del af vores arbejdsfællesskab afgørende for os.

Når vi har et godt arbejdsfællesskab, oplever vi, at det giver de bedste forudsætninger for at lykkes med vores kerneopgave i mødet med vores beboere.

I Fynsgade ønsker vi:

  • At du er udannet social- og sundhedsassistent eller social- og sundhedshjælper
  • at du er mødestabil og fleksibel
  • At du hviler i dig selv, er nysgerrig og kender dit eget kompetenceområde
  • At du er fortrolig med IT og elektroniske omsorgsjournaler

Lyder ovenstående som noget for dig, ser vi frem til at høre fra dig.


Praktiske oplysninger

Løn- og ansættelsesvilkår fastsættes i henhold til gældende overenskomst.

Hvis du er interesseret i at vide mere om jobbet, er du velkommen til at kontakte afdelingsleder Eva Boel Graversen på tlf.: 41 22 53 31


Jobsamtaler afholdes løbende


Send ansøgning online

Du sender din ansøgning, CV og relevante bilag via vores rekrutteringssystem. Du bliver guidet igennem processen ved at trykke på knappen "Søg stillingen".


Vi ser frem til at modtage din ansøgning.
