title: Senior Data Engineer, Amazon Security Experience
description:
The Amazon Security Experiences (ASE) organization is the data intelligence backbone of Amazon Security. We build and operate the data platform that powers security insights, builder experience analytics, and tooling decisions across Amazon's security ecosystem. Every insight surfaced to security leadership, from builder productivity trends to security issue quality metrics, flows through systems our team designs, builds, and maintains.

We operate at scale, processing large volumes of security and operational data daily through hundreds of pipelines consisting of transformations, reporting queries, ingestions, and infrastructure management scripts. Our engineers work directly with source systems across AWS and SDO (Security, Developer, and Operations) data domains to procure data, convert it into structured formats, build large-scale processing pipelines, design analytical data models, and maintain infrastructure with the highest security and compliance standards.

We are seeking a Senior Data Engineer to join our Security Data Intelligence (SDI) team. This individual will own multiple data domains end-to-end, operate hundreds of pipelines, and drive architectural improvements that impact how security leadership makes decisions. You will partner with teams across ASE, BizOps, MapSec, and other security organizations to design data contracts, build ingestion flows, and deliver analytical models that serve the broader Amazon Security organization

Key job responsibilities
Identify limitations and opportunities in data processing tools, drive improvements and innovation, define data processing guidelines, and ensure best practices in all pipelines designed and reviewed. For example: redesigning ingestion frameworks to handle new security telemetry data, or building reusable transformation patterns adopted across multiple teams.

Define and own data architecture at the team and organization level, ensuring architecture effectively matches business problems and data challenges with security, scalability, and cost effectiveness. Show good judgment making technical trade-offs between short-term technology needs and long-term business needs.

Produce exemplary code, solutions that are easily usable by customers, inventive, secure, easily maintainable, appropriately scalable, and extensible. Build solutions that are easy for others to contribute to. Work to simplify, optimize, and remove bottlenecks.

Define and own infrastructure architecture at the team level. title: Office Engineer
description:
Job Description

Saylor Consulting Group is seeking a full-time Lead Office Engineer to support our client, the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC). The role provides office engineering and construction management services for the Moccasin Dam and Reservoir Long-Term Improvements Project, as part of an anticipated multi-year construction management contract. Work must be done in person. Under the contract, all services are performed onsite, full-time, at the project site in Moccasin, California (Tuolumne County), and remote work is allowed only at the SFPUC Regional Construction Manager's discretion.

The Lead Office Engineer will support construction management of a major water infrastructure project within the SFPUC's Hetchy Capital Improvement Program. The project will increase spillway capacity at Moccasin Dam, an earth and rockfill dam built in 1930. Planned work includes:

  • access improvements and utility relocation
  • heavy excavation and blasting
  • retaining walls
  • a new concrete spillway with underdrain systems
  • a single-span concrete bridge over the spillway
  • downstream creek channel improvements
  • a temporary bypass of the Grizzly Gulch Canal

The project uses the Construction Manager/General Contractor (CM/GC) delivery method. Pre-construction runs through 2028, and construction is expected from late 2028 through 2032.

Working under the SFPUC Regional Construction Manager and the Resident Engineer, the Lead Office Engineer will manage the flow of contract documentation between the contractor, the SFPUC construction management team, design engineers, operations staff, and environmental compliance staff. The role is central to keeping submittals, RFIs, contract documents, and record drawings accurate and processed on time over the life of the project. All work follows the HCIP Construction Management Plan and SFPUC CM procedures.

Daily Duties

  • Lead the submittal management process: log submittals, review them for completeness and conformance with the contract documents, route them to the designated reviewers, and return them to the contractor within contractual timeframes.
  • Manage contractor Requests for Information (RFIs): verify proper format, coordinate review with the Project Engineer and design team, and track responses to timely resolution.
  • Coordinate review of contractor Requests for Substitution (RFS) with the Project Engineer and Client/Operations Representative, and prepare responses with thorough supporting documentation.
  • Maintain the controlled set of contract drawings and specifications, and annotate all approved changes to the contract documents as they occur.
  • Audit the contractor's as-built "red-line" record drawings every month and track deficiencies to correction.
  • Use the Construction Management Information System (CMIS) to carry out document control and records management for all documentation received or generated during construction.
  • Prepare agendas and meeting minutes for weekly construction progress meetings and the Pre-Construction Conference, and maintain action item logs and follow-up on open items.
  • Support the Field Contract Administrator with change management by keeping change documentation current and supporting the change order log, from change order initiation through certification.
  • Help verify contractor monthly applications for payment and assemble supporting documentation for SFPUC review.
  • Contribute to monthly and quarterly progress and status reports, including tracking of contractor performance against the approved baseline schedule.
  • Coordinate with SFPUC Operations staff and the Client/Operations Representative on system shutdowns, testing, and startup/commissioning documentation.
  • Coordinate with the Lead Environmental Inspector to make sure environmental submittals and compliance documentation are tracked and routed correctly.
  • Support CM/GC pre-construction activities, including document tracking for constructability reviews and trade package development.
  • Direct and review the work of the Assistant Office Engineer and coordinate with the Administrative Document Control Specialist on document and records management.
  • Support project closeout: track final as-built drawings, spare parts, warranties, and turnover documentation, help prepare the Project History and Lessons Learned Report, and transfer project files for archiving.
  • Uphold the Project CM Safety Plan, Project Labor Agreement requirements, and site security procedures in all office and field activities.

Minimum Qualifications

  • At least 5 years of experience in construction management of heavy civil construction projects for a public utility.
  • Experience as the Office Engineer on at least one completed, verifiable heavy civil infrastructure project of similar type and scope (e.g., dams, reservoirs, spillways, or other water infrastructure). The project must have had a construction value over $15 million and been completed within the past 10 years.
  • Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or Construction Management from an accredited institution.
  • Demonstrated experience administering construction contract submittals and RFIs.
  • Experience on projects using alternative delivery methods, especially Construction Manager/General Contractor (CM/GC).
  • Current OSHA 10-hour safety training certificate.
  • Familiarity with SFPUC or other public agency construction management procedures.
  • At least 2 years of experience using construction management software (e.g., CMIS, Procore, e-Builder, Unifier, or similar) within the last 5 years.
  • Experience tracking and auditing contractor as-built drawings on a routine monthly basis.
  • Registration as an Engineer-in-Training (EIT) in California, or certification as a Certified Associate Constructor (CAC) or Construction Manager-in-Training (CMIT).
  • Valid driver's license issued by any U.S. state.
  • Ability to obtain Cal/OSHA 10-hour safety training certification within 30 days of contract Notice to Proceed, if not already held.
  • Strong ability to read and interpret plans and specifications.
  • Organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage high document volumes and multiple deadlines at once.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, and comfortable working with owner representatives, contractors, design engineers, and operations staff.

Featured Benefits

401(k), Medical Insurance, Dental Insurance, 100% employer paid premiums

Additional Information

Saylor Consulting Group (SCG) is a great place to work where your opinion matters, where you can grow with a supportive staff and make a difference in our project outcomes. We are proud to be an advisor on some of the largest, most technically complex projects in the nation. Our business is thriving and we offer unlimited opportunities for growth and career advancement. Additionally, we offer a competitive rate, flexibility, and an environment that recognizes and rewards hard work, with unlimited opportunities for professional development and advancement. Salary is commensurate to education and experience and we offer a competitive full benefits package to full-time employees.

We seek like-minded professionals who have a passion for estimating, drive to achieve results, creative problem-solving ability, and a dedication to client service and relationship management. We want our people to succeed both in work and life. To support this we promote a healthy, productive and flexible working environment that respects work-life balance. Come join us and partner with our world-class team and do your best work.

Please apply by emailing a brief cover letter and CV to nsaylor@saylorconsulting.com. We look forward to hearing from you! Saylor Consulting Group is an equal opportunity employer and makes hiring decisions solely on the basis of merit.

title: TONOPAH PEST CONTROL
description:
Company Overview

Here at Hickman’s Family Farms every day is a fresh start. Hickman’s Family Farms is proud to be the freshest egg provider in the Southwest since 1944, but it’s the eggs-traordinary people behind the farm fresh eggs that really make Hickman’s special. We want you and your egg-cellent set of skills to join our community of employees, neighbors and friends in one of the various positions available.

Job Summary:

The Pest Control Technician is responsible for ensuring that all pest control activities across our facilities are carried out effectively and efficiently. This includes managing rodent, fly, insect, bird, and weed control, as well as performing fumigation procedures, while adhering to strict safety and biosecurity protocols. The role involves regular monitoring, inspections, treatment application, and documentation to maintain a pest-free environment and ensure compliance with company standards.

Duties/Responsibilities:

Rodent Control:

  • Monitor, inspect, and service rodent traps and bait stations in accordance with the site’s Integrated Pest Management (IPM) plan.
  • Log findings and monitor bait levels at the end of each workday.
  • Identify areas needing corrective action and coordinate follow-up to implement corrective measures.

Fly Control/Prevention:

  • Apply sprays to the front and back of Lay Houses twice a week.
  • Monitor and spray break areas, office areas, and the Breaker Plant daily depending on fly activity levels.
  • Spray manure pits in high-rise houses every 6 weeks after manure removal.
  • Apply NEPOREX to sawdust to break the fly life cycle.
  • Monitor and service fly bait stations weekly.
  • Inspect Bug Lights in barns bi-weekly.
  • Use scatter bait and perform monthly fly indexing, implementing corrective actions when necessary.

Insect Control/Prevention:

  • Spray the exterior of processing plants, dry storage, and liquid egg facilities monthly.
  • Apply insecticides inside dry storage every 3 months.
  • Treat Lay Houses for spiders with two applications: immediately after hens are removed and after cleaning procedures are completed, to eliminate and prevent spider infestations.

Weed Control:

  • Maintain a weed-free environment around the facility to prevent pest harboring.
  • Choose and apply the appropriate weed control methods, such as herbicides, weed whackers, or tractor-mounted attachments.

Bird Control:

  • Immediately report any bird sightings inside facilities to the Pest Control Department.
  • Set up nets or use other methods to safely remove birds from facilities.
  • Remove nests and install deterrents to prevent future bird intrusion.

Fumigation:

  • Follow all safety protocols during fumigation procedures, ensuring that buildings are properly sealed, and safety signage is in place.
  • Conduct fogging after cleaning procedures in Lay Houses, ensuring that all personnel are cleared of the area.
  • Use disinfectants and viruses during fumigation to ensure a clean environment.

Safety and Biosecurity Compliance:

  • Comply with all company safety policies and biosecurity protocols.
  • Report any safety concerns or biosecurity issues immediately to the manager or appropriate personnel.

Required Skills/Abilities:

  • Previous pest control, agricultural, or related experience preferred.
  • Strong attention to detail for monitoring pest activity and implementing corrective actions.
  • Basic knowledge of pest biology and behavior, particularly rodents, flies, insects, and birds.
  • Good communication skills, both verbal and written, for documentation and reporting.
  • Ability to work independently and efficiently.

Education/Experience:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Pest control certification or related experience is a plus.
  • Familiarity with monitoring and servicing pest control systems, including rodent traps, bait stations, and bug lights, is preferred.
  • Knowledge of safe handling and application of pesticides, herbicides, and fumigation procedures is an advantage.
  • Experience with mechanical equipment, such as weed control tools (e.g., tractors or weed whackers), is a plus.

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds regularly and perform physically demanding tasks.
  • Ability to work in various environmental conditions (outdoors and inside facilities).
  • Stand, walk, bend, kneel, crouch, and climb for extended periods.
  • Work in confined spaces and varying environmental conditions, including heat, humidity, and dust.
  • Visual and manual ability to inspect and operate pest control equipment.
  • Tolerate exposure to odors, chemicals, and fumigation substances with protective gear.
  • Move across uneven terrain and climb stairs or ladders safely.

Benefits and Perks:

  • Matching 401(k) plan
  • Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
  • Paid Time Off (PTO), Paid Sick Leave, and Paid Holidays
  • Birthday Day Off
  • Access to Wellness and Fitness programs

Now you don't have to scramble for opportunities. Crack open the possibilities & Apply today!

Hickman's Family Farms and its brands are an Equal Opportunity Employer of all qualified individuals, including minorities, women, veterans and individuals with disabilities. Hickman's Family Farms will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with all federal, state, and local ordinances. You are applying for a position with Hickman’s Family Farms that is designated as a Safety Sensitive Position pursuant to A.R.S. §23-493 et seq. You are ineligible for placement in a Safety Sensitive Position if you are engaged in the current use of any drug, whether legal, prescribed by a physician or otherwise, if it could cause an impairment or otherwise decrease or lessen your job performance or ability to perform your job duties.

title: Director of Finance — Printing & Manufacturing
description:
Director of Finance — Printing & Manufacturing

Location: Scottsdale, Arizona
Reports to: Chief Financial Officer / President
Direct Reports: Accounting Manager
Employment Type: Full-Time, Exempt


Position Summary

Lead the financial future of the world’s largest temporary tattoo company.
At Tattoo Manufacturing International (TMI), we turn creativity into products that reach millions of people around the world. From our Tucson-based manufacturing facility, we design and produce temporary tattoos, coasters, activity kits, and specialty printed products for major brands, retailers, event organizers, and custom customers across more than 80 countries.

We’re seeking a strategic, hands-on Director of Finance to partner with senior leadership in driving profitability, operational efficiency, and sustainable growth. This is more than a traditional finance leadership role—it’s an opportunity to shape financial strategy for a high-volume manufacturer with global reach, complex inventory and production operations, and an expanding portfolio of consumer and commercial brands. As Director of Finance, you will provide clear financial insight, strengthen reporting and forecasting, guide budgeting and cost management, and help translate business performance into smart decisions. You’ll work closely with operations, sales, supply chain, and executive leadership to ensure TMI continues to grow with financial discipline and confidence.


If you’re a finance leader who enjoys manufacturing, fast-paced decision-making, international business, and making a measurable impact, we want to meet you.

Required Experience

The ideal candidate will have 12–15 years of progressive finance/accounting experience, including 5–8 years in a senior finance or Director-level leadership role. This experience should include direct exposure to manufacturing or printing operations, raw materials, inventory and cost accounting, FP&A, forecasting, payroll, and financial leadership.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Leadership & Strategy

· Serve as a trusted financial business partner to executive leadership, operations, sales, procurement, HR, and plant management.

· Develop and execute financial strategies that support revenue growth, margin expansion, cost control, capital investment, and long-term profitability.

· Provide timely and accurate P&L, balance sheet, cash-flow, KPI, and variance reporting to senior leadership.

· Lead monthly, quarterly, and annual business reviews; identify financial risks, opportunities, and corrective actions.

· Support pricing strategy, customer profitability, product/SKU profitability, quote review, and make-versus-buy decisions.

Accounting & Financial Reporting

· Oversee the monthly, quarterly, and annual close process and ensure timely, accurate financial statements in accordance with GAAP.

· Manage general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, fixed assets, inventory accounting, accruals, reconciliations, and intercompany accounting.

· Maintain strong internal controls, audit readiness, and compliance with applicable tax, regulatory, and reporting requirements.

· Serve as a key liaison with external auditors, tax advisors, banks, insurance providers, and other financial partners.

· Improve accounting policies, procedures, documentation, and financial systems.

FP&A, Budgeting & Forecasting

· Lead the annual operating budget, capital budget, rolling forecast, and long-range financial planning processes.

· Build driver-based financial models incorporating sales volume, pricing, raw-material costs, labor, overhead, production efficiency, and capacity utilization.

· Prepare monthly forecasts, budget-versus-actual analysis, margin bridges, cash-flow forecasts, and executive-level performance narratives.

· Analyze revenue, gross margin, operating expenses, plant performance, working capital, and cash-flow trends.

· Evaluate capital expenditures, equipment purchases, automation projects, facility investments, and cost-reduction initiatives using ROI, payback, NPV, and IRR analysis.

Manufacturing, Raw Materials & Cost Accounting

· Partner with operations, procurement, production, supply chain, and plant leadership to understand and manage manufacturing cost drivers.

· Oversee standard costing, product costing, work-in-process accounting, scrap/waste analysis, yield analysis, and manufacturing variance reporting.

· Analyze raw-material costs, purchase-price variance, inventory turns, obsolescence, supplier cost changes, and material-usage efficiency.

· Ensure accuracy of raw-material, WIP, and finished-goods inventory valuation, cycle counts, and inventory reporting.

· Support initiatives to reduce waste, improve press/run efficiency, optimize material usage, control overtime, and improve plant profitability.

· Assess the financial impact of production scheduling, changeovers, machine utilization, labor allocation, freight, outsourcing, and capacity constraints.

Payroll, Labor & HR Partnership

· Oversee payroll operations, payroll accounting, payroll compliance, timekeeping integration, and payroll reconciliations.

· Ensure accurate and timely processing of payroll, payroll taxes, deductions, garnishments, and related filings.

· Partner with Human Resources on compensation planning, benefits administration, workforce planning, and labor-cost management.

· Analyze labor productivity, headcount planning, shift costs, overtime trends, and the financial impact of staffing decisions.

· Maintain strong controls around payroll approvals, employee data, and payroll-related changes.

Cash Management & Working Capital

· Manage cash flow, cash forecasting, banking relationships, credit facilities, and liquidity planning.

· Monitor accounts receivable aging, collections, customer credit risk, payment terms, and bad-debt exposure.

· Oversee accounts payable strategy, vendor terms, payment timing, and working-capital optimization.

· Analyze inventory investment, raw-material purchasing patterns, and supply-chain financing opportunities to improve cash conversion.

Team Leadership & Continuous Improvement

· Lead, coach, and develop the finance and accounting team, creating a culture of accuracy, accountability, and continuous improvement.

· Establish performance expectations, improve close-cycle speed, and strengthen the quality of financial reporting.

· Identify opportunities to automate reporting, streamline workflows, and improve ERP, payroll, and business-intelligence systems.

· Champion cross-functional continuous improvement across finance, operations, procurement, and plant reporting.

title: Systems and Cloud Engineer
description:
Anglicare Southern Queensland are seeking a Cloud and Systems Engineer to join our Technology and Digital team based in Fortitude Valley.

Reporting to the Technology Operations Manager, you will play a key role in keeping critical platforms patched, backed up, monitored and recoverable while supporting security operations, vulnerability management and remediation activities, supporting the retirement of legacy systems and Anglicare’s transition to a cloud-first environment. You will also provide specialist service, guidance and advice to support the organisation’s core business operations.

How you will help make a difference

  • Administer Windows server environments, Active Directory / Entra ID, file and print services, and end-user computing platforms.
  • Perform operational database administration including backups, recovery, performance monitoring, patching and access control.
  • Execute backup, restore and recovery processes and participate in disaster recovery testing.
  • Apply patches, vulnerability remediations, and identity and access controls to agreed standards.
  • Support security operations through vulnerability identification, assessment, remediation and ongoing management across server, cloud and end-user computing environments.
  • Administer VMware vSphere and Citrix environments during the data centre transition period.
  • Automate repetitive administration tasks through scripting, including PowerShell.
  • Maintain accurate system documentation, CMDB records and operational runbooks.
  • Monitor system performance and capacity, identify improvement opportunities and support continual improvement initiatives.
  • Support cloud migration activities including discovery, dependency mapping, migration support and post-migration validation.
  • Plan and execute the decommissioning of legacy servers, systems and on-premises infrastructure as part of the cloud-first transition.
  • Contribute to knowledge sharing, cross-skilling and a positive, inclusive team culture.

What you will bring to the role

  • Current National Police Check OR Current NDIS Worker Screening Clearance.
  • Relevant IT qualification (degree, diploma or certification) or equivalent demonstrated experience.
  • Demonstrated systems administration experience in a Windows/Microsoft environment.
  • Demonstrated scripting and automation capability and cloud administration skills, or a commitment to develop these capabilities.
  • Demonstrated understanding of security operations, vulnerability management, patch management and security remediation within enterprise infrastructure environments.
  • Effective communication and negotiation skills.
  • Ability to support operational resilience through documentation, knowledge sharing and continuous improvement.
  • ITIL 4 Foundation certification (desirable).
  • Microsoft certifications such as Azure Administrator Associate, M365 or Windows Server (desirable).
  • SQL Server administration experience (desirable).
  • VMware and/or Citrix administration experience (desirable).
  • Experience with Rapid7 Managed Detection and Response (MDR), Rapid7 Vulnerability Management, or equivalent security monitoring and vulnerability management platforms (desirable).

title: Winter Lift Operator 26/27 Season
description:
Join the Team: Lift Operator

Bogus Basin Mountain Recreation Area, Boise National Forest, ID | Seasonal, Winter Operating Season

The Lift Operator is responsible for the daily set up, closing, and safe operation of your assigned chairlift or conveyor during the winter operational season. This role ensures an orderly, efficient and safe guest experience, and provides quality customer service while maintaining safety standards.

Why Bogus Basin?


Where Mountain Life Meets City Living:

Work at a four-season mountain recreation area while living in Boise—one of the fastest-growing, most livable cities in the U.S. With a thriving downtown, welcoming neighborhoods, and an energetic arts and dining scene, Boise pairs urban life with quick access to the outdoors, just 16 miles from the slopes.


Mission-Driven, Community-Focused:

As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, Bogus Basin is dedicated to providing accessible, affordable outdoor recreation, education, and community programming year-round. Every dollar earned is reinvested into the mountain and its people, not shareholders. Our values of kindness, respect, professionalism, and fun create a workplace where everyone is welcome.

Unbeatable Access to the Outdoors:

Located in the Boise National Forest, Bogus Basin offers year-round activities: skiing, snowboarding, cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, and tubing in the winter; mountain biking, hiking, and chairlift rides in the summer. Employees enjoy the perks of mountain life while being part of a community-oriented team.


How You’ll Make a Difference

As a Lift Operator, you’ll be the frontline of guest safety and experience on the mountain. You’ll oversee loading and unloading of lifts, maintain lift ramps, provide guidance and assistance to guests, maintain safety standards, and ensure smooth and efficient lift line operations. Your presence ensures that each guest has a safe and enjoyable day on the slopes.


A Day in the Life

You’ll start your day setting up your assigned lift and conducting safety checks. Throughout the day, you’ll maintain the lift area, direct guests safely through the lift line, assist with guest questions, and report any safety concerns to supervisors. Each shift requires vigilance, clear communication, and active engagement to keep operations running smoothly.


Key Responsibilities

Lift Operations & Safety

  • Assume responsible charge of the lift.
  • Conduct all safety checks.
  • Maintain ramps and maze areas to standard.
  • Maintain orderly passenger traffic within lift area.
  • Immediately inform Lift Supervisor or Manager of any conditions or occurrences affecting safety.

Guest Experience

  • Advise and assist guests using the lift.
  • Confidently communicate with large groups of guests.
  • Present a professional and positive image of the company at all times.

Operational Support

  • Maintain a clean and orderly work environment.
  • Assist in mountain rescue efforts if necessary.
  • Perform other related tasks as assigned.

title: Windows System Engineer
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Windows System Engineer based in India.

This role is responsible for managing and supporting enterprise Windows Server infrastructure across critical IT environments. You will work across Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, Group Policy, patching, virtualization, security, and high-availability systems. The position combines hands-on infrastructure administration with advanced troubleshooting and PowerShell automation. You will help maintain secure, reliable, and highly available Windows workloads while supporting business continuity and disaster recovery. The role also involves infrastructure monitoring, performance optimization, incident management, and technical documentation. It offers an opportunity to work with large-scale enterprise environments and modern Microsoft and virtualization technologies.

Accountabilities:

The Windows System Engineer will oversee day-to-day administration, support, security, and optimization of enterprise Windows infrastructure while contributing to operational resilience and continuous improvement. Key responsibilities include:

  • Install, configure, administer, and support Windows Server 2016, 2019, 2022, and 2025 environments.
  • Manage Active Directory Domain Services, including OUs, users, groups, computer accounts, FSMO roles, and Sites & Services.
  • Administer and troubleshoot DNS zones, records, DHCP scopes, and related services.
  • Create, configure, and troubleshoot Group Policy Objects and enterprise policies.
  • Perform server builds, upgrades, migrations, hardening, and decommissioning activities.
  • Manage Windows patching using WSUS, SCCM/MECM, or equivalent platforms.
  • Troubleshoot operating system, application, authentication, networking, performance, and system-level issues.
  • Support Microsoft Failover Clustering, Windows Server roles, and high-availability environments.
  • Support Windows workloads running on VMware vSphere and/or Microsoft Hyper-V.
  • Analyze system performance and optimize infrastructure capacity and reliability.
  • Implement and maintain Windows security baselines, hardening standards, and endpoint security controls.
  • Troubleshoot authentication technologies and issues involving Kerberos, NTLM, LDAP, certificates, and domain connectivity.
  • Manage Windows services, scheduled tasks, event logs, registry settings, and system configurations.
  • Support backup, restore, replication, disaster recovery, and business continuity activities.
  • Develop PowerShell scripts and automation to streamline repetitive administration and operational tasks.
  • Monitor infrastructure using enterprise monitoring, logging, and performance-management platforms.
  • Participate in incident, problem, change, and service-request management processes.
  • Create and maintain technical documentation, SOPs, knowledge articles, and infrastructure reports.
  • Participate in 24x7 on-call or shift support when required.

    • Requirements

    The role requires strong enterprise Windows administration experience, advanced troubleshooting capabilities, and a practical understanding of infrastructure security, virtualization, and IT service management. Candidates should demonstrate:

    • Strong experience administering Windows Server environments, particularly versions 2016, 2019, 2022, and/or 2025.
    • Hands-on expertise with Active Directory, including AD DS, OUs, users, groups, FSMO, and Sites & Services.
    • Strong knowledge of DNS, DHCP, Group Policy, and Windows authentication.
    • Proficiency in PowerShell scripting, automation, and Windows administration.
    • Experience with enterprise patching platforms such as WSUS, SCCM/MECM, or equivalent tools.
    • Experience with VMware vSphere and/or Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization.
    • Knowledge of Windows security hardening, security baselines, and endpoint security.
    • Understanding of TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VLANs, basic routing, and firewall concepts.
    • Experience with Windows monitoring, event logs, performance counters, and infrastructure troubleshooting.
    • Understanding of backup, restore, replication, disaster recovery, and business continuity concepts.
    • Familiarity with ITSM processes covering incidents, problems, changes, and service requests.
    • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills with the ability to resolve complex infrastructure issues.
    • Ability to document technical solutions, procedures, and operational processes clearly.
    • Strong communication and collaboration skills for working across infrastructure and support teams.
    • Ability to work effectively in enterprise environments and participate in on-call or shift support when required.

      • Additional experience that would be valuable includes:

      • Microsoft Azure and Azure Virtual Machines.
      • Microsoft Entra ID and hybrid identity environments.
      • Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
      • SCCM/MECM administration.
      • Windows Failover Clustering.
      • IIS administration.
      • Certificate Services and PKI.
      • VMware vCenter and ESXi.
      • ServiceNow or other ITSM platforms.
      • Enterprise monitoring platforms such as SCOM, SolarWinds, Dynatrace, or equivalent tools.
      • Large-scale data center infrastructure environments.
      • Advanced PowerShell automation.

        • Benefits

        • Full-time position.
        • Fully remote role open to candidates anywhere in India.
        • Opportunity to work with enterprise-scale Windows Server infrastructure.
        • Exposure to Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, Group Policy, virtualization, security, and high-availability technologies.
        • Hands-on experience with VMware and/or Hyper-V environments.
        • Opportunity to work with PowerShell automation and infrastructure optimization.
        • Exposure to Microsoft Azure, Entra ID, Intune, Defender, and other modern infrastructure technologies.
        • Experience supporting backup, disaster recovery, business continuity, and large-scale data center environments.
        • Cross-functional exposure to enterprise monitoring, ITSM, incident management, and infrastructure operations.
        • Opportunity to contribute to infrastructure security, reliability, and continuous improvement initiatives.

title: Mandarin Chinese (Simplified) Language Transcription Expert
description:
Join our team as an Independent Contractor for Project Lupin.
Project Lupin aims to help improve AI-powered speech recognition models
In this project, participants contribute by checking and modifying the audio segmentation and transcription. The transcriptions generated will contribute to the development of improved AI-powered speech recognition models.

Project Benefits

-Flexible hours – Work on your own schedule
-Remote – Work from anywhere
-Fair pay globally – Always above minimum wage in your market
-Scalable earnings – The more you work, the more you earn

Task Summary

You will listen to real audio recordings and produce precise, verbatim transcripts — capturing not just what was said, but how it was said. That means every “uh,” every repeated word, and every trailing sentence matters. Your work will include:

• Verbatim transcription with a target of 98%+ accuracy
• Timestamping segments with less than 500ms deviation
• Speaker labeling for conversations with 2 to 8 participants
• Event annotation for non-speech elements (e.g., laughter, background noise, unintelligible audio)

Requirements

  • Native-level fluency in Mandarin Chinese (Simplified), including familiarity with regional accents and informal speech
  • Strong listening comprehension and attention to detail.
  • Ability to produce verbatim transcriptions, including stutters, repetitions, and filler words.
  • Experience in transcription, annotation, or linguistics is an advantage.
  • Comfortable using browser-based tools (training will be provided).
  • Reliable internet connection.
  • Access to a laptop or desktop computer (mobile devices are not supported).
  • Reliable availability for minimum 10+ hours per week.

Please Note

This project follows a first-come, first-served approach and operates with demographic quotas to ensure fair and balanced representation across all participant groups. As a result, some individuals may not receive a task assignment if their group has already been filled.

You will need to log in to this account and reset the password, complete the setup requirements, and proceed with your application for this project-based role.
Join us in shaping the future of voice AI. Your participation in Project Lupin will directly help improve how technology understands and responds to real human speech.

title: Mechanical Engineering Intern | Summer 2027
description:
DLR Group is an integrated design firm with a promise to elevate the human experience through design. This fuels the work we do around the world and inspires our mission to improve the lives of our clients, our communities, and our planet. If this sparks your interest, you’re in the right place.

DLR Group’s Overland Park, KS studio has an opening for a Mechanical Engineering Summer Intern.

We have multiple positions and locations available; please refer to all openings posted and apply to the locations that are most suitable for your living situation during the course of your internship. This is not a remote position.

About EPX at DLR Group

As an intern at DLR Group, you’ll be part of our Emerging Professional Experience (EPX) Program, designed to give you a meaningful introduction to life within an integrated design firm and a strong foundation for your career in the AEC industry.

Each person at DLR Group has a design voice, and EPX gives you opportunities to develop and share yours. Through hands-on project work, mentorship, and learning experiences, you’ll gain exposure to the people, disciplines, and ideas that shape the built environment. You may participate in design discussions, project meetings, site visits, business development efforts, office activities, and other experiences that broaden your understanding of the design profession.

The program combines three core components: mentorship, project work, and weekly learning sessions. Topics may include design culture, sustainability, design technology, communication, marketing and business development, project and resource management, research, equity, career development, and more. Along the way, you’ll hear from leaders and integrated designers across DLR Group and build connections with fellow emerging professionals.

Position Summary

As a Mechanical Engineering Intern at DLR Group, you will be an important part of our integrated design team, contributing to the design of mechanical systems for buildings of various types, sizes, and complexities. Working alongside mechanical engineers and professionals across architecture, engineering, interiors, and other disciplines, you will gain hands-on experience with the design process from early concepts and system development through documentation and construction administration.

Our Summer Internship Program is a paid, full-time opportunity running May 18 through August 6, 2027, and interns are expected to participate for the duration of the program. This is an opportunity to apply what you’ve learned in the classroom, build your technical and professional skills, and contribute your perspective to design solutions that support our brand promise of Elevating the Human Experience through design.

What you will do

  • Work with a licensed engineer designing mechanical systems for new construction and/or building renovation projects
  • Attend design team meetings with a mechanical engineer and observe the coordination that occurs among the team members of a multi-disciplinary design team

title: Project Manager I
description:

This position coordinates project activities across engineering, operations, supply chain, quality, finance, contracts, and other functional organizations to ensure customer commitments are achieved within established scope, schedule, budget, and quality requirements.

The Project Manager I develops and maintains project plans, monitors project performance, communicates status and issues to internal and external stakeholders, and supports the resolution of project risks and variances. Projects assigned to this position generally involve limited to moderate commitment of Company resources and are performed under the direction of the Program Management leadership team.

Thurston County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office is seeking a professional, motivated, and dependable candidate for the position of Victim Advocate to join our team. A successful candidate will perform specialized counseling and referral functions in support of victims and/or witnesses; and work as part of a team to provide information, support, and referral to victims about justice system procedures.

Essential functions may include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • From locations including the Thurston County Family Justice Center and the Thurston County Courthouse, the Victim Advocate consults with and provides suggestions and information to assigned deputy prosecuting attorneys regarding the status of witnesses and expectations for court testimony. Makes recommendations to the court as requested by the court.
  • Serves as the advocate assigned to a specific team, working with other members of the team to provide services to victims and/or witnesses. Maintains detailed notes and files. Works as a team with other advocates to prepare reports and statistics as they are needed and may prepare annual reports.
  • Provides victim counseling and makes appropriate referrals. Interviews and assesses needs of victims and/or witnesses; determines needed community resources such as counseling and support groups and refers victims and/or witnesses; educates victims and/or witnesses about justice system procedures and court proceedings, and may educate victims and/or witnesses of relevant laws. Escorts victims to court and explains procedures and forms.
  • Reviews completed cases by examining case records and reports; provides feedback and suggestions to other team members regarding case methodologies and procedures as they relate to victim services.
  • Establishes and maintains working relationships with the community, human and social service agencies to which victims may be referred, and with other agencies in the criminal justice system.

title: Computational Protein Engineer
location: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, United States
description:
**Worker Type**

Regular

**Job Description**

**Position Overview**

The Biological Materials and Processing Research Team is seeking a Computational Protein Engineer to lead the design and optimization of proteins for use in novel metal separation technologies that address the nation’s growing need for critical materials. This role will focus on de novo protein design and optimizing protein performance and will involve using generative protein design software, machine learning methodologies for analysis of large experimental datasets, and other computational workflows. The successful candidate will play a foundational role in a growing research program and will have the opportunity for significant project ownership. They will join a group of collaborative scientists with diverse skill sets and should have strong communication skills, a collaborative mindset, and an enthusiasm for innovative research.

**Key Responsibilities**

- **Machine Learning for Data Analysis:** Implement and fine-tune machine learning algorithms to analyze large protein function datasets and generate sequences with predicted improvements in performance.

- **Computational Design & Generative AI:** Deploy advanced protein design suites (e.g., RFDiffusion, Rosetta, LigandMPNN) to architect novel binding pockets for polyvalent metals.

- **Structural Bioinformatics:** Develop and implement high-throughput workflows for in-silico assessment of the quality of engineered protein scaffolds.

- **Interdisciplinary Interface:** Translate computational predictions into actionable design parameters and assess resulting experimental data in collaboration with experimental team members as a part of design-test-learn workflows.

**Required Qualifications**

- **Education:** Ph.D. in Computational Chemistry, Biophysics, Protein Engineering, or a related field. (Candidates with an M.S. and 5+ years of specialized experience will be considered).

- **Technical Expertise:** Extensive experience with the use of regression, optimization, protein language, or transformer models to analyze large datasets. Experience using generative and physics-based models for de-novo protein design and in-silico screening. Strong understanding of protein structure-function relationships.

- **Programming**: Fluency in Python and/or C++/Rust for pipeline development and custom script generation. Experience automating computational workflows and implementing them on high-performance computers to reduce design turnaround time.

- **Citizenship:** U.S.Citizenship is required due to government facility access requirements.

**Preferred Skills**

- **Technical Project Coordination:** Experience coordinating work done by third parties (e.g. CROs, academic collaborators, and other external partners).

- **Metalloproteins**: Familiarity with the structure and function of metalloproteins.

- **QM Modeling:** Experience with quantum mechanical modeling of protein-metal interactions

- **Laboratory Familiarity:** Experience with (or willingness to learn) theory behind experimental techniques for characterizing protein function.

title: Senior Product Manager
description:
About SirenOpt

SirenOpt helps manufacturers make better, safer, and more reliable micro- and nano-materials. These materials are the building blocks of critical sectors of the global economy such as batteries, computer chips, aircraft components, and power systems. But, surging material demand and growing complexity are pushing production to unprecedented scales and speeds, leaving manufacturers effectively flying blind. Small, undetected variations during production lead to wastage, lower performance, higher costs, and safety risks.

SirenOpt is changing this by developing a manufacturing intelligence platform that non-destructively probes materials during production, revealing critical internal information without damaging them. Using a novel combination of cold atmospheric plasma, physics-informed machine learning, and predictive analytics, SirenOpt generates unique, real-time material fingerprints that capture material signals not accessible through conventional measurement techniques. These insights give manufacturers unprecedented visibility into how materials behave as they are made.

We turn hidden data into actionable intelligence to help manufacturers reduce variability and thus increase yield and performance. The technology can be deployed as a standalone tool or integrated directly into factory production lines. SirenOpt is currently deploying early versions of its platform with some of the largest industrial manufacturers in the world across North America, Europe, and Asia.

About the job

Job Title: Senior Product Manager

Location: On-Site (San Leandro, CA)

Job Type: Full-Time

Role Overview

SirenOpt is looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the product experience through which our customers understand their materials. This is a customer-obsessed, hands-on product role. You will spend significant time in the field with process engineers, technicians, and quality managers, mapping their workflows in detail, understanding where our product creates value, and translating that understanding into a complete hardware and software experience that is intuitive, reliable, and genuinely delightful to use.

Our software is how customers get their answers. Making it simple, clear, and sticky is the core of this role. You will lead the design of user workflows and interfaces, prototype and test them directly with users, and define the product experience across our standalone and inline offerings. You will work closely with engineering, data science, and commercial teams, and partner directly with the Head of Product on roadmap and product direction.

What You'll Do

Customer & User Understanding

  • Spend substantial time in the field understanding how customers work: their processes, their pain points, and how our product fits into their day-to-day.

  • Map user workflows in detail across personas i.e. technician, process engineer, quality manager, and distinguish stated needs from latent ones.

  • Build and maintain a deep, structured understanding of user needs that informs every product decision.

Product Experience & Design

  • Own the end-to-end software product experience, designed first for non-expert users who need clear, actionable answers without deep metrology, machine learning or software training.

  • Use Figma or equivalent tools to personally prototype and test interface concepts and workflows with real users before involving engineering.

  • Systematically simplify: reduce the number of steps, parameters, and decisions a user faces, working with engineering to hide or automate complexity that should not be user-facing.

  • Define how measurement results and analytics are presented to each persona, communicating confidence and uncertainty in plain language.

Product Definition & Collaboration

  • Translate customer and user understanding into clear product definition and feed it into the requirements process owned by engineering through active collaboration.

  • Partner with data science and machine learning teams to shape how the analytics layer serves non-expert users, including reducing manual model training as a user-facing step.

  • Contribute customer and product insight to the roadmap and product direction led by the Head of Product.

  • Prioritize Jira tickets for product workstreams and facilitate planning with engineering, and commercial teams.

What We're Looking For

  • BS or MS in Human-Computer Interaction, Interaction Design, physical sciences or engineering

  • 5 to 10 years in software product management or UX/product design, with at least 3 years owning a software product experience end to end

  • Hands-on UX and UI design ability: a portfolio of interface work you personally produced and tested in Figma or equivalent tools

  • A track record of deep customer and user research - spending time in the field, mapping workflows, and translating observation into shipped product decisions

  • Demonstrated ability to take complex or technical products and make them simple and intuitive for non-expert users

  • Experience with ML or analytics platform products: presenting model outputs to non-expert users and managing features with non-deterministic behavior

  • Proficiency with Jira and Agile practices

Nice to have:

  • Experience designing software for industrial, scientific instrumentation, or non-destructive testing applications

  • Background in or exposure to battery manufacturing, aerospace coatings, or semiconductor materials

  • Experience with software deployed in industrial or manufacturing environments

  • Willingness to travel to customer sites in North America, the United Kingdom, Europe, and Asia

  • Prior experience at an early-stage deep-tech startup

Base Pay Range
$155,000—$190,000 USD

Benefits

  • Equity and Salary compensation depends on experience
  • Health, Dental, Vision plans provided
  • 401k matching provided
  • Time off: 20 days of PTO per year, plus approximately 15 paid US holidays per year

title: Manufacturing Engineering Systems/Program Lead
description:
**Worker Type**

Regular

**Job Description**

**Summary**

AV is seeking an experienced Manufacturing Systems Engineering/Program Lead to provide technical leadership for manufacturing engineering activities across multiple programs. This role will serve as the technical lead responsible for factory value-stream analysis, capacity modeling, Earned Value Management System (EVMS) and Control Account Manager (CAM) activities, and manufacturing capacity expansion initiatives.

The ideal candidate has a strong manufacturing engineering background supporting moderate- to high-volume operations, preferably in mechanical manufacturing, printed circuit board (PCB), or circuit card assembly (CCA) environments. Working across manufacturing, engineering, program management, operations, quality, supply chain, and leadership teams, this individual will evaluate factory performance, identify constraints, develop scalable manufacturing solutions, and support program execution.

The successful candidate will translate manufacturing data and program requirements into actionable plans that improve throughput, capacity, cost, quality, and schedule performance. This role requires strong technical ownership, analytical ability, communication skills, and the ability to work effectively in a dynamic, cross-functional environment.

**Position Responsibilities**

- Serve as the technical lead for manufacturing engineering systems, factory capacity, and related initiatives across multiple programs.
- Develop and maintain value-stream and capacity models to evaluate material and process flow, throughput, cycle time, bottlenecks, capacity requirements, and factory performance.
- Lead capacity expansion and factory planning efforts, including evaluation of equipment, tooling, facilities, staffing, process capability, production flow, and resource requirements.
- Support EVMS, Integrated Master Schedule (IMS), budgets, performance metrics, and cost/schedule integration in partnership with Program Management and CAMs.
- Serve as a CAM or provide CAM support, including control account planning, estimates, schedules, and performance assessments.
- Analyze manufacturing data and develop recommendations to improve throughput, capacity utilization, cost, quality, productivity, and schedule performance.
- Partner with cross-functional organizations to resolve manufacturing constraints, execution issues, and program risks.
- Develop manufacturing strategies and implementation plans for program ramp-up, production scaling, and long-term capacity expansion.
- Develop and maintain manufacturing metrics, dashboards, and performance indicators to support data-driven decision-making.
- Lead or support Lean, Six Sigma, Theory of Constraints, and other continuous improvement initiatives.
- Present manufacturing performance, capacity, risks, investment recommendations, and status updates to program and functional leadership.
- Perform other relevant duties as assigned.

**Basic Qualifications (Required Skills & Competencies)**

- Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
- At least 8 years of experience in manufacturing engineering, industrial engineering, or a related field, preferably in moderate- to high-volume manufacturing.
- Experience with mechanical manufacturing, PCB/CCA assembly, or complex electromechanical manufacturing.
- Experience with capacity analysis, modeling, planning, value-stream mapping, and factory performance analysis.
- Experience with EVMS, program planning, cost/schedule performance management, and CAM responsibilities, including control account planning and performance reporting.
- Experience developing manufacturing metrics, dashboards, production forecasts, and capacity expansion solutions.
- Strong proficiency with Microsoft Excel and other data analysis or modeling tools.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, technical leadership, and communication skills.
- Ability to collaborate effectively across manufacturing, engineering, program management, operations, and leadership organizations.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.
- Must be a U.S. Citizen.

**Other Qualifications & Desired Competencies**

- Ten or more years of relevant manufacturing or industrial engineering experience.
- Experience with factory-level capacity models, production forecasts, manufacturing execution systems (MES), enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, or other manufacturing data systems.
- Experience with EVMS implementation and compliance in a government, aerospace, defense, or high-reliability manufacturing environment.
- Experience with IMS development, resource loading, and schedule/cost integration.
- Experience leading manufacturing capacity expansion, factory transformation, or production scaling initiatives.
- Experience with automated manufacturing processes, production test, tooling, fixtures, and manufacturing equipment.
- Experience supporting aerospace, defense, spaceflight, or other high-reliability programs.
- Experience presenting capacity, performance, and investment recommendations to senior leadership.
- Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, factory flow, capacity planning, and production systems.
- Ability to assume technical responsibility for manufacturing systems and capacity initiatives across multiple programs.

**Physical Demands and Work Environment**

- This position operates in a professional office and manufacturing environment.
- Routinely interacts with manufacturing operations and may spend time on the factory floor evaluating production processes, equipment, material flow, and manufacturing constraints.
- Required to sit and stand for long periods; talk, hear, and use hands and fingers to operate a computer and telephone keyboard.

**Clearance Level**

No Clearance

$111,500 - $170,000
